defs.def_en: If you are acquainted with something, you know about it because you have learned it or experienced it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 任何与这对夫妇有私交的人都不准和新闻界谈话。
ext.ext_en: No-one personally acquainted with the couple was permitted to talk to the Press...

ext.ext_cn: 我们的确认识，但仅此而已。
ext.ext_en: It's true we were acquainted, but no more than that.

defs.def_en: If you are acquainted with someone, you have met them and you know them. You can also say that two people are acquainted.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 这些会议是一种相互结交的途径。
ext.ext_en: The meetings were a way to get acquainted with each other.

ext.ext_cn: 增进领导人之间相互了解的机会
ext.ext_en: ...an opportunity for the leaders to become better acquainted.

defs.def_en: If you get or become acquainted with someone that you do not know, you talk to each other or do something together so that you get to know each other. You can also say that two people get or become acquainted .

ext.ext_cn: 她对他的爱经受着极其严峻的考验。
ext.ext_en: Her love for him was being tested to its limits...

ext.ext_cn: 每天食用多少新鲜水果都可以。
ext.ext_en: There is no limit to how much fresh fruit you can eat in a day...

defs.def_en: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.

ext.ext_cn: 3个月的限期截至6月中旬。
ext.ext_en: The three month time limit will be up in mid-June...

ext.ext_cn: 经济部长宣布了对石油销售的限制。
ext.ext_en: The economic affairs minister announced limits on petrol sales.

defs.def_en: A limit of a particular kind is the largest or smallest amount of something such as time or money that is allowed because of a rule, law, or decision.

ext.ext_cn: 巴格达市区
ext.ext_en: ...the city limits of Baghdad.

defs.def_en: The limit of an area is its boundary or edge.

ext.ext_cn: 她不得不在相当紧张的预算范围内精打细算。
ext.ext_en: She has to work within the limits of a fairly tight budget...

ext.ext_cn: 他勾画了英国的势力范围。
ext.ext_en: He outlined the limits of British power.

defs.def_en: The limits of a situation are the facts involved in it which make only some actions or results possible.

ext.ext_cn: 他对该国外债的偿还作出了限制。
ext.ext_en: He limited payments on the country's foreign debt...

ext.ext_cn: 这一观点认为经济将会增长2.25%，这将把失业人数限定在250万左右。
ext.ext_en: The view was that the economy would grow by 2.25 per cent. This would limit unemployment to around 2.5 million.

defs.def_en: If you limit something, you prevent it from becoming greater than a particular amount or degree.

ext.ext_cn: 现在人们已经接受，男性一周饮酒量不应超过20个单位。
ext.ext_en: It is now accepted that men should limit themselves to 20 units of alcohol a week...

ext.ext_cn: 选民削减了市政会委员的薪酬，并且限定他们每人只配一个工作人员。
ext.ext_en: Voters cut councillors' pay and limited them to one staff member each.

defs.def_en: If you limit yourself to something, or if someone or something limits you, the number of things that you have or do is reduced.

ext.ext_cn: 抗议活动不只限于纽约。
ext.ext_en: The protests were not limited to New York...

ext.ext_cn: 这次抽奖只限英国公民参加。
ext.ext_en: Entry to this prize draw is limited to UK residents.

defs.def_en: If something is  limited to a particular place or group of people, it exists only in that place, or is had or done only by that group.

ext.ext_cn: 沉船方圆一英里内仍然禁止进入。
ext.ext_en: A one-mile area around the wreck is still off limits...

ext.ext_cn: 这些建筑禁止普通公民入内。
ext.ext_en: These establishments are off limits to ordinary citizens.

defs.def_en: If an area or a place is off limits, you are not allowed to go there.

ext.ext_cn: 到处都禁止吸烟。
ext.ext_en: Smoking was off limits everywhere.

defs.def_en: If you say that something is off limits, you mean that you are not allowed to do it.

defs.def_cn: （驾驶时）血液中酒精浓度超标的

ext.ext_cn: 如果警察对我作呼气测醉试验，发现我饮酒过量，我将会被禁驾很长时间。
ext.ext_en: If police breathalyse me and find I am over the limit I face a long ban...

ext.ext_cn: 他血液中的酒精浓度是允许极限的3倍。
ext.ext_en: He was found to be three times over the limit.

defs.def_en: If someone is over the limit, they have drunk more alcohol than they are legally allowed to when driving a vehicle.

defs.def_cn: 没有任何限制；一切都是可能的（或能达到的）

ext.ext_cn: 他们发现，就收入和事业成功来讲，多高都有可能的。
ext.ext_en: They have found that, in terms of both salary and career success, the sky is the limit.

defs.def_en: If you say the sky is the limit, you mean that there is nothing to prevent someone or something from being very successful.

defs.def_cn: 在一定范围内；有限度地

ext.ext_cn: 在这种情况下，我们会把能告诉你的都告诉你，当然这是有限度的，而且需要保密。
ext.ext_en: In the circumstances we'll tell you what we can, within limits, of course, and in confidence.

defs.def_en: If you add within limits to a statement, you mean that it is true or applies only when talking about reasonable or normal situations.

ext.ext_cn: 我对上帝存在与否还是困惑不解。
ext.ext_en: I was left with puzzlement as to the existence or non-existence of God...

ext.ext_cn: 代表们的掌声稀稀拉拉，几近于无。
ext.ext_en: The applause from the delegates was thin to the point of non-existence.

defs.def_en: Non-existence is the fact of not existing.

ext.ext_cn: 人们被迫学会了自力更生。
ext.ext_en: People learned self-reliance because they had to...

ext.ext_cn: 首相呼吁加强经济上的自给自足。
ext.ext_en: The Prime Minister called for more economic self-reliance.

defs.def_en: Self-reliance is the ability to do things and make decisions by yourself, without needing other people to help you.

ext.ext_cn: 内拉河和韦利诺河的汇合处是落差达160米的瀑布，景象十分壮观。
ext.ext_en: The 160-metre falls mark the dramatic confluence of the rivers Nera and Velino.

defs.def_en: The confluence of two rivers is the place where they join and become one larger river.

ext.ext_cn: 如同大多数极端天气状况一样，其剧烈程度是由于几种气象条件反常地汇集在一起造成的。
ext.ext_en: Like most cases of extreme weather, its severity was due to an unusual confluence of events.

ext.ext_cn: 非洲文化与葡萄牙文化在巴西的汇合
ext.ext_en: ...the confluence of African and Portuguese cultures in Brazil.

defs.def_en: If there is a confluence of two things, they join, combine, or come together.

ext.ext_cn: 当我们在外面的时候，他变得很爱发号施令，开始不停地让我干这干那。
ext.ext_en: When we're out he gets really bossy and starts ordering me around...

ext.ext_cn: 奶奶毫不客气地随意支使她。
ext.ext_en: Grandmother felt free to order her about just as she wished.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is ordering you around or is ordering you about, you mean they are telling you what to do as if they have authority over you, and you dislike this.

ext.ext_cn: 我们准备在学校里搞个旧物义卖。
ext.ext_en: We are having a jumble sale at our school.

defs.def_en: A jumble sale is a sale of cheap second-hand goods, usually held to raise money for charity.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 似顽童的;顽皮的;调皮的

ext.ext_cn: 吉莱斯皮以他精灵搞怪的幽默感而广为人知。
ext.ext_en: Gillespie is well known for his impish sense of humour.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as impish, you mean that they are rather disrespectful or naughty in a playful way.

ext.ext_cn: 几小时以后拆弹专家拆除了该爆炸装置的引信。
ext.ext_en: A few hours later bomb disposal experts defused the devices.

ext.ext_cn: 陆军拆弹小组
ext.ext_en: ...an Army bomb disposal squad.

defs.def_en: Bomb disposal is the job of dealing with bombs which have not exploded, by taking out the fuse or by blowing them up in a controlled explosion.

defs.def_cn: 使安心;使得到保证;打消…的疑虑

ext.ext_cn: 我试图使她安心，“不要担心。我们不会让它再次发生了。”
ext.ext_en: I tried to reassure her, 'Don't worry about it. We won't let it happen again.'...

ext.ext_cn: 她刚刚让我放心，说一切都好。
ext.ext_en: She just reassured me that everything was fine.

defs.def_en: If you reassure someone, you say or do things to make them stop worrying about something.

defs.def_cn: （加在多数短形容词后构成比较级，也可以加在某些不是以-ly结尾的副词后构成比较级）表示“更…”，“较…”
defs.def_en: You add -er to many short adjectives to form comparatives. For example, the comparative of 'nice' is 'nicer'; the comparative of 'happy' is 'happier'. You also add it to some adverbs that do not end in -ly. For example, the comparative of 'soon' is 'sooner'.

defs.def_cn: （加在动词后构成名词）表示“做…的人（或事、动物）”
defs.def_en: You add -er to verbs to form nouns which refer to a person, animal, or thing that does the action described by the verb; for example a 'reader' is someone who reads and a 'money-saver' is something that saves money.

defs.def_cn: （加在某些词之后构成名词）表示“与…有关之人”
defs.def_en: You add -er to words to form nouns which refer to a person who is associated or involved with the thing described by the word; for example a 'pensioner' is someone who is entitled to a pension.

defs.def_cn: （加在名词后构成名词或形容词）表示“具有…特征之物”
defs.def_en: You add -er to nouns to form nouns or adjectives which refer to things with a particular characteristic or feature; for example a 'three-wheeler' is a vehicle with three wheels.

defs.def_cn: （加在某些词之后构成名词）表示“做…工作的人”，“从事…职业的人”
defs.def_en: You add -er to words to form nouns which refer to a person with a particular job. For example, someone who works in a mine is a 'miner'.

defs.def_cn: （加在地名之后构成名词）表示“…地方的人”，“来自…的人”
defs.def_en: You add -er to the names of some places to form nouns which refer to a person who comes from that place. For example, someone who comes from London is a 'Londoner'.

defs.pos_cn: 可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词
defs.def_en: A bishop is a clergyman of high rank in the Roman Catholic, Anglican, and Orthodox churches.
In chess a bishop is a piece that can be moved diagonally across the board on squares that are the same colour.

ext.ext_cn: 肯开始对独子的死悲痛不已。
ext.ext_en: Ken began to lament the death of his only son...

ext.ext_cn: 他哀叹埃尔萨尔瓦多镇的居民居然不信任警方。
ext.ext_en: He laments that people in Villa El Salvador are suspicious of the police...

defs.def_en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

ext.ext_cn: 她谈到职业女性的悲哀：与男性相比，她们的判断力更易遭人质疑。
ext.ext_en: She spoke of the professional woman's lament that a woman's judgment is questioned more than a man's.

defs.def_en: Someone's lament is an expression of their sadness, regret, or disappointment about something.

ext.ext_cn: 乡村音乐电台中，一位歌手正演唱歌曲哀悼已故的伟大音乐人巴迪·霍利。
ext.ext_en: A singer on the country music station was singing a lament for the late, great Buddy Holly.

defs.def_en: A lament is a poem, song, or piece of music which expresses sorrow that someone has died.

ext.ext_cn: 他额头上冒出了滴滴汗珠。
ext.ext_en: Droplets of sweat were welling up on his forehead.

ext.ext_cn: 小水滴
ext.ext_en: ...water droplets.

defs.def_en: A droplet is a very small drop of liquid.

defs.def_cn: 没资格的；资格不够的；不合格的

ext.ext_cn: 她没资格做这份工作。
ext.ext_en: She was unqualified for the job...

ext.ext_cn: 医院里一些还未取得资格的员工没有受到充分的督导。
ext.ext_en: Unqualified members of staff at the hospital were not sufficiently supervised.

defs.def_en: If you are unqualified, you do not have any qualifications, or you do not have the right qualifications for a particular job.

defs.def_cn: 完全的；绝对的；无保留的；不受限制的

ext.ext_cn: 这一活动取得了极大成功。
ext.ext_en: The event was an unqualified success...

ext.ext_cn: 埃及几乎全力支持华盛顿。
ext.ext_en: Egypt has given almost unqualified backing to Washington.

defs.def_en: Unqualified means total or unlimited.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 竞争激烈的;残酷无情的

ext.ext_cn: 个人电脑市场上残酷无情的竞争
ext.ext_en: ...the cut-throat competition in personal computers.

ext.ext_cn: 竞争激烈的国际金融界
ext.ext_en: ...the cut-throat world of international finance.

defs.def_en: If you describe a situation as cut-throat, you mean that the people or companies involved all want success and do not care if they harm each other in getting it.

ext.ext_cn: 一瓶瓶不含酒精的啤酒
ext.ext_en: ...bottles of non-alcoholic beer.

defs.def_en: A non-alcoholic drink does not contain alcohol.

defs.def_cn: 室友;合租一套公寓（或一幢房子）的人
defs.def_en: Your roommate is the person you share a rented room, apartment, or house with, for example when you are at university.
Your roommate is the person you share a rented room with, for example when you are at university.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我的烛光将他拉长的影子投射在墙上。
ext.ext_en: The light from my candle threw his elongated shadow on the walls.

defs.def_en: If something is elongated, it is very long and thin, often in an unnatural way.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 蒜香色拉
ext.ext_en: ...a garlicky salad.

ext.ext_cn: 透着蒜味的呼吸
ext.ext_en: ...garlicky breath.

defs.def_en: Something that is garlicky tastes or smells of garlic.
The transitivity of a verb is whether or not it is used with a direct object.

ext.ext_cn: 为使公众熟悉新法律所赋予的权利而作出的努力
ext.ext_en: ...efforts to acquaint the public with their rights under the new law...

ext.ext_cn: 我想知道你有哪些长处以及不足。
ext.ext_en: I want to acquaint myself with your strengths and weaknesses.

defs.def_en: See also:acquainted;If you acquaint someone with something, you tell them about it so that they know it. If you acquaint yourself with something, you learn about it.

ext.ext_cn: 阿里斯蒂德通过口译员向媒体发表讲话。
ext.ext_en: Aristide spoke to the press through an interpreter.

defs.def_en: An interpreter is a person whose job is to translate what someone is saying into another language.

ext.ext_cn: 多年来弗雷尼一直是普契尼歌剧女主角的最佳表演者之一。
ext.ext_en: Over the years Freni has been one of the supreme interpreters of Puccini's heroines.

defs.def_en: The interpreter of something such as a piece of music is the person who performs it.

ext.ext_cn: 我希望他把我当作一个职业女性来尊重。
ext.ext_en: I want him to respect me as a career woman...

ext.ext_cn: 他需要从他敬重的人那里获得建议，而他一向都很敬重你。
ext.ext_en: He needs the advice of people he respects, and he respects you.

defs.def_en: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

ext.ext_cn: 我非常敬重迪安。
ext.ext_en: I have tremendous respect for Dean...

ext.ext_cn: 他的声音里充满了友善和敬意。
ext.ext_en: His voice was warm with friendship and respect.

defs.def_en: See also:self-respect;If you have respect for someone, you have a good opinion of them.

ext.ext_cn: 最后，为了尊重她的意愿，我说我会离开。
ext.ext_en: Finally, trying to respect her wishes, I said I'd leave.

defs.def_en: If you respect someone's wishes, rights, or customs, you avoid doing things that they would dislike or regard as wrong.

ext.ext_cn: 他们会争取讨回世代相传的土地，并要求尊重土著居民的权利和风俗。
ext.ext_en: They will campaign for the return of traditional lands and respect for aboriginal rights and customs.

defs.def_en: If you show respect for someone's wishes, rights, or customs, you avoid doing anything they would dislike or regard as wrong.

defs.def_cn: 遵守，遵从（法律或道德规范）

ext.ext_cn: 旅行社是时候该遵守法律和行业规范了。
ext.ext_en: It is about time tour operators respected the law and their own code of conduct.

ext.ext_cn: 遵守法律，反对使用暴力
ext.ext_en: ...respect for the law and the rejection of the use of violence.

defs.def_en: If you respect a law or moral principle, you agree not to break it.

defs.def_cn: 恕我直言，恕我冒昧(用于礼貌地表示不同意见或批评)

ext.ext_cn: 部长，恕我冒昧，您还没有回答我的问题。
ext.ext_en: With respect, Minister, you still haven't answered my question...

ext.ext_cn: 恕我直言，但我认为这不是重点。
ext.ext_en: With respect, I hardly think that's the point.

defs.def_en: You can say with respect when you are politely disagreeing with someone or criticizing them.

ext.ext_cn: 卡尔已经让他去医院看望弗朗西斯。
ext.ext_en: Carl had asked him to visit the hospital and to pay his respects to Francis.

defs.def_en: If you pay your respects to someone, you go to see them or speak to them. You usually do this to be polite, and not necessarily because you want to do it.

defs.def_cn: 和(死者)告别;参加…的葬礼

ext.ext_cn: 这个儿子没有参与葬礼的安排，但是来向遗体告别了。
ext.ext_en: The son had nothing to do with arranging the funeral, but came along to pay his last respects.

defs.def_en: If you pay your last respects to someone who has just died, you show your respect or affection for them by coming to see their body or their grave.

defs.def_cn: 在这个方面/在许多方面

ext.ext_cn: 这些孩子并非愚钝——事实上，在这个方面他们似乎很正常。
ext.ext_en: The children are not unintelligent—in fact, they seem quite normal in this respect...

ext.ext_cn: 在很多方面，亚洲女性都认为自己和丈夫是平等的。
ext.ext_en: In many respects Asian women see themselves as equal to their men.

defs.def_en: You use expressions like in this respect and in many respects to indicate that what you are saying applies to the feature you have just mentioned or to many features of something.

defs.def_cn: 关于，至于（英国英语中也用in respect of）

ext.ext_cn: 关于孩子的治疗方法，父母通常没有什么选择的余地。
ext.ext_en: Parents often have little choice with respect to the way their child is medically treated...

ext.ext_cn: 沙普兰博士认为系统在专业培训上的运作效率不是非常高。
ext.ext_en: Where Dr Shapland feels the system is not working most effectively is in respect of professional training.

defs.def_en: See also:respected;You use with respect to to say what something relates to. In British English, you can also say in respect of .

defs.def_cn: (指代先前提及的人或物)这，这个

ext.ext_cn: 食物出炉后都应该静置一会。在此期间，中心部分还在继续加热。
ext.ext_en: When food comes out of any oven, it should stand a while. During this delay the centre carries on cooking...

ext.ext_cn: 10 月 1 号，美国暂停了拟议中的一项 1991 年度总计 5.74 亿美元的一揽子援助方案，这其中有 2.5 亿美元是用于军事采购的。
ext.ext_en: On 1 October the US suspended a proposed $574 million aid package for 1991. Of this amount, $250 million is for military purchases.

defs.def_en: You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.

defs.def_cn: (引出将要谈论的人或物)下面(这个)，以下

ext.ext_cn: 下面是我要做的：我要给安娜打电话解释清楚。
ext.ext_en: This is what I will do. I will telephone Anna and explain.

ext.ext_cn: 以下是来自我们科学部的戴维·库克的报道：“为什么恐龙灭绝了？”
ext.ext_en: This report is from David Cook of our Science Unit: 'Why did the dinosaurs become extinct?'

defs.def_en: You use this to introduce someone or something that you are going to talk about.

defs.def_cn: 这一点(指前一句或几句话中提到的观点或情况)

ext.ext_cn: 你觉得要求大家分组工作不划算，这是为什么呢？
ext.ext_en: You feel that it's uneconomic to insist that people work together in groups. Why is this?...

ext.ext_cn: 工作时间多数是朝九晚五，你觉得这样会让你感觉愉快吗？
ext.ext_en: A job is pretty much nine-to-five. Is this what you feel would make you happy?

defs.def_en: You use this to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.

defs.def_cn: (叙述时引出新出现的人或物)这个，一个

ext.ext_cn: 我碰巧来到这儿，正看着热闹，突然一个女孩袭击了我。
ext.ext_en: I came here by chance and was just watching what was going on, when this girl attacked me...

ext.ext_cn: 于是我就拾级而上，走进了这座漂亮的大教堂。
ext.ext_en: So I just walked up the steps into this big, beautiful church.

defs.def_en: In spoken English, people use this to introduce a person or thing into a story.

defs.def_cn: 这个，这位(尤指所触碰或指向的离自己较近的人或物，有两个以上时，用于指最近的一个)

ext.ext_cn: “您要是喜欢别的，我很乐意帮您调换一下。”——“不用了，这个挺好。”
ext.ext_en: 'If you'd prefer something else I'll gladly have it changed for you.' — 'No, this is great.'...

ext.ext_cn: “你刚才找的是不是这个？”布拉德利掏出那块手绢。
ext.ext_en: 'Is this what you were looking for?' Bradley produced the handkerchief...

defs.def_en: You use this to refer to a person or thing that is near you, especially when you touch them or point to them. When there are two or more people or things near you, this refers to the nearest one.

defs.def_cn: 这个，这(指代正在发生或刚刚发生的与自己有关的一般情况、活动或事件)

ext.ext_cn: 我想，这就是我为何不远千里赶来的原因。
ext.ext_en: I thought, this is why I've travelled thousands of miles...

ext.ext_cn: 蒂姆，这可糟了。我知道你心里在想什么，但实际情况不是这样的。
ext.ext_en: Tim, this is awful. I know what you must think, but it's not so...

defs.def_en: You use this when you refer to a general situation, activity, or event which is happening or has just happened and which you feel involved in.

defs.def_cn: 这，该，此(指当前所处地点或时间)

ext.ext_cn: 我们已停止用火车向该国运送武器。
ext.ext_en: We've stopped transporting weapons to this country by train...

ext.ext_cn: 这个地方的经营方式就是旅馆应该有的样子。
ext.ext_en: This place is run like a hotel ought to be run...

defs.def_en: You use this when you refer to the place you are in now or to the present time.

defs.def_cn: 本，今，这个，下一个(指接下来将要发生某事的特定时间)

ext.ext_cn: 本周日 7 点 45 分的表演
ext.ext_en: ...this Sunday's 7.45 performance...

ext.ext_cn: 我们准备今年 6 月结婚。
ext.ext_en: We're getting married this June...

defs.def_en: You use this to refer to the next occurrence in the future of a particular day, month, season, or festival.

defs.def_cn: 这么，这样(用于用手比划大小、形状时)

ext.ext_cn: 他们说伤口只有这么一点大，他还用手指比划给我看。
ext.ext_en: They'd said the wound was only about this big you see and he showed me with his fingers.

defs.def_en: You use this when you are indicating the size or shape of something with your hands.

defs.def_cn: 这么，这样(用于说明自己知道或能告知的内容)

ext.ext_cn: 我不想透露我的七年计划的具体内容，不过有一点可以告诉你，如果顺利实施，今后的七年将非常有意义。
ext.ext_en: I am not going to reveal what my seven-year plan is, but I will tell you this much, if it works out, the next seven years will be very interesting.

defs.def_en: You use this when you are going to specify how much you know or how much you can tell someone.

ext.ext_cn: “你知道，人们会选择性地忘记自己说过的话。”——“嗯，是这样。”
ext.ext_en: 'You know, people conveniently forget the things they say.' — 'Well this is it.'

defs.def_en: If you say this is it, you are agreeing with what someone else has just said.

defs.def_cn: (用于电话、广播或电视中，表明身份或所代表的机构)我是，这里是

ext.ext_cn: 喂，我是约翰·汤普森。
ext.ext_en: Hello, this is John Thompson...

ext.ext_cn: “喂，是雷蒙德·布朗吗？”——“对，您是哪位？”
ext.ext_en: 'Hello, is this Raymond Brown?' — 'Yeah, who's this?'...

defs.def_en: You use this in order to say who you are or what organization you are representing, when you are speaking on the telephone, radio, or television.

defs.def_cn: 这个(指说话、写作时的媒介)

ext.ext_cn: 我在今天的讲座中将主要探讨一些非常具体的问题。
ext.ext_en: What I'm going to do in this lecture is focus on something very specific...

ext.ext_cn: 一本书能做到的，也是本书努力实现的，就是列举一些例子说明如何让生活变得更加愉快。
ext.ext_en: What a book can do, and what this one will try to accomplish, is to present examples of how life can be made more enjoyable...

defs.def_en: You use this to refer to the medium of communication that you are using at the time of speaking or writing.

defs.def_cn: 各种各样的东西;这样那样

ext.ext_cn: “那你现在在做什么呢？”——“哦，瞎忙。”
ext.ext_en: 'And what are you doing now?' — 'Oh this and that.'

ext.ext_cn: 我想就水费及其他各种各样费用的上涨谈谈看法。
ext.ext_en: I want to make a point about all these charges going up, water rates and all this that and the other.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are doing or talking about this and that, or this, that, and the other you mean that you are doing or talking about a variety of things that you do not want to specify.

defs.def_cn: 像样的;尚好的;过得去的

ext.ext_cn: 附近的村子里有一家还不错的酒馆。
ext.ext_en: Nearby is a village with a decent pub...

ext.ext_cn: 他没有得到一个像样的解释。
ext.ext_en: He didn't get a decent explanation...

defs.def_en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

defs.def_cn: 合宜的;得体的;适当的;正当的

ext.ext_cn: 但是适当地间断一段时间后，贸易关系开始恢复正常。
ext.ext_en: But, after a decent interval, trade relations began to return to normal...

ext.ext_cn: 棺材慢慢放入墓穴时她一直注视着他的脸。礼仪许可的时间一到，他便挤过人群走向那些车子。
ext.ext_en: She watched his face, as the coffin was lowered into the ground. As soon as it was decent, he plunged through the crowd towards the cars.

defs.def_en: Decent is used to describe something which is morally correct or acceptable.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 这里的大多数人都很正派。
ext.ext_en: The majority of people around here are decent people...

ext.ext_cn: 陪审团将会认识到他是一个多么正派的人。
ext.ext_en: The jury will see what a decent guy he is.

defs.def_en: Decent people are honest and behave in a way that most people approve of.

defs.def_cn: 做（不想做但）应该做的事

ext.ext_cn: 他应该识时务地辞职。
ext.ext_en: He should do the decent thing and resign.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone should do the decent thing, you mean that they should do something which they do not really want to do, but which you think they ought to do.

ext.ext_cn: 安东尼娅是个想象力丰富的女人。
ext.ext_en: Antonia is a woman with a vivid imagination...

ext.ext_cn: 阿利斯泰尔逻辑思维能力很强,但缺乏想象力。
ext.ext_en: Alistair had a logical mind, and little imagination...

defs.def_en: Your imagination is the ability that you have to form pictures or ideas in your mind of things that are new and exciting, or things that you have not experienced.

ext.ext_cn: 早在我真正踏足之前很久,非洲就已在我的脑海中活灵活现了。
ext.ext_en: Long before I ever went there, Africa was alive in my imagination.

defs.def_en: Your imagination is the part of your mind which allows you to form pictures or ideas of things that do not necessarily exist in real life.

defs.def_cn: 吸引…的注意力;摄人魂魄;引人入胜

ext.ext_cn: 上个赛季意大利足球吸引了全国上下的注意。
ext.ext_en: Italian football captured the imagination of the nation last season.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone or something captured your imagination, you mean that you thought they were interesting or exciting when you saw them or heard them for the first time.

ext.ext_cn: 他们的电影非常精彩且发人深省。
ext.ext_en: Their films are exciting and really stretch the imagination.

defs.def_en: If you say that something stretches your imagination, you mean that it is good because it makes you think about things that you had not thought about before.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 喧闹的；活泼的；精力充沛的

ext.ext_cn: 一群大声喧嚷但很和善的人
ext.ext_en: ...a boisterous but good-natured crowd...

ext.ext_cn: 大多数孩子都又吵又闹。
ext.ext_en: Most of the children were noisy and boisterous.

defs.def_en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他通常很善于使自己的私生活避开媒体的关注。
ext.ext_en: He's usually very adept at keeping his private life out of the media...

ext.ext_cn: 他是个吉他高手。
ext.ext_en: He is an adept guitar player.

defs.def_en: Someone who is adept at something can do it skilfully.

ext.ext_cn: 黄昏时分，更多的鱼游到了浅水区。
ext.ext_en: At dusk more fish come into the shallows.

defs.def_en: The shallows are the shallow part of an area of water.

ext.ext_cn: 快速开展工作的伯明翰警方已经开始发现间接证据。
ext.ext_en: Fast work by the police in Birmingham had started producing circumstantial evidence.

defs.def_en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence that makes it seem likely that something happened, but does not prove it.

defs.def_cn: 视情况而定的;与特定情况有关的

ext.ext_cn: 工程垮掉系环境所迫。
ext.ext_en: The reasons for the project collapsing were circumstantial.

defs.def_en: Something that is circumstantial is  related to a particular circumstance.

ext.ext_cn: 抗议者们试图冲破警察的封锁线。
ext.ext_en: Protesters tried to break through a police cordon...

ext.ext_cn: 大约15名犯人闯到了屋顶上。
ext.ext_en: About fifteen inmates broke through onto the roof.

defs.def_en: If you break through a barrier, you succeed in forcing your way through it.

ext.ext_cn: 仍有一些领域需要新作家们去开拓。
ext.ext_en: There is still scope for new writers to break through...

ext.ext_cn: 我摆脱了贫困，这要归功于教育。
ext.ext_en: I broke through the poverty barrier and it was education that did it.

defs.def_en: If you break through, you achieve success even though there are difficulties and obstacles.

ext.ext_cn: 不管怎样，伊丽莎白还是不断显露出其作为普通人的一面。
ext.ext_en: Despite everything, Elizabeth's human side keeps breaking through...

ext.ext_cn: 阳光冲破了云层。
ext.ext_en: Sunlight had broken through the clouds.

defs.def_en: When something that was previously hidden or could not be seen breaks through, it appears.
In grammar, direct speech is speech which is reported by using the exact words that the speaker used.
A shopkeeper is a person who owns or manages a small shop.

ext.ext_cn: 我们傍晚到家。
ext.ext_en: We arrived home at dusk.

defs.def_en: Dusk is the time just before night when the daylight has almost gone but when it is not completely dark.

ext.ext_cn: 她转身消失在暮色中。
ext.ext_en: She turned and disappeared into the dusk.

defs.def_en: The dusk is the dull, shadowy light there is at dusk.

ext.ext_cn: 为期5天的短假游报价从5,395英镑起。
ext.ext_en: Five-day mini-breaks start at £5,395.

defs.def_en: A mini-break is a short holiday.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 这种训练没有效率，而且是对稀缺资源的浪费。
ext.ext_en: This kind of training is ineffective, and wasteful of scarce resources...

ext.ext_cn: 尽量避免无用的重复劳动。
ext.ext_en: Try to avoid wasteful duplication of effort.

defs.def_en: Action that is wasteful uses too much of something valuable such as time, money, or energy.
A probationer is someone who has been found guilty of committing a crime but is on probation rather than in prison.

ext.ext_cn: 见习警察
ext.ext_en: ...a probationer policeman.

defs.def_en: A probationer is someone who is still being trained to do a job and is on trial.
In ancient times, a charioteer was a chariot driver.
Spectra is a plural form of spectrum.

ext.ext_cn: 杰茜卡看到了洛伊丝，就冲她挥手致意。
ext.ext_en: Jessica caught sight of Lois and waved to her...

ext.ext_cn: 他冲服务员招了招手，服务员就急忙跑到桌边。
ext.ext_en: He waved at the waiter, who rushed to the table...

defs.def_en: If you wave or wave your hand, you move your hand from side to side in the air, usually in order to say hello or goodbye to someone.

defs.def_cn: 挥手示意(方向);挥手指引

ext.ext_cn: 廖什克恼火地挥手让他离开。
ext.ext_en: Leshka waved him away with a show of irritation...

ext.ext_cn: 他等着警察来让车辆停下，指挥人们前行。
ext.ext_en: He waited for a policeman to stop the traffic and wave the people on...

defs.def_en: If you wave someone away or wave them on, you make a movement with your hand to indicate that they should move in a particular direction.

ext.ext_cn: 医院的工作人员都在外面一边挥动旗子一边鼓掌欢迎他。
ext.ext_en: Hospital staff were outside to welcome him, waving flags and applauding...

ext.ext_cn: 她经常会提高嗓门，双手胡乱挥舞。
ext.ext_en: She was apt to raise her voice and wave her hands about.

defs.def_en: If you wave something, you hold it up and move it rapidly from side to side.

ext.ext_cn: 随风摇曳的花草
ext.ext_en: ...grass and flowers waving in the wind.

defs.def_en: If something waves, it moves gently from side to side or up and down.

ext.ext_cn: 海浪拍岸的声音
ext.ext_en: ...the sound of the waves breaking on the shore.

defs.def_en: A wave is a raised mass of water on the surface of water, especially the sea, which is caused by the wind or by tides making the surface of the water rise and fall.
If someone's hair has waves, it curves slightly instead of being straight.

ext.ext_cn: 地震带来的冲击波在德黑兰也能感觉到。
ext.ext_en: The shock waves of the earthquake were felt in Teheran...

ext.ext_cn: 爆炸冲击波震得尼尔喘不过气来，不过他还是得以幸存。
ext.ext_en: The blast wave crushed the breath from Neil, but he survived.

defs.def_en: A wave is a sudden increase in heat or energy that spreads out from an earthquake or explosion.

ext.ext_cn: 声波、光波或无线电波等都有特定的频率，或者说是每秒的波数。
ext.ext_en: Sound waves, light waves, and radio waves have a certain frequency, or number of waves per second.

defs.def_en: Waves are the form in which things such as sound, light, and radio signals travel.

ext.ext_cn: 她感到一阵恐慌，但还是强作镇定地离开了房间。
ext.ext_en: She felt a wave of panic, but forced herself to leave the room calmly...

ext.ext_cn: 爱尔兰举国上下都同情她。
ext.ext_en: A wave of sympathy for her swept Ireland...

defs.def_en: If you refer to a wave of a particular feeling, you mean that it increases quickly and becomes very intense, and then often decreases again.

ext.ext_cn: 目前的暴力浪潮
ext.ext_en: ...the current wave of violence.

ext.ext_cn: 更新一波的犯罪风潮
ext.ext_en: ...an even newer crime wave.

defs.def_en: A wave is a sudden increase in a particular activity or type of behaviour, especially an undesirable or unpleasant one.

ext.ext_cn: 移民潮正席卷西欧。
ext.ext_en: A wave of immigrants is washing over Western Europe.

defs.def_en: A wave is a sudden increase in the number of people moving somewhere.

If a crowd of people do the wave, each person in the crowd stands up and puts their arms in the air after the person to one side of them, then sits down again, creating a continuous wave-like motion through the crowd.
A crop top is a very short, usually tight, top worn by a girl or a woman.
The Old Testament is the first part of the Bible. It deals especially with the relationship between God and the Jewish people.

ext.ext_cn: 至于回程，我觉得我能多花点钱坐头等舱。
ext.ext_en: For my return journey, I felt I could afford the extra and travel first class...

ext.ext_cn: 我能觉察到有什么事很不对头。
ext.ext_en: I could see that something was terribly wrong...

defs.def_en: You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn't to say that someone was unable to do something.  →see usage note at:can

ext.ext_cn: 虽然他爱发脾气，而且有时还很讨厌，但向来都只是一阵儿。
ext.ext_en: Though he had a temper and could be nasty, it never lasted...

ext.ext_cn: 他想要友好的时候会非常友好。
ext.ext_en: He could be very pleasant when he wanted to.

defs.def_en: You use could to indicate that something sometimes happened.

defs.def_cn: 本能够，本可以(表示某事本有可能发生但却并未发生)

ext.ext_cn: 他本可以当律师挣大钱的。
ext.ext_en: He could have made a fortune as a lawyer...

ext.ext_cn: 你差点儿就没命了！
ext.ext_en: You could have been killed!...

defs.def_en: You use could have to indicate that something was a possibility in the past, although it did not actually happen.

defs.def_cn: (表示某事可能属实或可能发生)可能

ext.ext_cn: 医生们告诉他这种疾病可能是由于多年在烟雾缭绕的俱乐部工作所致。
ext.ext_en: Doctors told him the disease could have been caused by years of working in smokey clubs...

ext.ext_cn: 可能多年之后生活水平才能得到提高。
ext.ext_en: An improvement in living standards could be years away...

defs.def_en: You use could to indicate that something is possibly true, or that it may possibly happen.

ext.ext_cn: 他们一直在争论，认为这对孩子肯定不好。
ext.ext_en: They argued all the time and thought it couldn't be good for the baby...

ext.ext_cn: 别指望安妮能弄明白当前情势。
ext.ext_en: Anne couldn't be expected to understand the situation...

defs.def_en: You use could not or couldn't to indicate that it is not possible that something is true.

defs.def_cn: (表示可能性、能力或机会)可能

ext.ext_cn: 他们希望能够诞生一个崭新的、更加美好的东德。
ext.ext_en: Their hope was that a new and better East Germany could be born...

ext.ext_cn: 我知道如果我同迈拉讲一声，就能让她给我父亲打电话。
ext.ext_en: I knew that if I spoke to Myra, I could get her to call my father.

defs.def_en: You use could to talk about a possibility, ability, or opportunity that depends on other conditions.

ext.ext_cn: 她画的那些优雅迷人的人物就好像是从20世纪30年代走出来的一样。
ext.ext_en: The charming characters she draws look like they could have walked out of the 1920s.

defs.def_en: You use could when you are saying that one thing or situation resembles another.

ext.ext_cn: 我可以给当地医生打电话。
ext.ext_en: I could call the local doctor...

ext.ext_cn: 咱们需要钱，对不对？咱们可以去周围打听一下看有没有人要找人做零工什么的。
ext.ext_en: We need money right? We could go around and ask if people need odd jobs done or something...

defs.def_en: You use could, or couldn't in questions, when you are making offers and suggestions.

defs.def_cn: (用于礼貌地提出请求或征得许可。当说话者意识到可能被拒绝时，可以用 couldn't 代替 could)能，可以

ext.ext_cn: 我今晚可以留下吗？
ext.ext_en: Could I stay tonight?...

ext.ext_cn: 约翰，我可以单独跟你说一会儿话吗？
ext.ext_en: Could I speak to you in private a moment, John?...

defs.def_en: You use could in questions when you are making a polite request or asking for permission to do something. Speakers sometimes use couldn't instead of 'could' to show that they realize that their request may be refused.

defs.def_cn: (用以礼貌地打断某人或引出将要说的话)请允许我

ext.ext_cn: 嗯，请允许我插一句。
ext.ext_en: Well, if I could just interject...

ext.ext_cn: 我能打断您一下吗？
ext.ext_en: Could I stop you there?...

defs.def_en: People sometimes use structures with if I could or could I as polite ways of interrupting someone or of introducing what they are going to say next.

defs.def_cn: (用以强调某人应该做所提及的事情，尤用于当说话者因为其没做该事而生气时)

ext.ext_cn: 我们都来看你了，你至少应该起身得体地打个招呼。
ext.ext_en: We've come to see you, so you could at least stand and greet us properly...

ext.ext_cn: 蠢货！你本应该告诉我！
ext.ext_en: Idiot! You could have told me!...

defs.def_en: You use could to say emphatically that someone ought to do the thing mentioned, especially when you are annoyed because they have not done it. You use why couldn't in questions to express your surprise or annoyance that someone has not done something.

defs.def_cn: (表示想要做某事的强烈感情)

ext.ext_cn: 我想杀了你！我发誓我真想杀了你！
ext.ext_en: I could kill you! I swear I could!...

ext.ext_cn: 他们只是说，“欢迎回来。”我真想亲他们一下！
ext.ext_en: 'Welcome back' was all they said. I could have kissed them!...

defs.def_en: You use could when you are expressing strong feelings about something by saying that you feel as if you want to do the thing mentioned, although you do not do it.

defs.def_cn: (用在if后以谈论没有能力或机会做但为考虑可能的结果而设想去做的事)

ext.ext_cn: 假如能买得起，我就会有4台电视机。
ext.ext_en: If I could afford it I'd have four television sets...

ext.ext_cn: 要是能睡上一会儿，我就能应付了。
ext.ext_en: If only I could get some sleep, I would be able to cope.

defs.def_en: You use could after 'if' when talking about something that you do not have the ability or opportunity to do, but which you are imagining in order to consider what the likely consequences might be.

defs.def_cn: (与比较级连用，强调某物或某人具备某种特征的程度)太…，再…不过

ext.ext_cn: 剩下的选手是一帮很棒的小伙子，我太高兴了。
ext.ext_en: The rest of the players are a great bunch of lads and I couldn't be happier...

ext.ext_cn: 亲爱的内维尔，我真太为你高兴了。
ext.ext_en: Darling Neville, I couldn't be more pleased for you...

defs.def_en: You use could not or couldn't with comparatives to emphasize that someone or something has as much as is possible of a particular quality. For example, if you say 'I couldn't be happier', you mean that you are extremely happy.

defs.def_cn: 怎么会(用在疑问句中强调对所发生的不愉快之事的感受)

ext.ext_cn: 你怎么会允许他做那样的事？
ext.ext_en: How could you allow him to do something like that?...

ext.ext_cn: 我怎么会那么蠢？
ext.ext_en: How could I have been so stupid?...

defs.def_en: In speech, you use how could in questions to emphasize that you feel strongly about something bad that has happened.

defs.def_cn: 不用了(谢绝更多的食物或饮品)

ext.ext_cn: “再来点蛋糕？”——“哦不，不用了。”
ext.ext_en: 'More cake?' — 'Oh no, I couldn't.'

defs.def_en: You say 'I couldn't' to refuse an offer of more food or drink.

defs.def_en: If you refer to someone's wish list, you mean all the things which they would like to happen or be given, although these things may be unlikely.

ext.ext_en: My hobbies are letter writing, football, music, photography, and tennis.

defs.def_en: A hobby is an activity that you enjoy doing in your spare time.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 盐水比淡水的传导性强得多。
ext.ext_en: Salt water is much more conductive than fresh water is.

defs.def_en: A conductive substance is able to conduct things such as heat and electricity.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: He was very respectful at home and obedient to his parents...

ext.ext_cn: 她上六年级的时候是个多么可爱温顺的小女孩啊！
ext.ext_en: What a sweet, obedient little girl she was in the sixth grade.

defs.def_en: A person or animal who is obedient does what they are told to do.

ext.ext_cn: 这个故事的基调和内容打动了我。

ext.ext_en: She just totally blew me away with her singing.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are blown away by something, or if it blows you away, you mean that you are very impressed by it.

ext.ext_cn: 他恨不得拿把枪，把他们全干掉。
ext.ext_en: He'd  like to get hold of a gun and blow them all away.

defs.def_en: If someone blows another person away, they kill them by shooting them.

ext.ext_cn: 我们对那个地区进行了彻底的搜查。
ext.ext_en: We went over that area with a fine-tooth comb.

defs.def_en: If you say that you will go over something with a fine-tooth comb or go through something with a fine-tooth comb, you are emphasizing that you will search it thoroughly or examine it very carefully.

ext.ext_en: 'You don't give a damn about my feelings, do you.' —

ext.ext_cn: “你根本不在乎我的感受，是不是。”——“说老实话，是不在乎。”
ext.ext_en: 'Quite frankly, I don't.'...

defs.def_en: See also:frank;You use frankly when you are expressing an opinion or feeling to emphasize that you mean what you are saying, especially when the person you are speaking to may not like it.

defs.def_cn: 一些，有些(表示不确切的数量或数目)

ext.ext_cn: 罗宾开了一些香槟。
ext.ext_en: Robin opened some champagne...

ext.ext_cn: 将几勺橄榄油、一片切碎的蒜瓣和一些黑胡椒粉放入深平底锅里加热。
ext.ext_en: Heat a couple of tablespoons of olive oil, a chopped clove of garlic and some black pepper in a heavy saucepan...

defs.def_en: You use some to refer to a quantity of something or to a number of people or things, when you are not stating the quantity or number precisely.

defs.def_cn: (表示数量或数目相当大)好些，大量

ext.ext_cn: 地方政府的财政问题已经争论了好些年。
ext.ext_en: The question of local government finance has been the subject of debate for some years...

ext.ext_cn: 我已经较为详细地探讨了这个话题。
ext.ext_en: I have discussed this topic in some detail...

defs.def_en: You use some to emphasize that a quantity or number is fairly large. For example, if an activity takes some time, it takes quite a lot of time.

defs.def_cn: (表示数量或数目相当小)有几分，有点儿

ext.ext_cn: 吉尔问：“威廉还有一线希望过上正常的生活吗？”
ext.ext_en: 'Isn't there some chance that William might lead a normal life?' asked Jill...

ext.ext_en: All mothers share to some extent in the tension of a wedding...

defs.def_en: You use some to emphasize that a quantity or number is fairly small. For example, if something happens to some extent, it happens a little.

ext.ext_cn: 一些已经工作的人将要失业。
ext.ext_en: Some of the people already in work will lose their jobs...

ext.ext_cn: 打开盖子，用勺子盛些调味汁到碗里。
ext.ext_en: Remove the cover and spoon some of the sauce into a bowl...

defs.def_en: If you refer to some of the people or things in a group, you mean a few of them but not all of them. If you refer to some of a particular thing, you mean a part of it but not all of it.

ext.ext_en: If you are worried about some aspect of your child's health, call us...

ext.ext_cn: 吉姆·帕特里奇从某座桥上跳了下去。
ext.ext_en: Jim Partridge chucked himself off some bridge or other...

defs.def_en: If you refer to some person or thing, you are referring to that person or thing but in a vague way, without stating precisely which person or thing you mean.

ext.ext_cn: 我养鸟大约有 30 年了。
ext.ext_en: I have kept birds for some 30 years...

ext.ext_cn: 他在距离那座粉红色的大别墅约 80 到 100 码的地方等候着。
ext.ext_en: He waited some 80 to 100 yards from the big pink villa...

defs.def_en: You can use some in front of a number to indicate that it is approximate.

ext.ext_cn: 如果苏珊不在，我就随便看看打发时间好了。
ext.ext_en: If Susanne is off somewhere, I'll kill time by looking around some...

ext.ext_cn: 杰德说：“我有时会去参加聚会。”
ext.ext_en: 'I party some,' said Jed...

defs.def_en: Some is used to mean to a small extent or degree.

defs.def_cn: (表示赞同或不赞同)也叫，也算；了不起的，好极的

ext.ext_en: She lived to be ninety-nine years old and only weighed eighty pounds but she'd raised eight kids. That was some tough woman!...

ext.ext_en: 'Some party!'—'Yep. One hell of a party.'

defs.def_en: You can use some in front of a noun in order to express your approval or disapproval of the person or thing you are mentioning.

ext.ext_cn: 生还者身上有冻伤。
ext.ext_en: The survivors suffered from frostbite.

defs.def_en: Frostbite is a condition in which parts of your body, such as your fingers or toes, become seriously damaged as a result of being very cold.

ext.ext_en: I have always believed that a garden dies with its creator.

defs.def_en: The creator of something is the person who made it  or invented it.

ext.ext_cn: 这是上帝安放在天堂里的第一件东西。
ext.ext_en: This was the first object placed in the heavens by the Creator.

defs.def_en: God is sometimes referred to as the Creator .

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 不再着迷的;不再抱有幻想的;感到幻灭的

ext.ext_en: I'm disenchanted with the state of British theatre at the moment.

defs.def_en: If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.

defs.def_en: A day trip is a journey to a place and back again on the same day, usually for pleasure.

ext.ext_cn: 我收到了一封简写来的信。她向你问好。
ext.ext_en: I had a letter from Jane. She asks after you.

defs.def_en: If someone asks after you, they ask someone how you are.

defs.def_cn: 爱发牢骚的人;牢骚满腹的人

ext.ext_en: He was a terrible complainer — always moaning about something.

defs.def_en: A complainer is someone who complains a lot about their problems or about things they do not like.

ext.ext_cn: 她紧紧抓住绳索。
ext.ext_en: She gripped the rope.

defs.def_en: If you grip something, you take hold of it with your hand and continue to hold it firmly.

defs.def_en: A grip is a firm, strong hold on something.

ext.ext_en: The president maintains an iron grip on his country...

ext.ext_en: Tony Blair last night tightened his grip on Labour mps with new powers to root out troublemakers.

defs.def_en: Someone's grip on something is the power and control they have over it.

ext.ext_en: The entire community has been gripped by fear.

defs.def_en: If something grips you, it affects you very strongly.

ext.ext_en: The nation is gripped by the dramatic story.

defs.def_en: If you are gripped by something such as a story or a series of events, your attention is concentrated on it and held by it.

defs.def_en: If things such as shoes or car tyres have grip, they do not slip.

defs.def_en: If you get to grips with a problem or if you come to grips with it, you consider it seriously, and start taking action to deal with it.

defs.def_cn: （使自己）镇定下来；控制住（自己）

ext.ext_cn: 英国依然没有摆脱经济衰退。

defs.def_en: If a person, group, or place is in the grip of something, they are being severely affected by it.

defs.def_en: If you lose your grip, you become less efficient and less confident, and less able to deal with things.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone has a grip on reality, you mean they recognize the true situation and do not have mistaken ideas about it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

defs.def_en: Something that is disagreeable is rather unpleasant.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 只要她不表露她的激情和情感，她就可以选择自己的婚姻伴侣。
ext.ext_en: She could choose her own partner in matrimony, as long as she gave no utterance to her passions and emotions.

defs.def_en: Utterance is the expression in words of ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

ext.ext_cn: 白镴盘子
ext.ext_en: ...pewter plates.

ext.ext_cn: 最好的18世纪白镴
ext.ext_en: ...the best 18th century pewter.

defs.def_en: Pewter is a grey metal which is made by mixing tin and lead. Pewter was often used in former times to make ornaments or containers for eating and drinking.
A trampoline is a piece of equipment on which you jump up and down as a sport. It consists of a large piece of strong cloth held by springs in a frame.

ext.ext_cn: 他心不在焉地看着镜中的自己。
ext.ext_en: He absent-mindedly looked at himself in the mirror...

ext.ext_cn: 他看了一下后视镜，发现一辆深色货车紧随其后。
ext.ext_en: He checked his mirror and saw that a dark coloured van was immediately behind him.

defs.def_en: A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.

ext.ext_cn: 这本书不可避免地反映出我个人的喜好与经历。
ext.ext_en: The book inevitably mirrors my own interests and experiences...

ext.ext_cn: 他和她面面相觑。
ext.ext_en: His own shock was mirrored on her face.

defs.def_en: If something mirrors something else, it has similar features to it, and therefore seems like a copy or representation of it.

ext.ext_cn: 刚刚被洪水淹没的田野映照出了天空，那里突然泛起亮光
ext.ext_en: ...the sudden glitter where a newly-flooded field mirrors the sky...

ext.ext_cn: 船会停靠在那里，映衬在一片波澜不兴的湛蓝海水之中。
ext.ext_en: The ship would lie there mirrored in a perfectly unmoving glossy sea.

defs.def_en: If you see something reflected in water, you can say that the water mirrors it.

ext.ext_cn: 我觉得他越修越糟。
ext.ext_en: I thought he had bodged the repair.

defs.def_en: If you bodge something, you make it or mend it in a way that is not as good as it should be.

defs.def_cn: （与指人的名词连用，构成复合名词）表示“主要的”，“最重要的”

ext.ext_cn: 他和他的死对头朱塞佩·德里察双双落败。
ext.ext_en: Neither he nor his arch-rival, Giuseppe De Rita, won.

ext.ext_cn: 他的死敌
ext.ext_en: ...his arch-enemy.

defs.def_en: Arch- combines with nouns referring to people to form new nouns that refer to people who are extreme examples of something. For example, your arch-rival is the rival you most want to beat.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (对自身社会地位、才智、品位等)过分自傲的，势利的

ext.ext_cn: 他们非常势利，不喜欢智力和社会地位不如自己的人。
ext.ext_en: They had a snobbish dislike for their intellectual and social inferiors...

ext.ext_cn: 我原以为她会非常势利，但她却非常热情和友好。
ext.ext_en: I'd expected her to be snobbish but she was warm and friendly.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as snobbish, you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 医生们说话简短生硬，十分忙碌。
ext.ext_en: The doctors are brusque and busy ...

ext.ext_cn: 他们从他那里得到的是一个粗鲁无礼的答复，他一贯都是那样的。
ext.ext_en: They received a characteristically brusque reply from him.

defs.def_en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with things, or say things, quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

ext.ext_cn: 他是伊娃最深恶痛绝的那种人中的典型。
ext.ext_en: He was the quintessence of all that Eva most deeply loathed.

defs.def_en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

ext.ext_cn: 一座堪称英格兰乡村风格之典范的石砌农舍
ext.ext_en: ...an old stone cottage, the quintessence of rural England.

defs.def_en: The quintessence of something is the aspect of it which seems to represent its central nature.

ext.ext_cn: 工作中的问题俯拾皆是。
ext.ext_en: There were problems aplenty at work.

defs.def_en: If you have something aplenty, you have a lot of it.

defs.def_cn: (使)(牛奶或鸡蛋)凝结；（使）结成凝乳

ext.ext_cn: 调味汁不能煮沸，不然蛋黄会凝结的。
ext.ext_en: The sauce should not boil or the egg yolk will curdle...

ext.ext_cn: 那种香草几个世纪以来都被用来制作酸乳。
ext.ext_en: The herb has been used for centuries to curdle milk.

defs.def_en: If milk or eggs curdle or if you curdle them, they separate into different bits.
Perfectionism is the attitude or behaviour of a perfectionist.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: （尤指对被自己击败或欺凌过自己的人）宽宏大量的，宽厚的，慷慨大度的

ext.ext_cn: 我准备表现得宽宏大量，同情他的境遇。
ext.ext_en: I was prepared to be magnanimous, prepared to feel compassion for him...

ext.ext_cn: 他是一个很有雅量的人。
ext.ext_en: He was a man capable of magnanimous gestures.

defs.def_en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously towards someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

ext.ext_cn: 新款汽车会有若干重大改进。
ext.ext_en: The new cars will incorporate a number of major improvements.

defs.def_en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

ext.ext_cn: 协议将允许把叛军收编入一支新的国家警备部队。
ext.ext_en: The agreement would allow the rebels to be incorporated into a new national police force...

ext.ext_cn: 该党宣誓要把环境因素纳入它所有的政策当中。
ext.ext_en: The party vowed to incorporate environmental considerations into all its policies.

defs.def_en: If someone or something is incorporated into a large group, system, or area, they become a part of it.

ext.ext_cn: 政府提高了面包、肉类等几种基本商品的价格。
ext.ext_en: The government increased prices on several basic commodities like bread and meat.

defs.def_en: A commodity is something that is sold for money.
An organist is someone who plays the organ.

defs.def_cn: 城垛；（城堡的）雉堞；有枪眼的防御墙
defs.def_en: The battlements of a castle or fortress consist of a wall built round the top, with gaps through which guns or arrows can be fired.

ext.ext_cn: 金的作品搬上银幕后似乎缺点什么。
ext.ext_en: King's works seem to lack something on celluloid.

defs.def_en: You can use celluloid to refer to films and the cinema.

ext.ext_cn: 那是这两个社会之间的根本性差异。
ext.ext_en: That is the fundamental difference between the two societies...

ext.ext_cn: 男女之间没有差别。
ext.ext_en: There is no difference between the sexes.

defs.def_en: The difference between two things is the way in which they are unlike each other.

ext.ext_en: The difference is 8532.

defs.def_en: A difference between two quantities is the amount by which one quantity is less than the other.

ext.ext_cn: 这两个社群正在学着如何解决彼此之间的分歧。
ext.ext_en: The two communities are learning how to resolve their differences.

defs.def_en: If people have their differences about something, they disagree about it.

ext.ext_cn: 住在哪里会极大地影响你的感受。
ext.ext_en: Where you live can make such a difference to the way you feel...

ext.ext_cn: 锻炼身体非常重要。
ext.ext_en: Exercise makes all the difference...

defs.def_en: If something makes a difference or makes a lot of difference, it affects you and helps you in what you are doing. If something makes no difference, it does not have any effect on what you are doing.

defs.def_cn: （在数量、价格上）折中，各让一步

ext.ext_cn: 我们折中一下，7,500 美元怎么样？
ext.ext_en: Shall we split the difference and say $7,500?

defs.def_en: If you split the difference with someone, you agree on an amount or price which is halfway between two suggested amounts or prices.

defs.def_cn: 非常有趣的;与众不同的

ext.ext_cn: 如果想去一个与众不同的海滨度假胜地，那就去基韦斯特吧。
ext.ext_en: For a beach resort with a difference, try Key West.

ext.ext_cn: 不同寻常的政治家
ext.ext_en: ...a politician with a difference.

defs.def_en: If you describe a job or holiday, for example, as a job with a difference or a holiday with a difference, you mean that the job or holiday is very interesting and unusual.

ext.ext_cn: 在如何利用那笔诺贝尔奖金的问题上有不同意见吗？
ext.ext_en: Was there a difference of opinion over what to do with the Nobel Prize money?

defs.def_en: If there is a difference of opinion between two or more people or groups, they disagree about something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 黛西说她傻乎乎的，但心肠很好。
ext.ext_en: Daisy called her daffy, but goodhearted.

ext.ext_cn: 怪趣的故事情节
ext.ext_en: ...a daffy storyline.

defs.def_en: If you describe a person or thing as daffy, you mean that they are strange or foolish, but in a rather attractive way.

ext.ext_cn: 安哥拉政府
ext.ext_en: ...the Angolan government.

defs.def_en: Angolan means belonging or relating to Angola or its people.

ext.ext_cn: 安哥拉人担心战火重燃。
ext.ext_en: Angolans are worrying about a return to war.

defs.def_en: An Angolan is someone who comes from Angola.

defs.def_cn: 无法辨别的；难以辨认的

ext.ext_cn: 囚犯的尸体上中枪太多，几乎无法辨认。
ext.ext_en: The corpses of the prisoners were nearly unrecognizable from the number of bullet wounds they'd received...

ext.ext_cn: 原来的居民可能会认不出这个崭新的城镇了。
ext.ext_en: The new town would have been unrecognisable to the original inhabitants.

defs.def_en: If someone or something is unrecognizable, they have become impossible to recognize or identify, for example because they have been greatly changed or damaged.

ext.ext_cn: 野生蘑菇有很多种。
ext.ext_en: There are many types of wild mushrooms.

ext.ext_cn: 鸡蛋、腊肉、香肠和蘑菇
ext.ext_en: ...eggs, bacon, sausage, and mushrooms.

defs.def_en: See also:button mushroom;Mushrooms are fungi that you can eat.

ext.ext_cn: 在过去10年里，媒体培训产业迅速成长。
ext.ext_en: The media training industry has mushroomed over the past decade...

ext.ext_cn: 几十万人的沉寂首府迅速发展成为拥有两百万人口的拥挤都市。
ext.ext_en: A sleepy capital of a few hundred thousand people has mushroomed to a crowded city of 2 million.

defs.def_en: If something such as an industry or a place mushrooms, it grows or comes into existence very quickly.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 容器一旦装满它会保持关闭，想要打开须按顺时针方向转动。
ext.ext_en: Once the container is full, it stays shut until you turn it clockwise.

ext.ext_cn: 一满箱汽油
ext.ext_en: ...a full tank of petrol.

defs.def_en: If something is full, it contains as much of a substance or as many objects as it can.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 箱子里塞满了衣服。
ext.ext_en: The case was full of clothes...

ext.ext_cn: 街道上仍到处可见连续两晚的骚乱留下的残迹。
ext.ext_en: The streets are still full of debris from two nights of rioting.

defs.def_en: If a place or thing is full of things or people, it contains a large number of them.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 充满(某一情感或特质)的

ext.ext_cn: 我感到信心十足，愿意考虑各种可能。
ext.ext_en: I feel full of confidence and so open to possibilities...

ext.ext_cn: 妈妈的脸上写满了痛苦。
ext.ext_en: Mom's face was full of pain.

defs.def_en: If someone or something is full of a particular feeling or quality, they have a lot of it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 满员的;没有空位(或空间)的

ext.ext_cn: 我 10 点 45 分左右离开时，主停车场已经没有车位了。
ext.ext_en: The main car park was full when I left about 10.45...

ext.ext_cn: 他们在这儿呆了几个小时后被送往难民营，而那里现在几乎已经满员了。
ext.ext_en: They stay here a few hours before being sent to refugee camps, which are now almost full...

defs.def_en: You say that a place or vehicle is full when there is no space left in it for any more people or things.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (手或胳膊)占着的，拿满了的，挂满了的

ext.ext_cn: 西尔维娅走了进来，怀里抱满了包裹。
ext.ext_en: Sylvia entered, her arms full of packages...

ext.ext_cn: 人们到这家商店来总是满载而归。
ext.ext_en: People would go into the store and come out with their arms full.

defs.def_en: If your hands or arms are full, you are carrying or holding as much as you can carry.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 饿了就吃，饱了就停，这样很健康。
ext.ext_en: It's healthy to eat when I'm hungry and to stop when I'm full.

defs.def_en: If you feel full, you have eaten or drunk so much that you do not want anything else.

ext.ext_cn: 所有细节会在申请接受后马上寄出。
ext.ext_en: Full details will be sent to you once your application has been accepted...

ext.ext_cn: 请问您的全名是什么？
ext.ext_en: May I have your full name?...

defs.def_en: You use full before a noun to indicate that you are referring to all the details, things, or people that it can possibly include.

defs.def_cn: (声音、光线、力气等)最大(强度)的

ext.ext_cn: 从他的书房里传出马勒的乐曲，音量开到了最大。
ext.ext_en: From his study came the sound of Mahler, playing at full volume...

ext.ext_cn: 官员们说行动将在大白天进行。
ext.ext_en: Officials say the operation will be carried out in full daylight...

defs.def_en: Full is used to describe a sound, light, or physical force which is being produced with the greatest possible power or intensity.

ext.ext_cn: 我们应该通过充分利用其他能源来节省石油和天然气。
ext.ext_en: We should conserve oil and gas by making full use of other energy sources...

ext.ext_cn: 电视摄像机把这场战争彻头彻尾的恐怖传送到全世界的千家万户。
ext.ext_en: Television cameras are carrying the full horror of this war into homes around the world...

defs.def_en: You use full to emphasize the completeness, intensity, or extent of something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 普里马科夫先生详细叙述了他和总统的会面。
ext.ext_en: Mr Primakov gave a full account of his meeting with the President.

ext.ext_cn: 在这份内容十分全面的文件里包含的海量细节
ext.ext_en: ...the enormous detail in this very full document.

defs.def_en: A full statement or report contains a lot of information and detail.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 你不管做什么都会成功，并且会过着非常充实有趣的生活。
ext.ext_en: You will be successful in whatever you do and you will have a very full and interesting life.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone has or leads a full life, you approve of the fact that they are always busy and do a lot of different things.

ext.ext_cn: 滚烫的液体正好溅进了他的右眼。
ext.ext_en: The burning liquid hit him full in the right eye...

ext.ext_cn: 她直接吻上了他的嘴唇。
ext.ext_en: She kissed him full on the mouth...

defs.def_en: You use full to emphasize the force or directness with which someone or something is hit or looked at.

defs.def_cn: (所拥有的权利、地位或重要性)完整的，正式的

ext.ext_cn: 面谈进行得怎么样，你成为正式成员了吗？
ext.ext_en: How did the meeting go, did you get your full membership?...

ext.ext_cn: 她将临时执照连同考试证书一起提交上去以申请升级为正式执照。
ext.ext_en: She sent her provisional licence with the test certificate to have it upgraded to a full licence.

defs.def_en: You use full to refer to something which gives you all the rights, status, or importance for a particular position or activity, rather than just some of them.

ext.ext_cn: 意大利李形番茄味道很重，最适合烹饪。
ext.ext_en: Italian plum tomatoes have a full flavour, and are best for cooking.

defs.def_en: A full flavour is strong and rich.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (身体某一部位)丰满的，圆润的

ext.ext_cn: 朱诺系列专门针对身材较为丰满的女士推出大号女装。
ext.ext_en: The Juno Collection specialises in large sizes for ladies with a fuller figure.

ext.ext_cn: 他坚挺的下巴、饱满的双唇和迷人的八字胡
ext.ext_en: ...his strong chin, his full lips, his appealing mustache.

defs.def_en: If you describe a part of someone's body as full, you mean that it is rounded and rather large.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我结婚礼服的裙摆很宽松。
ext.ext_en: My wedding dress has a very full skirt.

defs.def_en: A full skirt or sleeve is wide and has been made from a lot of fabric.
When there is a full moon, the moon appears as a bright, complete circle.

ext.ext_cn: 医学专家尚未提出完整的报告。
ext.ext_en: The medical experts have yet to report in full...

ext.ext_cn: 我们保证在 10 个工作日内悉数回复。
ext.ext_en: We guarantee to reply in full within 10 working days.

defs.def_en: You say that something has been done or described in full when everything that was necessary has been done or described.

defs.def_cn: (尤指对令人不快的事)很清楚地知道(或了解)，一清二楚

ext.ext_cn: 他很清楚地知道自己过后会无地自容。
ext.ext_en: He knew full well he'd be ashamed of himself later.

defs.def_en: If you say that a person knows full well that something is true, especially something unpleasant, you are emphasizing that they are definitely aware of it, although they may behave as if they are not.

defs.def_cn: 尽量;在最大程度上;充分地;彻底地

ext.ext_cn: 她可能很有头脑，应该充分运用。
ext.ext_en: She probably has a good mind, which should be used to the full...

ext.ext_cn: 对于爱情我们只应有一种态度：趁其尚未消失时尽情享受。
ext.ext_en: There's only one thing we should do with love; experience it to the full for as long as it lasts.

defs.def_en: Something that is done or experienced to the full is done to as great an extent as is possible.

ext.ext_cn: 他是个自以为是的家伙，说话尖酸又爱挑衅，有时会给人留下极差的印象。
ext.ext_en: He's full of himself, sharp and aggressive and sometimes he comes over badly.

defs.def_en: If you say to someone 'you're full of yourself', you disapprove of them because they appear very pleased with themselves, thinking that they are very clever, special, or important.
A preparatory school is the same as a prep school .
A reported question is a question which is reported using a clause beginning with a word such as 'why' or 'whether', as in 'I asked her why she'd done it'.

ext.ext_cn: 据亨明先生所说，菲利普住在旅馆里。
ext.ext_en: Philip stayed at the hotel, according to Mr Hemming...

ext.ext_cn: 当地风传，他和父亲已多年未联系了。
ext.ext_en: He and his father, according to local gossip, haven't been in touch for years.

defs.def_en: If someone says that something is true according to a particular person, book, or other source of information, they are indicating where they got their information.

ext.ext_cn: 他们俩都依章行事。
ext.ext_en: They both played the game according to the rules...

ext.ext_cn: 他们必须根据各自律师的意见自行决定。
ext.ext_en: They must take their own decision according to their own legal advice.

defs.def_en: If something is done according to a particular set of principles, these principles are used as a basis for the way it is done.

ext.ext_cn: 价格随订购数量不同而有所变化。
ext.ext_en: Prices vary according to the quantity ordered...

ext.ext_cn: 船夫选择的路线会随水位的变化而有所不同。
ext.ext_en: The route that the boatmen choose varies according to the water level.

defs.def_en: If something varies according to a changing factor, it varies in a way that is determined by this factor.

defs.def_cn: 按照计划；如同料想的那样

ext.ext_cn: 如果一切都按计划进行的话，第一场音乐会将在星期二晚上举行。
ext.ext_en: If all goes according to plan, the first concert will be Tuesday evening.

defs.def_en: If something happens according to plan, it happens in exactly the way that it was intended to happen.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我们翻看他们的八卦时带着不洁的想法。
ext.ext_en: We read the gossip written about them with prurient interest.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as prurient, you mean that they show too much interest in sexual matters.

defs.def_cn: 错误的陈述;虚假的报道;谎报

ext.ext_cn: 他终于纠正了自己的错误说法，提出要减少费用。
ext.ext_en: He finally corrected his misstatement and offered to reduce the fee...

ext.ext_cn: 尽管这本小册子已经成为正式的信息来源，里面仍然错误百出。
ext.ext_en: While this booklet has become an official source of information, it is filled with misstatements of fact.

defs.def_en: A misstatement is an incorrect statement, or the giving of false information.

ext.ext_cn: 照理说，价格应该标在货架上。
ext.ext_en: Theoretically, the price is supposed to be marked on the shelf...

ext.ext_cn: 从理论上讲，移民仍是个个人选择的问题。
ext.ext_en: Emigration was still theoretically a matter of choice.

defs.def_en: You use theoretically to say that although something is supposed to be true or to happen in the way stated, it may not in fact be true or happen in that way.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 宁静的;平静的;让人放松的

ext.ext_cn: 调节灯光使其看上去既柔和又能给人带来舒缓感。
ext.ext_en: Adjust the lighting so it is soft and restful...

ext.ext_cn: 度过了愉快轻松的3天后，我离开了这个美丽的城市。
ext.ext_en: After a joyous and restful three days, I left this beautiful city.

defs.def_en: Something that is restful helps you to feel calm and relaxed.

ext.ext_cn: 水供应不足
ext.ext_en: ...the inadequacy of the water supply...

ext.ext_cn: 人们已经认识到现行体制的不足。
ext.ext_en: The inadequacies of the current system have already been recognised...

defs.def_en: The inadequacy of something is the fact that there is not enough of it, or that it is not good enough.

defs.def_cn: 不够格;能力不足;无法胜任

ext.ext_cn: 无法胜任的感觉非常强烈。
ext.ext_en: The feeling of inadequacy was overpowering.

ext.ext_cn: 他内心那种根深蒂固的不自信
ext.ext_en: ...his deep-seated sense of inadequacy.

defs.def_en: If someone has feelings of inadequacy, they feel that they do not have the qualities and abilities necessary to do something or to cope with life in general.

ext.ext_cn: 智人和其他生物的区别在于大脑。
ext.ext_en: What distinguishes homo sapiens from every other living creature is the mind.

defs.def_en: Homo sapiens is used to refer to modern human beings as a species, in contrast to other species of ape or animal, or earlier forms of human.
A swimming costume is the same as a swimsuit .

defs.def_cn: 捡破烂;拾荒;(从废弃物中)觅食，寻找

ext.ext_cn: 很多人是孤儿，他们的父母在垃圾中找吃的时丢了性命。
ext.ext_en: Many are orphans, their parents killed as they scavenged for food...

ext.ext_cn: 孩子们翻捡垃圾。
ext.ext_en: Children scavenge through garbage...

defs.def_en: If people or animals scavenge for things, they collect them by searching among waste or unwanted objects.

ext.ext_cn: 工作中他被看作一个奇人，冒了不少风险却从不会失败。
ext.ext_en: At work he was regarded as a miracle worker, the man who took risks and could not lose.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as a miracle worker, you mean that they have achieved or are able to achieve success in something that other people have found very difficult.
A refinery is a factory where a substance such as oil or sugar is refined.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 虽然地位显赫，但是公爵夫人并不会得到优待。
ext.ext_en: Despite her status, the Duchess will not be given preferential treatment.

defs.def_en: If you get preferential treatment, you are treated better than other people and therefore have an advantage over them.

ext.ext_cn: 公共汽车滑到了一边。
ext.ext_en: The bus slewed sideways...

ext.ext_cn: 一辆 7 吨的货车侧滑到了一侧。
ext.ext_en: A seven-ton lorry slewed across their path...

defs.def_en: If a vehicle slews or is slewed across a road, it slides across it.

ext.ext_cn: 发生过大量枪击案。
ext.ext_en: There have been a whole slew of shooting incidents...

ext.ext_cn: 他们处理了大量的其他问题。
ext.ext_en: They dealt with a slew of other issues.

defs.def_en: A slew of things is a large number of them.
A tree trunk is the wide central part of a tree, from which the branches grow.
A chamber of commerce is an organization of businessmen that promotes local commercial interests.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 水沫四溅的波涛
ext.ext_en: ...foamy waves...

ext.ext_cn: 把蛋清搅至起沫而不黏稠的程度。
ext.ext_en: Whisk the egg whites until they are foamy but not stiff.

defs.def_en: A foamy liquid has a mass of small bubbles on its surface or consists of a mass of bubbles.

ext.ext_cn: 积极呼吁他们的国家融入世界市场的主要倡导者
ext.ext_en: ...the main protagonists of their countries' integration into the world market.

defs.def_en: Someone who is a protagonist of an idea or movement is a supporter of it.

defs.def_cn: 主人公；主角；（真实事件的）主要人物

ext.ext_cn: 塞林格的小说《麦田里的守望者》的主人公
ext.ext_en: ...the protagonist of J. D. Salinger's novel 'The Catcher in the Rye'...

ext.ext_cn: 这场纠纷的主角是世界两大信用卡品牌——维萨和万事达。
ext.ext_en: The chief protagonists in the row are Visa and Mastercard, the world's leading credit card brands.

defs.def_en: A protagonist in a play, novel, or real event is one of the main people in it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 高傲自大的;倨傲无礼的;目中无人的

ext.ext_cn: 他说起话来口气傲慢。
ext.ext_en: He spoke in a haughty tone.

defs.def_en: You use haughty to describe someone's behaviour or appearance when you disapprove of the fact that they seem to be very proud and to think that they are better than other people.

ext.ext_cn: 罐焖羊肉
ext.ext_en: ...lamb hotpot.

defs.def_en: A hotpot is a mixture of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid in the oven.
If you have indigestion, you have pains in your stomach and chest that are caused by difficulties in digesting food.
A plasterer is a person whose job it is to cover walls and ceilings with plaster.

defs.def_cn: 超出常人的;非凡的;超人的

ext.ext_cn: 军官们被他超凡的力量吓坏了。
ext.ext_en: Officers were terrified of his superhuman strength...

ext.ext_cn: 尽管他们已想方设法节约用水，水费仍旧在稳步上升。
ext.ext_en: They saw their bills rising steadily, in spite of superhuman efforts to save water.

defs.def_en: If you describe a quality that someone has as superhuman, you mean that it seems to be much greater than that of ordinary people.
Stocktaking is the activity of counting and checking all the goods that a shop or business has.
Embezzlement is the crime of embezzling money.

defs.def_cn: 某物，某事(指事物、情况、事件、想法等)

ext.ext_cn: 他马上意识到什么地方出了问题。
ext.ext_en: He realized right away that there was something wrong...

ext.ext_cn: 他身上有着某种似曾相识的东西。
ext.ext_en: There was something vaguely familiar about him...

defs.def_en: You use something to refer to a thing, situation, event, or idea, without saying exactly what it is.

defs.def_cn: (描述、数量等)大概，大致，大约，左右

ext.ext_cn: 他形容那种气味介于马戏团和海港的味道之间。
ext.ext_en: He described the smell as something between a circus and a seaport...

ext.ext_cn: 克莱夫发出一种声响，像是咕哝了一句。
ext.ext_en: Clive made a noise, something like a grunt...

defs.def_en: You can use something to say that the description or amount that you are giving is not exact.

ext.ext_cn: 你真了不起。
ext.ext_en: You're really something...

ext.ext_cn: 这些门真是极品，全部由红木一类的优质木材加工而成。
ext.ext_en: The doors here are really something, all made of good wood like mahogany...

defs.def_en: If you say that a person or thing is something or is really something, you mean that you are very impressed by them.

defs.def_cn: 聊以自慰的事;还算幸运的事

ext.ext_cn: 好啦，至少他在城里，还算幸运。
ext.ext_en: Well, at least he was in town. That was something...

ext.ext_cn: 啊，你准备留下来了。我想这算是能够聊以自慰吧。
ext.ext_en: Well, you're staying. That's something I suppose.

defs.def_en: You can use something in expressions like 'that's something' when you think that a situation is not very good but is better that it might have been.

ext.ext_cn: 结果这座城市有点儿令人失望。
ext.ext_en: The city proved to be something of a disappointment...

ext.ext_cn: 当罗伯特说他就要来纽约的时候，她有点吃惊。
ext.ext_en: She received something of a surprise when Robert said that he was coming to New York...

defs.def_en: If you say that a thing is something of a disappointment, you mean that it is quite disappointing. If you say that a person is something of an artist, you mean that they are quite good at art.

defs.def_cn: (想法或建议)有道理，值得考虑

ext.ext_en: Christianity has stood the test of time, so there must be something in it...

ext.ext_cn: 德斯最初的陈述有些道理。
ext.ext_en: There had been something in Des's first statement...

defs.def_en: If you say that there is something in an idea or suggestion, you mean that it is quite good and should be considered seriously.

defs.def_cn: (表示对说的话不能肯定)或别的什么，或诸如此类

ext.ext_en: This guy, his name was Briarly or Beardly or something...

ext.ext_en: The air fare was about a hundred and ninety-nine pounds or something like that.

defs.def_en: You use something in expressions such as 'or something' and 'or something like that' to indicate that you are referring to something similar to what you have just mentioned but you are not being exact.

defs.def_cn: (书面语中表示反对、厌烦、同情等发出的)啧啧声,咂嘴声
defs.def_en: Tut-tut is used in writing to represent the sound that you make with your tongue touching the top of your mouth when you want to indicate disapproval, annoyance, or sympathy.

defs.def_cn: 反对；（尤指）啧啧地表示反对

ext.ext_cn: 我们都没少对安吉和她的生活方式啧啧非议。
ext.ext_en: We all spent a lot of time tut-tutting about Angie and her lifestyle...

ext.ext_cn: 医生啧啧不满，把我的话当作借口不予理睬。
ext.ext_en: The doctor tut-tutted, dismissing my words as excuses.

defs.def_en: If you tut-tut about something, you express your disapproval of it, especially by making a sound with your tongue touching the top of your mouth.

ext.ext_cn: 1,000吨原油从一艘油轮中泄漏，流入了海洋。
ext.ext_en: A thousand tons of crude oil has spilled into the sea from an oil tanker.

defs.def_en: Crude oil is oil in its natural state before it has been processed or refined.

ext.ext_cn: 新生的肯尼亚民主政治

ext.ext_cn: 方兴未艾的心理学
ext.ext_en: ...the still nascent science of psychology.

defs.def_en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

defs.def_en: The chief executive officer of a company is the person who has overall responsibility for the management of that company. The abbreviation CEO is often used.

ext.ext_cn: 他说自己可以对这枚邮票进行鉴定。
ext.ext_en: He says he'll have no problem authenticating the stamp...

ext.ext_cn: 所有的古董都已经过鉴别并进行记录。
ext.ext_en: All the antiques have been authenticated and recorded.

defs.def_en: If you authenticate something, you state officially that it is genuine after examining it.

ext.ext_en: Documentaries offered the chance to authenticate the accuracy of the various details in these models...

ext.ext_en: There have now been well authenticated reports that the use of this drug is very occasionally responsible for heart attacks.

defs.def_en: If you authenticate something, you prove or confirm that it is true.

ext.ext_cn: 她跑出了13.01秒的个人最好成绩。
ext.ext_en: She ran a personal best of 13.01 sec.

defs.def_en: A sports player's personal best is the highest score or fastest time that they have ever achieved.

defs.def_cn: (have 为助动词时， could have 的常用口语形式)
defs.def_en: Could've is the usual spoken form of 'could have', when 'have' is an auxiliary verb.

ext.ext_cn: 最近的民意测验预测竞争将会非常激烈。
ext.ext_en: The latest opinion polls are predicting a very close contest...

ext.ext_cn: 他预言我的头发“一眨眼”就会长回来。
ext.ext_en: He predicted that my hair would grow back 'in no time'...

defs.def_en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 莫里斯连续3周都不大舒服，但又没有什么明显的症状。
ext.ext_en: For three weeks Maurice felt off-colour but did not have any dramatic symptoms.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are feeling off-colour, you mean that you are slightly ill.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 表现差强人意的；状态不佳的

ext.ext_en: Milan looked off-colour but eventually took the lead in the 82nd minute.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone's performance is off-colour, you mean that they are not performing as well as they usually do.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: （笑话、言语）近乎下流的，不成体统的

ext.ext_cn: 他否认曾口出对女性不敬的污言秽语。
ext.ext_en: He denies making off-color remarks about women.

defs.def_en: An off-colour joke or remark is rather rude or offensive.

defs.def_cn: 服装的;裁缝的;缝纫的;衣着的

ext.ext_en: ...Sebastian's sartorial elegance...

ext.ext_cn: 詹姆斯给了他一些穿着方面的建议。
ext.ext_en: James gave him some sartorial advice.

defs.def_en: Sartorial means relating to clothes and to the way they are made or worn.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: He was thin and tall, with a hooked nose.

ext.ext_cn: 钩状爪
ext.ext_en: ...hooked claws.

defs.def_en: If you describe something as hooked, you mean that it is shaped like a hook.

ext.ext_en: Many of the leaders have become hooked on power and money...

defs.def_en: If you are hooked on something, you enjoy it so much that it takes up a lot of your interest and attention.

ext.ext_en: He spent a number of years hooked on cocaine, heroin and alcohol.

defs.def_en: If you are hooked on a drug, you are addicted to it.

ext.ext_cn: 但是，那已不在法庭权限之内；那是个外交问题。
ext.ext_en: That, however, was beyond the purview of the court; it was a diplomatic matter.

defs.def_en: The purview of something such as an organization or activity is the range of things it deals with.

ext.ext_cn: 报纸的大字标题表明峰会上大家作出了妥协。
ext.ext_en: The newspaper's headline indicates that there was a trade-off at the summit.

ext.ext_cn: 在通货膨胀与失业之间求得平衡
ext.ext_en: ...the trade-off between inflation and unemployment.

defs.def_en: A trade-off is a situation where you make a compromise between two things, or where you exchange all or part of one thing for another.

ext.ext_en: Ozone is best known for its role in screening the Earth from harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun...

ext.ext_cn: 他们的发现可以揭示如果臭氧持续减少，世界范围内可能会出现什么情况。
ext.ext_en: What they find could provide clues to what might happen worldwide if ozone depletion continues.

ext.ext_cn: 已故的朋友
ext.ext_en: ...departed friends.

ext.ext_en: We held services for the departed.

defs.def_en: Departed friends or relatives are people who have died.

defs.def_cn: 佛陀（对佛教创始人乔答摩·悉达多的尊称）
defs.def_en: Buddha is the title given to Gautama Siddhartha, the religious teacher and founder of Buddhism.

A hammock is a piece of strong cloth or netting which is hung between two supports and used as a bed.

defs.def_cn: （书籍、影片或展览的）简介，宣传信息
defs.def_en: The blurb about a new book, film, or exhibition is information about it that is written in order to attract people's interest.

ext.ext_cn: 官员们感觉自己的观点并未准确地传达到大臣们那里。
ext.ext_en: Officers felt their point of view was not getting across to ministers...

ext.ext_cn: 我想出了一种能言简意赅地表达自己意思的方法。
ext.ext_en: I had created a way to get my message across while using as few words as possible.

defs.def_en: When an idea gets across or when you get it across, you succeed in making other people understand it.
If an organization or system is given a shakedown, it is thoroughly reorganized in order to make it more efficient.

defs.def_cn: (船只、飞机、汽车的)试用，试航，试飞
defs.def_en: A shakedown of a boat, plane, or car is its final test before it starts to be used.

ext.ext_cn: 能让人充分发挥学习潜质的轻松愉快的环境
ext.ext_en: ...a relaxed and happy atmosphere that will allow you to study to your full potential...

ext.ext_cn: 他去了赫尔大学学习历史和经济学。
ext.ext_en: He went to Hull University, where he studied History and Economics...

defs.def_en: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

ext.ext_cn: 利用地图和图像资料研究当地历史
ext.ext_en: ...the use of maps and visual evidence in the study of local history...

ext.ext_cn: 为了生亚历山大，她放弃了学业。
ext.ext_en: She gave up her studies to have Alexander.

defs.def_en: Study is the activity of studying.

ext.ext_cn: 最近的研究成果表明在 1000 个刚生产完的妈妈中，有 5 个可能存在这样的问题。
ext.ext_en: Recent studies suggest that as many as 5 in 1000 new mothers are likely to have this problem.

ext.ext_cn: 首个关于英国儿童观念的研究
ext.ext_en: ...the first study of English children's attitudes.

defs.def_en: A study of a subject is a piece of research on it.

ext.ext_cn: 新的伊斯兰教研究中心
ext.ext_en: ...a new centre for Islamic studies...

ext.ext_cn: 她目前在利兹大学修读一门商科课程。
ext.ext_en: She is currently doing a business studies course at Leeds.

defs.def_en: You can refer to educational subjects or courses that contain several elements as studies of a particular kind.

ext.ext_en: Debbie studied her friend's face for a moment.

defs.def_en: If you study something, you look at it or watch it very carefully, in order to find something out.

ext.ext_en: I know that you've been studying chimpanzees for thirty years now...

ext.ext_en: I invite every citizen to carefully study the document.

defs.def_en: If you study something, you consider it or observe it carefully in order to be able to understand it fully.

ext.ext_cn: 他们只好找体力活儿干。

ext.ext_en: Four people who sought refuge in the Italian embassy have left voluntarily...

defs.def_en: If you seek something such as a job or a place to live, you try to find one.

ext.ext_en: On important issues, they seek a second opinion...

defs.def_en: If you seek someone's help or advice, you contact them in order to ask for it.
