ext.ext_en: He cast his eyes at the rows of cabinets that filled the enormous work area...

ext.ext_cn: 正文占了 231 页。
ext.ext_en: The text fills 231 pages.

defs.def_en: If something fills a space, it is so big, or there are such large quantities of it, that there is very little room left.

ext.ext_cn: 用颜色相配的木质填料填平小孔。
ext.ext_en: Fill small holes with wood filler in a matching colour...

ext.ext_cn: 掘墓人把墓穴填上。
ext.ext_en: The gravedigger filled the grave.

defs.def_en: If you fill a crack or hole, you put a substance into it in order to make the surface smooth again.

ext.ext_cn: 警报声响彻学校停车场。
ext.ext_en: In the parking lot of the school, the siren filled the air...

ext.ext_cn: 所有灯条都打开了，满屋都是旋转的光柱。
ext.ext_en: All the light bars were turned on which filled the room with these rotating beams of light...

defs.def_en: If a sound, smell, or light fills a space, or the air, it is very strong or noticeable.

defs.def_cn: 使强烈地感到;(感情)充盈于

ext.ext_cn: 我很钦佩父亲，并对他的工作充满了敬畏和好奇。
ext.ext_en: I admired my father, and his work filled me with awe and curiosity...

ext.ext_cn: 他看着我没有说话，我第一次看出他内心充满了自豪。
ext.ext_en: He looked at me without speaking, and for the first time I could see the pride that filled him...

defs.def_en: If something fills you with an emotion, or if an emotion fills you, you experience this emotion strongly.

ext.ext_cn: 如果她想做些日常的事务来打发白天的时间，就让她去做社区工作吧。
ext.ext_en: If she wants a routine to fill her day, let her do community work.

ext.ext_cn: 星期四晚上她去上了瑜伽课，很高兴自己有事可做。
ext.ext_en: On Thursday night she went to her yoga class, glad to have something to fill up the evening.

defs.def_en: If you fill a period of time with a particular activity, you spend the time in this way.

ext.ext_cn: 组织得当、人员配备齐整的日托中心满足了人们的需求，保持了家庭结构不受破坏。
ext.ext_en: ...properly organized and staffed day-care programs fill a need which allows family structures to remain intact...

ext.ext_cn: 她带给他开心快乐，弥补了他生命中的缺憾。
ext.ext_en: She brought him a sense of fun, of gaiety that filled a gap in his life.

defs.def_en: If something fills a need or a gap, it puts an end to this need or gap by existing or being active.

ext.ext_cn: 德娜利用她多年来学到的处事技巧扮演着外交家妻子的角色。
ext.ext_en: Dena was filling the role of diplomat's wife with the skill she had learned over the years.

defs.def_en: If something fills a role, position, or function, they have that role or position, or perform that function, often successfully.

ext.ext_cn: 一个没有提及的问题是，失业人员也许缺乏填补所提供的空职的技能。
ext.ext_en: One problem not mentioned is the unemployed may not have the skills to fill the vacancies on offer...

ext.ext_cn: 有一个职位空了出来，我想要补上。
ext.ext_en: A vacancy has arisen which I intend to fill.

defs.def_en: If a company or organization fills a job vacancy, they choose someone to do the job. If someone fills a job vacancy, they accept a job that they have been offered.

ext.ext_cn: 他们开着玩笑，喝着咖啡，尽情地吃着巧克力蛋糕。
ext.ext_en: They joked and drank coffee and filled themselves with chocolate cake.

defs.def_en: If you fill yourself with food, you eat so much that you do not feel hungry.

defs.def_cn: 使爆满;使满座;使座无虚席

ext.ext_cn: 孩子们为他的故事所着迷;众所周知他在澳大利亚总是场场爆满。
ext.ext_en: Children are enthralled by his stories; he has been known to fill theatre halls in Australia.

defs.def_en: A play, film, or performer that fills a theatre, concert hall, or cinema attracts a very large audience.

ext.ext_cn: 几乎不可能找到一位愿意接受国民医疗保健来补牙的医师。
ext.ext_en: It is almost impossible to find a dentist who will fill a tooth on the National Health.

defs.def_en: When a dentist fills someone's tooth, he or she puts a filling in it.

ext.ext_cn: 只要药剂师认定处方有效就可按方配药。
ext.ext_en: A pharmacist can fill any prescription if, in his or her judgment, the prescription is valid.

defs.def_en: If you fill an order or a prescription, you provide the things that are asked for.

ext.ext_cn: 我们觉得已经受够了失望和情绪困扰。
ext.ext_en: We feel that we have had our fill of disappointments and emotional upsets.

defs.def_en: If you have had your fill of something, you have had enough of it, and do not want to experience it any more or do it any more.

ext.ext_cn: 如果想要一份免费的《病人约章》，就把这张表填一下。
ext.ext_en: If you want your free copy of the Patients' Charter fill this form in...

ext.ext_cn: 填写订单，并按一类邮件寄至注明的地址。
ext.ext_en: Fill in the coupon and send it first class to the address shown.

defs.def_en: If you fill in a form or other document requesting information, you write information in the spaces on it.

ext.ext_cn: 两人都把图案填好色后，不妨互相交换着看一下。
ext.ext_en: When you have both filled in your patterns, you may want to share these with each other...

ext.ext_cn: 用唇线笔勾出双唇的轮廓，然后涂上唇膏。
ext.ext_en: With a lip pencil, outline lips and fill them in.

defs.def_en: If you fill in a shape, you cover the area inside the lines with colour or shapes so that none of the background is showing.

ext.ext_cn: 我还没有告诉里德所有详情——我会讲给他听的。
ext.ext_en: I didn't give Reid all the details yet — I'll fill him in...

ext.ext_cn: 他告诉她威尔伯·坎特此行的详细经过。
ext.ext_en: He filled her in on Wilbur Kantor's visit.

defs.def_en: If you fill someone in, you give them more details about something that you know about.

ext.ext_cn: 副总统夫人们将临时代替各位第一夫人。
ext.ext_en: Vice-presidents' wives would fill in for first ladies.

defs.def_en: If you fill in for someone, you do the work or task that they normally do because they are unable to do it.

ext.ext_cn: 那算不上什么事业，她只不过是在嫁人之前打发一下时间而已。
ext.ext_en: That's not a career. She's just filling in time until she gets married.

defs.def_en: See also:fill;If you are filling in time, you are using time that is available by doing something that is not very important.

ext.ext_cn: 仔细填写申请表，并且保存副本。
ext.ext_en: Fill out the application carefully, and keep copies of it.

defs.def_en: If you fill out a form or other document requesting information, you write information in the spaces on it.

ext.ext_cn: 女孩子在长足个头之前可能会发胖。
ext.ext_en: A girl may fill out before she reaches her full height.

defs.def_en: If a fairly thin person fills out, they become fatter.

ext.ext_cn: 用碳水化合物含量高、脂肪含量低的土豆、面包和意大利面食填饱肚子。
ext.ext_en: Fill up on potatoes, bread and pasta, which are high in carbohydrate and low in fat...

ext.ext_cn: 一个人如果感觉舒心，就不必去胡吃海塞。
ext.ext_en: When you are happy about yourself you won't need to fill yourself up with food.

defs.def_en: If you fill up or fill yourself up with food, you eat so much that you do not feel hungry.

ext.ext_cn: 吃土豆容易让我们有一种饱胀感，又不会摄入过多的热量。
ext.ext_en: Potatoes fill us up without overloading us with calories.

defs.def_en: See also:fill 1;2;6;A type of food that fills you up makes you feel that you have eaten a lot, even though you have only eaten a small amount.

ext.ext_cn: 到旅游淡季，价格会降到315英镑。
ext.ext_en: Prices drop to £315 in the low season.

defs.def_en: The low season is the time of year when a place receives the fewest visitors, and fares and holiday accommodation are often cheaper.
A footlocker is a large box for keeping personal possessions in, especially one that is placed at the end of a bed.

defs.def_cn: (连衣裙或胸罩)无肩带的，无吊带的

ext.ext_cn: 黑色的无肩带女式晚礼服
ext.ext_en: ...a black, strapless evening dress.

defs.def_en: A strapless dress or bra does not have the usual narrow bands of material over the shoulders.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: （研究、检查、调查）十分小心的，极其仔细的，缜密的

ext.ext_cn: 法医专家对残骸进行了极其仔细的搜索。
ext.ext_en: Forensic experts carried out a painstaking search of the debris.

defs.def_en: A painstaking search, examination, or investigation is done extremely carefully and thoroughly.
A cake pan is a metal container that you bake a cake in.

ext.ext_cn: 自己在家锻炼需要很强的自我约束能力。
ext.ext_en: Exercising at home alone requires a tremendous amount of self-discipline.

defs.def_en: Self-discipline is the ability to control yourself and to make yourself work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell you what to do.

ext.ext_cn: 鳕鱼子
ext.ext_en: ...cod's roe.

defs.def_en: Roe is the eggs or sperm of a fish, which is eaten as food.

ext.ext_cn: 伊朗在伦敦重开使馆。
ext.ext_en: Iran reopened its embassy in London...

ext.ext_cn: 造船厂计划明天重新开张。
ext.ext_en: It plans to reopen the shipyard tomorrow...

defs.def_en: If you reopen a public building such as a factory, airport, or school, or if it reopens, it opens and starts working again after it has been closed for some time.

ext.ext_cn: 今天有人呼吁对爆炸事件重新展开调查。
ext.ext_en: There was a call today to reopen the investigation into the bombing.

defs.def_en: If police or the courts reopen a legal case, they investigate it again because it has never been solved or because there was something wrong in the way it was investigated before.

ext.ext_cn: 但现在高层代表团将恢复今年早些时候终止的对话。
ext.ext_en: But now high level delegations will reopen talks that broke up earlier this year.

ext.ext_cn: 与政府重启谈判的可能性
ext.ext_en: ...the possibility of reopening negotiations with the government...

defs.def_en: If people or countries reopen talks or negotiations or if talks or negotiations reopen, they begin again after they have stopped for some time.

defs.def_cn: 重新建立，恢复(联系或关系)

ext.ext_cn: 今年早些时候他重新建立了和莫斯科的联系。
ext.ext_en: He reopened ties with Moscow earlier this year...

ext.ext_cn: 英国和阿根廷重新建立了外交关系。
ext.ext_en: Britain and Argentina reopened diplomatic relations.

defs.def_en: If people or countries reopen ties or relations, they start being friendly again after a time when they were not friendly.

defs.def_cn: 重新提出(问题);重新引起(辩论)

ext.ext_cn: 他的结果可能会重新引起关于种族和教育的辩论。
ext.ext_en: His results are likely to reopen the debate on race and education.

defs.def_en: If something reopens a question or debate, it makes the question or debate relevant again and causes people to start discussing it again.

ext.ext_cn: 约旦重新开放了与伊拉克的边界。
ext.ext_en: Jordan reopened its border with Iraq...

ext.ext_cn: 到中午的时候这条路线就重新开放了。
ext.ext_en: The route had been reopened by noon.

defs.def_en: If a country reopens a border or route, or if it reopens, it becomes possible to cross or travel along it again after it has been closed.

ext.ext_cn: 贝里先生说这是时间上的巧合，他的决定与罗曼先生的离开没有关系。
ext.ext_en: Mr. Berry said the timing was a coincidence and that his decision was unrelated to Mr. Roman's departure...

ext.ext_cn: 一连串惊人的巧合
ext.ext_en: ...a string of amazing coincidences...

defs.def_en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

ext.ext_cn: 他几乎没受过正式的学校教育。
ext.ext_en: He had little formal schooling.

ext.ext_cn: 帮助较贫穷家庭支付私立学校学费的代币券计划
ext.ext_en: ...a voucher scheme to help poorer families pay for private schooling.

defs.def_en: Schooling is education that children receive at school.
A POW is the same as a prisoner of war .

ext.ext_cn: 妇女有时仅仅因为性别而无法获得种种机会。
ext.ext_en: Women are sometimes denied opportunities solely because of their gender.

ext.ext_cn: 长期以来因为性别、肤色、种族或年龄而遭歧视的人群
ext.ext_en: ...groups that are traditionally discriminated against on grounds of gender, colour, race, or age.

defs.def_en: A person's  gender is the fact that they are male or female.

ext.ext_cn: 虽然她的评论就某些男人而言可能是正确的，但绝不适用于所有男性。
ext.ext_en: While her observations may be true about some men, they could hardly apply to the entire gender.

ext.ext_cn: 两性具备的不同能力和技能
ext.ext_en: ...the different abilities and skills of the two genders.

defs.def_en: You can refer to all male people or all female people as a particular gender.

defs.def_cn: （语法中名词、代词或形容词的）性

ext.ext_cn: 在威尔士语和爱尔兰语中，表示“月亮”的词是阴性的。
ext.ext_en: In both Welsh and Irish the word for 'moon' is of feminine gender.

defs.def_en: In grammar, the gender of a noun, pronoun, or adjective is whether it is masculine, feminine, or neuter. A word's  gender can affect its form and behaviour. In English, only personal pronouns such as 'she', reflexive pronouns such as 'itself', and possessive determiners such as 'his' have gender.
A cinder block is a large grey brick made from coal cinders and cement which is used for building.

ext.ext_cn: 拿起听筒就会发亮的电话键盘
ext.ext_en: ...a keypad that lights up when you pick up the handset...

ext.ext_cn: 9月5日，也就是庆祝活动的最后，会有大型焰火表演照亮布罗德兰附近的夜空。
ext.ext_en: On September 5, at the end of the festival, a massive display of fireworks will light up the sky around Broadlands.

defs.def_en: If you light something up or if it lights up, it becomes bright, usually when you shine light on it.

defs.def_cn: 现出吃惊的神情；露出喜色

ext.ext_cn: 她一脸惊诧。
ext.ext_en: Sue's face lit up with surprise...

ext.ext_cn: 你真该看看他谈到家的时候眼睛放光的模样。
ext.ext_en: You should see his eyes light up when he talks about home.

defs.def_en: If your face or your eyes light up you suddenly look very surprised or happy.

ext.ext_cn: 他拿了根火柴为她点烟。
ext.ext_en: He held a match while she lit up...

ext.ext_cn: 他不慌不忙地点了一支烟。
ext.ext_en: He took his time lighting up a cigarette.

defs.def_en: If you light up, you make a cigarette, cigar, or pipe start burning and you start smoking it.
A goblet is a type of cup without handles and usually with a long stem.

ext.ext_cn: 婚礼的前奏非常有意思。
ext.ext_en: The lead-up to the wedding was extremely interesting.

defs.def_en: The lead-up to an event is the things connected to that event that happen before it.

defs.def_cn: (尤指帆船上系绳用的)系索耳，羊角
defs.def_en: A cleat is a kind of hook with two ends which is used to hold ropes, especially on sailing boats.
A biopic is a film that tells the story of someone's life.

defs.def_cn: 收条；收据；购物小票（在美语里常用 sales slip）

ext.ext_cn: 我给她写了一张收钱的收条。
ext.ext_en: I wrote her a receipt for the money.

defs.def_en: A receipt is a piece of paper that you get from someone as proof that they have received money or goods from you. In British English a receipt is a piece of paper that you get in a shop when you buy something, but in American English the more usual term for this is sales slip .

defs.def_cn: （商店或影院等一定时期的）收入，收益

ext.ext_cn: 这部影片的票房收入开始的时候持续上涨，但是后来急剧下降。
ext.ext_en: The film opened to healthy box office receipts before rapidly falling off...

ext.ext_cn: 他正在清点一天的收入。
ext.ext_en: He was tallying the day's receipts.

defs.def_en: Receipts are the amount of money received during a particular period, for example by a shop or theatre.

ext.ext_cn: 应该在收到订单后28天内供货。
ext.ext_en: Goods should be supplied within 28 days after the receipt of your order.

defs.def_en: The receipt of something is the act of receiving it.

ext.ext_cn: 收到他的信之后我们正在采取行动。
ext.ext_en: We are taking action, having been in receipt of a letter from him...

ext.ext_cn: 我定期领取养老金。
ext.ext_en: I am in receipt of a pension.

defs.def_en: If you are in receipt of something, you have received it or you receive it regularly.
Tonsillitis is a painful swelling of your tonsils caused by an infection.

ext.ext_cn: 路面上有些油，汽车车轮经过时直打滑。
ext.ext_en: The car wheels spun and slipped on some oil on the road.

ext.ext_cn: 带轮的小推车
ext.ext_en: ...a trolley on wheels...

defs.def_en: The wheels of a vehicle are the circular objects which are fixed underneath it and which enable it to move along the ground.

ext.ext_cn: 一个带有水轮的18世纪磨粉机
ext.ext_en: ...an eighteenth century mill with a water wheel.

defs.def_en: A wheel is a circular object which forms a part of a machine, usually a moving part.

ext.ext_cn: 我的副驾驶突然抓住了方向盘。
ext.ext_en: My co-pilot suddenly grabbed the wheel...

ext.ext_cn: 由柯蒂斯开车，他们启程返回小屋。
ext.ext_en: Curtis got behind the wheel and they started back toward the cottage...

defs.def_en: The wheel of a car or other vehicle is the circular object that is used to steer it. The wheel is used in expressions to talk about who is driving a vehicle. For example, if someone is at the wheel of a car, they are driving it.

ext.ext_cn: “你有房吗？”——“没有，但我有车。”
ext.ext_en: 'Do you own a house?' — 'No. But I have wheels.'

defs.def_en: People sometimes refer to a car as wheels .

ext.ext_cn: 他把自行车推进了房子旁的小巷中。
ext.ext_en: He wheeled his bike into the alley at the side of the house...

ext.ext_cn: 他们用担架床把她推了出去。
ext.ext_en: They wheeled her out on the stretcher.

defs.def_en: If you wheel an object that has wheels somewhere, you push it along.

ext.ext_cn: 一群乌鸦在头顶上盘旋。
ext.ext_en: A flock of crows wheeled overhead.

defs.def_en: If something such as a group of animals or birds wheels, it moves in a circle.

defs.def_cn: (因惊讶、震惊或生气)突然转身

ext.ext_cn: 他突然转过身来面对她。
ext.ext_en: He wheeled around to face her...

ext.ext_cn: 她突然转身，朝收银台走去。
ext.ext_en: She wheeled sharply and headed for the check-out counter.

defs.def_en: If you wheel around, you turn around suddenly where you are standing, often because you are surprised, shocked, or angry.

defs.def_cn: (尤指多次发生相同的情形)命运之轮

ext.ext_cn: 风水会轮流转；在政治上，它总是如此。
ext.ext_en: The wheel of fortune will swing round again; in politics, it always does...

ext.ext_cn: 在他看来历史的车轮不能倒退。
ext.ext_en: In his view the wheel of history could not be turned back.

defs.def_en: You use wheel in expressions such as the wheel of fortune to refer to the changes that take place in life, especially when you are referring to the fact that the same situations occur more than once.

ext.ext_cn: 他知道行政机关办事效率低。
ext.ext_en: He knows the wheels of administration turn slowly.

defs.def_en: People talk about the wheels of an organization or system to mean the way in which it operates.  to oil the wheels→see: oil;

defs.def_cn: (各种影响、原因和行动交织在一起的)错综复杂的情况

ext.ext_cn: 我们的文化比他所知道的要复杂得多，相当庞杂。
ext.ext_en: Our culture is more complex than he knows. Wheels within wheels.

defs.def_en: If you say that there are wheels within wheels, you mean that there are a number of different influences, reasons, and actions which together make a situation complicated and difficult to understand.

defs.def_cn: 雷格泰姆音乐（20世纪初流行于美国的一种爵士乐）
defs.def_en: Ragtime is a kind of jazz piano music that was invented in America in the early 1900s.

defs.def_cn: 雪利酒(原产自西班牙西南部的烈性葡萄酒，通常于餐前饮用)

ext.ext_cn: 我给大家倒了杯雪利酒。
ext.ext_en: I poured us a glass of sherry.

ext.ext_cn: 世界上的一些极品雪利酒
ext.ext_en: ...some of the world's finest sherries.

defs.def_en: Sherry is a type of strong wine that is made in south-western Spain. It is usually drunk before a meal.
A nunnery is a group of buildings in which a community of nuns live together.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (食物)加了很多香料的，辛辣的

ext.ext_cn: 泰国菜味道辛辣浓烈。
ext.ext_en: Thai food is hot and spicy.

ext.ext_cn: 番茄芫荽香辣酱
ext.ext_en: ...a spicy tomato and coriander sauce.

defs.def_en: Spicy food is strongly flavoured with spices.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 她学习了8种外语，但是只能流利地说其中 6 种。
ext.ext_en: She studied eight foreign languages but is fluent in only six of them...

ext.ext_cn: 他说一口流利的俄语。
ext.ext_en: He speaks fluent Russian.

defs.def_en: Someone who is fluent in a particular language can speak the language easily and correctly. You can also say that someone speaks fluent French, Chinese, or some other language.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (语言或文字)流畅的，熟练的;文笔好的

ext.ext_cn: 他从一个吞吞吐吐、缺乏自信的候选人成长为口若悬河的辩论者。
ext.ext_en: He had emerged from being a hesitant and unsure candidate into a fluent debater.

defs.def_en: If your speech, reading, or writing is fluent, you speak, read, or write easily, smoothly, and clearly with no mistakes.

ext.ext_cn: 她的针线活很漂亮，并且还会刺绣台布。
ext.ext_en: She did beautiful needlework and she embroidered table napkins.

defs.def_en: Needlework is sewing or stitching that is done by hand.

ext.ext_cn: 看我妈妈和祖母外祖母做针线活
ext.ext_en: ...watching my mother and grandmothers doing needlework.

defs.def_en: Needlework is the activity of sewing or stitching.
A rivulet is a small stream.
A translator is a person whose job is translating writing or speech from one language to another.

defs.def_cn: 不假思索地说出；脱口而出

ext.ext_cn: 问他懂哪些英文词，塞姆科先生不假思索地回答：“一，二，三。”
ext.ext_en: Asked what English he knew, Mr Semko rattled off 'One, two, three'...

ext.ext_cn: 亨德里在一场下午的比赛中以6比1的比分轻松地打败了英国选手。
ext.ext_en: Hendry, playing an afternoon match, rattled off a 6-1 win over the Englishman.

defs.def_en: If you rattle off something, you say it or do it very quickly and without much effort.

ext.ext_cn: 斜纹图案
ext.ext_en: ...a pattern of diagonal lines.

defs.def_en: A diagonal line or movement goes in a sloping direction, for example, from one corner of a square across to the opposite corner.

ext.ext_cn: 床单有漂亮的方格形、条纹、斜纹和三角形图案。
ext.ext_en: The bed linen is patterned in stylish checks, stripes, diagonals and triangles.

defs.def_en: A diagonal is a line that goes in a sloping direction.

ext.ext_cn: 在对角线上等距地标出5点。
ext.ext_en: Mark five points an equal distance apart along the diagonals.

defs.def_en: In geometry, a diagonal is a straight line that joins two opposite corners in a flat four-sided shape such as a square.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 那音乐有一种梦幻般的哀伤。
ext.ext_en: The music has a dreamy, elegiac quality.

defs.def_en: Something that is elegiac expresses or shows sadness.

ext.ext_cn: 到了晚上，瞳孔就会扩大以接收更多光线。
ext.ext_en: At night, the pupils dilate to allow in more light...

ext.ext_cn: 运动会使大脑表层的血管扩张。
ext.ext_en: Exercise dilates blood vessels on the surface of the brain.

defs.def_en: When things such as blood vessels or the pupils of your eyes dilate or when something dilates them, they become wider or bigger.

defs.def_cn: 心灵手巧;善于创造发明

ext.ext_cn: 探查鸟巢是需要些技巧的。
ext.ext_en: Inspecting the nest may require some ingenuity.

defs.def_en: Ingenuity is skill at working out how to achieve things or skill at inventing new things.

ext.ext_cn: 新的激光技术
ext.ext_en: ...new laser technology...

ext.ext_cn: 研究人员意识到，可调谐激光束也许可以用在外科手术中。
ext.ext_en: Researchers realised that a tunable laser beam might be useful in surgery.

defs.def_en: A laser is a narrow beam of concentrated light produced by a special machine. It is used for cutting very hard materials, and in many technical fields such as surgery and telecommunications.

ext.ext_cn: 有史以来第一台激光器，于1960年制造
ext.ext_en: ...the first-ever laser, built in 1960.

defs.def_en: A laser is a machine that produces a laser beam.

ext.ext_cn: 叛乱分子完全控制了局面。
ext.ext_en: The rebels had taken complete control...

ext.ext_cn: 这表明管理层对此完全不了解。
ext.ext_en: It shows a complete lack of understanding by management...

defs.def_en: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.

ext.ext_cn: 整幢公寓大楼被付之一炬。
ext.ext_en: A complete tenement block was burnt to the ground...

ext.ext_cn: 工作指导卡最终装满了整整一个册子。
ext.ext_en: The job sheets eventually filled a complete book.

defs.def_en: You can use complete to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something and not just part of it.

ext.ext_cn: 这个单子可能不全。
ext.ext_en: The list may not be complete.

ext.ext_cn: 一整套餐具
ext.ext_en: ...a complete dinner service...

defs.def_en: If something is complete, it contains all the parts that it should contain.

ext.ext_cn: 小孩要到两三岁才会长齐20颗乳牙。
ext.ext_en: Children don't complete their set of 20 baby teeth until they are two to three years old.

ext.ext_cn: 集全一整套所需的贴纸
ext.ext_en: ...the stickers needed to complete the collection.

defs.def_en: To complete a set or group means to provide the last item that is needed to make it a full set or group.

ext.ext_cn: 《威廉·莎士比亚全集》
ext.ext_en: ...the Complete Works of William Shakespeare.

defs.def_en: The complete works of a writer are all their books or poems published together in one book or as a set of books.

ext.ext_cn: 这个日记本配有一支金色的圆珠笔。
ext.ext_en: The diary comes complete with a gold-coloured ballpoint pen.

defs.def_en: If one thing comes complete with another, it has that thing as an extra or additional part.

ext.ext_cn: 修复农舍的工作已经完成。
ext.ext_en: The work of restoring the farmhouse is complete...

ext.ext_cn: 这个过程需要两年才能完成。
ext.ext_en: It'll be two years before the process is complete.

defs.def_en: If something is complete, it has been finished.

ext.ext_cn: 彼得·梅尔刚刚完成他的第一部小说。
ext.ext_en: Peter Mayle has just completed his first novel.

ext.ext_cn: 为了让各个体育场按时完工进行的匆忙赶工
ext.ext_en: ...the rush to get the stadiums completed on time.

defs.def_en: If you complete something, you finish doing, making, or producing it.

ext.ext_cn: 她用两年的时间修完了课程，拿到了学位。
ext.ext_en: She completed her degree in two years...

ext.ext_cn: 这本书耗时多年才写完。
ext.ext_en: This book took years to complete.

defs.def_en: If you complete something, you do all of it.

ext.ext_cn: 填写下面的订货单即可。
ext.ext_en: Simply complete the coupon below...

ext.ext_cn: 我们让候选人填写一份心理测试问卷。
ext.ext_en: We ask candidates to complete a psychometric questionnaire...

defs.def_en: If you complete a form or questionnaire, you write the answers or information asked for in it.

ext.ext_cn: 他是一名全能的记者。
ext.ext_en: He was the complete all-round journalist.

defs.def_en: You can use complete to emphasize that someone is skilled at all aspects of a particular activity and is therefore the best example of that kind of person.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 恩爱缠绵的；卿卿我我的

ext.ext_cn: 我的朋友不是卿卿我我的情侣，就是狂野的单身女郎。
ext.ext_en: All my friends were either lovey-dovey couples or wild, single girls.

defs.def_en: You can use lovey-dovey to describe, in a humorous or slightly disapproving way, lovers who show their affection for each other very openly.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他的表演非常出色，但他却很谦虚。
ext.ext_en: He gave a great performance, but he was very humble...

ext.ext_cn: 安迪是个谦逊而且彬彬有礼的绅士。
ext.ext_en: Andy was a humble, courteous and gentle man.

defs.def_en: A humble person is not proud and does not believe that they are better than other people.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 斯皮罗斯·拉齐斯的第一份职业是爱琴海上一名地位卑贱的渔夫。
ext.ext_en: Spyros Latsis started his career as a humble fisherman in the Aegean...

ext.ext_cn: 他出生在一个地位相当低下的贫穷家庭。
ext.ext_en: He came from a fairly humble, poor background.

defs.def_en: People with low social status are sometimes described as humble.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 粗陋的;简陋的;不起眼的

ext.ext_cn: 专门做这些菜的餐馆既有毫不起眼的也有价格昂贵的。
ext.ext_en: There are restaurants, both humble and expensive, that specialize in them...

ext.ext_cn: 瓦恩德尔用一狭条普通的厨房用箔纸自制了反光板来拍摄这些照片。
ext.ext_en: Varndell made his own reflector for these shots from a strip of humble kitchen foil.

defs.def_en: A humble place or thing is ordinary and not special in any way.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 依拙见，这可能是英国最好的牛排馆。
ext.ext_en: It is, in my humble opinion, perhaps the best steak restaurant in Great Britain.

defs.def_en: People use humble in a phrase such as in my humble opinion as a polite way of emphasizing what they think, even though they do not feel humble about it.

ext.ext_cn: 安森被迫认错并公开向她道歉。
ext.ext_en: Anson was forced to eat humble pie and publicly apologise to her.

defs.def_en: If you eat humble pie, you speak or behave in a way which tells people that you admit you were wrong about something.

ext.ext_cn: 本田在20世纪80年代作为一家轻易挫败行业巨头的小汽车公司而声名鹊起。
ext.ext_en: Honda won fame in the 1980s as the little car company that humbled the industry giants...

ext.ext_cn: 排名第三的巴尼特队以0–3的比分在克鲁遭遇惨败。
ext.ext_en: Third-placed Barnet were humbled 3-0 at Crewe.

defs.def_en: If you humble someone who is more important or powerful than you, you defeat them easily.

defs.def_cn: 使谦逊;使感到卑微;羞辱

ext.ext_cn: 特德的话让我感到自惭。
ext.ext_en: Ted's words humbled me...

ext.ext_cn: 我相信数百万观众看了这个故事后都会感到自己的渺小。
ext.ext_en: I am sure millions of viewers were humbled by this story.

defs.def_en: If something or someone humbles you, they make you realize that you are not as important or good as you thought you were.

defs.def_cn: 农牧神（长着羊腿羊角人身的神话人物）
defs.def_en: A faun is an imaginary creature which is like a man with goat's legs and horns.

defs.def_cn: (表示强调)奇怪地，异常地，不可思议地

ext.ext_cn: 很奇怪，赛跑直到晚上 8 点 15 分才开始。
ext.ext_en: Strangely, the race didn't start until 8.15pm...

ext.ext_cn: 不，说来也怪，事情不是这样的。
ext.ext_en: No, strangely enough, this is not the case.

defs.def_en: See also:strange;You use strangely to emphasize that what you are saying is surprising.
A parade ground is an area of ground where soldiers practise marching and have parades.
A bacillus is any bacterium that has a long, thin shape.

ext.ext_cn: 成车的食物、毯子与其他必需品抵达了该市。
ext.ext_en: Truckloads of food, blankets, and other necessities reached the city.

defs.def_en: A truckload of goods or people is the amount of them that a truck can carry.

defs.def_cn: 意志移物；念力；心灵致动
defs.def_en: Psychokinesis is the ability, which some people believe exists, to move objects using the power of your mind.
A poof is a homosexual man.

defs.def_cn: （表示某事突然发生）噗的一声

ext.ext_cn: 他们走近、拥抱，然后噗的一下就在一道炫目的光亮中消失了。
ext.ext_en: They approach, embrace, and poof! they disappear in a blinding flash of light.

defs.def_en: Some people say poof to indicate that something happened very suddenly.
Kerosene is a clear, strong-smelling liquid which is used as a fuel, for example in heaters and lamps.
A melon is a large fruit which is sweet and juicy inside and has a hard green or yellow skin.

ext.ext_cn: 她离开桌子，站在了那两个男人之间。
ext.ext_en: She left the table to stand between the two men...

ext.ext_cn: 查利从车流中间穿过，到了街对面。
ext.ext_en: Charlie crossed between the traffic to the far side of the street.

defs.def_en: If something is between two things or is in between them, it has one of the things on one side of it and the other thing on the other side.

ext.ext_cn: 八十年代初，我有很多时间穿梭于伦敦和布拉德福德之间。
ext.ext_en: I spent a lot of time in the early Eighties travelling between London and Bradford.

defs.def_en: If people or things travel between two places, they travel regularly from one place to the other and back again.

defs.def_cn: 在（两个人、群体或事物）之间

ext.ext_cn: 我认为医患关系变得越来越缺乏人情味。
ext.ext_en: I think the relationship between patients and doctors has got a lot less personal...

ext.ext_cn: 近几天，双方政府一直在进行紧张的磋商。
ext.ext_en: There have been intensive discussions between the two governments in recent days...

defs.def_en: A relationship, discussion, or difference between two people, groups, or things is one that involves them both or relates to them both.

ext.ext_cn: 他的责任感经常让他无法好好享受生活。
ext.ext_en: His sense of duty often stood between him and the enjoyment of life.

defs.def_en: If something stands between you and what you want, it prevents you from having it.

ext.ext_cn: 步行15至20分钟，增加一下你的运动时间。
ext.ext_en: Increase the amount of time you spend exercising by walking between 15 and 20 minutes...

ext.ext_cn: 阿姆斯特丹非常有趣——它有1/3的人口年龄介于18到30岁之间。
ext.ext_en: Amsterdam is fun — a third of its population is aged between 18 and 30.

defs.def_en: If something is between two amounts or ages, it is greater or older than the first one and smaller or younger than the second one.

ext.ext_cn: 运河开凿于1793到1797年间。
ext.ext_en: The canal was built between 1793 and 1797...

ext.ext_cn: 在两次世界大战之间，柏林生活的优裕是众所周知的。
ext.ext_en: Berlin was well known for its good living in between the two world wars.

defs.def_en: If something happens between or in between two times or events, it happens after the first time or event and before the second one.

ext.ext_cn: 学生可以在英语、法语和俄语中间选择一门作为第一外语。
ext.ext_en: Students will be able to choose between English, French and Russian as their first foreign language.

defs.def_en: If you must choose between two or more things, you must choose just one of them.

ext.ext_cn: 这三处共雇用了12,500名员工。
ext.ext_en: The three sites employ 12,500 people between them...

ext.ext_cn: 他们在兰伯恩总共驯了五十多匹马。
ext.ext_en: Between them, they train over fifty horses in Lambourn.

defs.def_en: If people or places have a particular amount of something between them, this is the total amount that they have.

ext.ext_cn: 他的公司被霍格·鲁宾逊公司以350万英镑的价格收购，分给了五位合伙人。
ext.ext_en: His company was bought out by Hogg Robinson for £3.5m, divided between five partners...

ext.ext_cn: 八间卧室共用一间浴室。
ext.ext_en: There is only one bathroom shared between eight bedrooms.

defs.def_en: When something is divided or shared between people, they each have a share of it.

defs.def_cn: 你我之间（的秘密）；只限于你我之间；我俩私下说说

ext.ext_cn: 不过你我之间说说，这事儿办得真不怎么样。
ext.ext_en: Between you and me, though, it's been awful for business...

ext.ext_cn: 我们私下说说，我知道他想娶她。
ext.ext_en: Between ourselves, I know he wants to marry her.

defs.def_en: When you introduce a statement by saying 'between you and me' or 'between ourselves', you are indicating that you do not want anyone else to know what you are saying.

ext.ext_cn: 这家公司聘有 6 名全职员工和1名兼职工。
ext.ext_en: The company employs six full-timers and one part-time worker.

defs.def_en: A full-timer is someone who works full-time.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 英勇的中士冒着生命危险从熊熊燃烧着的拖网渔船上救出了29名渔民。
ext.ext_en: The heroic sergeant risked his life to rescue 29 fishermen from their blazing trawler...

ext.ext_cn: 他的英雄事迹在印度广为传颂。
ext.ext_en: His heroic deeds were celebrated in every corner of India.

defs.def_en: If you describe a person or their actions as heroic, you admire them because they show extreme bravery.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 矢志不渝的;艰苦卓绝的

ext.ext_cn: 公司在降低成本方面付出了艰苦卓绝的努力。
ext.ext_en: The company has made heroic efforts at cost reduction...

ext.ext_cn: 他在这场艰苦比赛的最后一局中踉跄结束。
ext.ext_en: He finally faltered in the last game of a heroic match...

defs.def_en: If you describe an action or event as heroic, you admire it because it involves great effort or determination to succeed.

ext.ext_cn: 书中的中心主角人物
ext.ext_en: ...the book's central, heroic figure.

defs.def_en: Heroic means being or relating to the hero of a story.

defs.def_cn: 英雄壮举;英勇果断的行为

ext.ext_cn: 以空中的英雄壮举拯救了直升机飞行员的人
ext.ext_en: ...the man whose aerial heroics helped save the helicopter pilot...

ext.ext_cn: 英格兰队此刻需要队长采取英勇果断的行为。
ext.ext_en: England need heroics from the captain now.

defs.def_en: Heroics are actions involving bravery, courage, or determination.

ext.ext_cn: 他说自己的建议是：“不要逞英雄，要遵纪守法。”
ext.ext_en: He said his advice was: 'No heroics, stay within the law'...

ext.ext_cn: 住手吧，佩里。你已经逞过英雄了。现在一切都结束了。
ext.ext_en: Cut it out, Perry. You've performed your heroics. It's all over now.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone's actions or plans as heroics, you think that they are foolish or dangerous because they are too difficult or brave for the situation in which they occur.

ext.ext_cn: 排名未有变化。
ext.ext_en: The placings remained unaltered...

ext.ext_cn: 北安普敦在联赛中名列第三。
ext.ext_en: Northampton were third in the League placings.

defs.def_en: The placings in a competition are the relative positions of the competitors at the end or at a particular stage of the competition.

defs.def_cn: 情有可原的;可减轻处罚的

ext.ext_cn: 被告方决定认罪，但是坚称有从轻情节。
ext.ext_en: The defendants decide to admit their guilt, but insist that there are extenuating circumstances.

defs.def_en: If you say that there are extenuating circumstances for a bad situation or wrong action, you mean that there are reasons or factors which partly excuse it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 对不起,我太不小心了。
ext.ext_en: I'm sorry. How careless of me...

ext.ext_cn: 有些当妈妈的花钱有点随意。
ext.ext_en: Some mothers were a bit careless with money...

defs.def_en: If you are careless, you do not pay enough attention to what you are doing, and so you make mistakes, or cause harm or damage.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 当同事身处危险时他表现英勇，不顾个人安危。
ext.ext_en: He had shown himself careless of personal safety where the life of his colleagues might be at risk...

ext.ext_cn: 她不注意个人卫生。
ext.ext_en: She's careless about her hygiene...

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is careless of something such as their health or appearance, you mean that they do not seem to be concerned about it, or do nothing to keep it in a good condition.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他手腕轻轻一抖,球就飞出去了。
ext.ext_en: With a careless flip of his wrists, he sent the ball quickly on its way.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone's movements as careless, you mean that they are relaxed or confident, and do not seem to require much effort or thought.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 浇上特别辛辣的调料的脆口什锦色拉
ext.ext_en: ...a crisp mixed salad with an unusually piquant dressing.

defs.def_en: Food that is piquant has a pleasantly spicy taste.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 引人入胜的；刺激有趣的

ext.ext_cn: 她的书问世时可能确有引人入胜的新颖之处。
ext.ext_en: There may well have been a piquant novelty about her books when they came out.

defs.def_en: Something that is piquant is interesting and exciting.

ext.ext_cn: 一种新的绝缘层压材料刚由阿特沃特父子公司设计推出。
ext.ext_en: A new insulating laminate has just been designed by Attwater and Sons...

ext.ext_cn: 可生产厚层压板而不会产生裂痕。
ext.ext_en: Thick sections of the laminate can be produced without the risk of cracking.

defs.def_en: A laminate is a tough material that is made by sticking together two or more layers of a particular substance.

ext.ext_cn: 哈莱姆最著名的夜总会，棉花俱乐部
ext.ext_en: ...Harlem's most famous nightspot, the Cotton Club.

defs.def_en: A nightspot is a nightclub.

ext.ext_cn: 风暴造成整个华盛顿地区电力供应中断。
ext.ext_en: A windstorm in Washington is causing power outages throughout the region.

defs.def_en: An outage is a period of time when the electricity supply to a building or area is interrupted, for example because of damage to the cables.
An aristocrat is someone whose family has a high social rank, especially someone who has a title.

ext.ext_cn: 不锈钢是有可能和普通钢焊接在一起的。
ext.ext_en: It's possible to weld stainless steel to ordinary steel...

ext.ext_cn: 它们也可用于工厂车间，用来焊接物体。
ext.ext_en: They will also be used on factory floors to weld things together...

defs.def_en: To weld one piece of metal to another means to join them by heating the edges and putting them together so that they cool and harden into one piece.

ext.ext_cn: 团结全党所需的权威和个人魅力她两者兼具。

defs.def_cn: (用于代替任何字符或字符串的)通配符

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: He took a bunch of keys from the pocket of his old corduroy trousers.

ext.ext_cn: 一把旧牙刷
ext.ext_en: ...an old toothbrush.

defs.def_en: Something that is old is no longer in good condition because of its age or because it has been used a lot.

ext.ext_en: Although the old secret police have been abolished, the military police still exist...

defs.def_en: You use old to refer to something that is no longer used, that no longer exists, or that has been replaced by something else.

defs.def_cn: 原来（属于自己）的；原先（生活中）的

ext.ext_en: I'll make up the bed in your old room...

defs.def_en: You use old to refer to something that used to belong to you, or to a person or thing that used to have a particular role in your life.

ext.ext_en: Mr Brownson, I assure you King's an old enemy of mine...

ext.ext_en: Are you all right, old chap?...

ext.ext_cn: 好心肠的老伯根会帮他这个忙的。
ext.ext_en: Good old Bergen would do him the favor.

defs.def_en: You can use old to express affection when talking to or about someone you know.

defs.def_cn: 随便哪个/不是随便哪个

ext.ext_en: Any old paper will do...

ext.ext_en: The portraits and sumptuous ornaments, and the gold clock, show that this is not just any old front room.

defs.def_en: You use any old to emphasize that the quality or type of something is not important. If you say that a particular thing is not any old thing, you are emphasizing how special or famous it is.

ext.ext_cn: 以前，兽医大概每年来我们这里出诊一次。
ext.ext_en: In the old days we got a visit from the vet maybe once a year.

defs.def_en: In the old days means in the past, before things changed.

defs.def_cn: 往昔的好日子；过去的好时光

ext.ext_cn: 他还记得村里人互相熟识、可以夜不闭户的美好往昔。
ext.ext_en: He remembers the good old days when everyone in his village knew him and you could leave your door open at night.

defs.def_en: When people refer to the good old days, they are referring to a time in the past when they think that life was better than it is now.

ext.ext_cn: 旧时骁勇善战的骑士
ext.ext_en: ...the warrior knights of old.

ext.ext_cn: 重现古时舍伍德森林的工程
ext.ext_en: ...a programme of work to recreate the Sherwood Forest of old.

defs.def_en: If you talk about people or things of old, you are referring to people or things that existed long ago but which no longer exist, or no longer exist in the same form.

ext.ext_cn: 他已断然否认曾对拉比的行为进行过诋毁。
ext.ext_en: He has flatly denied casting aspersions on the rabbi's behaviour.

defs.def_en: If you cast aspersions on someone or something, you suggest that they are not very good in some way.

ext.ext_cn: 一件黑色短款收腰皮夹克
ext.ext_en: ...a black leather bomber jacket.

defs.def_en: A bomber jacket is a short jacket which is gathered into a band at the waist or hips.

defs.def_cn: (用于名词前构成名词)表示“小型的”，“微型的”

ext.ext_en: Provisions may be purchased from the mini-market...

ext.ext_cn: 我们在打迷你高尔夫。
ext.ext_en: We were playing mini-golf.

defs.def_en: Mini- is used before nouns to form nouns which refer to something which is a smaller version of something else.

ext.ext_en: The yacht now lies in a boatyard at Lymington.

ext.ext_en: He was just lying there completely pissed.

defs.def_en: Someone who is pissed is drunk.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: You know Molly's pissed at you.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is pissed, you mean that they are annoyed.

defs.def_cn: 字节（计算机存储单位，约等于一个印刷字符）

ext.ext_cn: 200万字节的数据
ext.ext_en: ...two million bytes of data.

defs.def_en: In computing, a byte is a unit of storage approximately equivalent to one printed character.

ext.ext_cn: 这是艾弗·罗伯茨-琼斯的作品，他还创作了议会广场上的丘吉尔塑像。
ext.ext_en: It is the work of Ivor Roberts-Jones, who also produced the statue of Churchill in Parliament Square...

ext.ext_cn: 他是个曾患贫血症的哮喘患者。
ext.ext_en: He is an asthmatic who was also anaemic...

defs.def_en: You can use also to give more information about a person or thing, or to add another relevant fact.

ext.ext_cn: 他的父亲，也是位高级军官，在战争中牺牲了。
ext.ext_en: His father, also a top-ranking officer, had perished during the war...

ext.ext_cn: 我们一直很努力工作，并且我们的家人也是如此。
ext.ext_en: We have been working very hard, and our families have also worked hard...

defs.def_en: You can use also to indicate that something you have just said about one person or thing is true of another person or thing.

ext.ext_cn: 虽然知道他的人不多，但他在这些人中名声却很响。
ext.ext_en: Although he is known to only a few, his reputation among them is very great...

ext.ext_cn: 虽然枪战目前已停止，但造成的破坏是巨大的。
ext.ext_en: Although the shooting has stopped for now, the destruction left behind is enormous.

defs.def_en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement which contrasts with the statement in the main clause.

defs.def_cn: 虽然（表示惊奇或出乎意料）

ext.ext_cn: 虽然那时我只有6岁，我依然记得在电视上见过它。
ext.ext_en: Although I was only six, I can remember seeing it on TV...

ext.ext_cn: 虽然他的年纪是我们的两倍，但他却成为了公司的灵魂人物。
ext.ext_en: Although he was twice as old as us, he became the life and soul of the company.

defs.def_en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement which makes the main clause of the sentence seem surprising or unexpected.

ext.ext_cn: 他爱着她，虽然他没有将其称为爱。
ext.ext_en: He was in love with her, although he did not put that name to it.

defs.def_en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which gives some information that is relevant to the main clause but modifies the strength of that statement.

defs.def_cn: 尽管;虽然（表示承认所述是事实）

ext.ext_cn: 尽管价格昂贵，但它们经久耐用，永不过时。
ext.ext_en: Although they're expensive, they last forever and never go out of style...

ext.ext_cn: 这种态度虽然不够理想，但还不至于消极透顶。
ext.ext_en: Although not ideal, this attitude is not entirely destructive.

defs.def_en: You use although when admitting a fact about something which you regard as less important than a contrasting fact.

ext.ext_cn: 他说话没个轻重，得罪了许多人。
ext.ext_en: He had alienated many people with his tactless remarks.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as tactless, you think what they say or do is likely to offend other people.

defs.def_en: You use -day with a number to indicate how long something lasts.

defs.def_en: A speaker or writer uses your to indicate that something belongs or relates to the person or people that they are talking or writing to.

defs.def_en: In spoken English and informal written English, your is sometimes used to indicate that something belongs to or relates to people in general.

ext.ext_cn: 她直奔西蒙的房间，敲了敲门。

defs.def_en: If you knock on something such as a door or window, you hit it, usually several times, to attract someone's attention.

defs.def_cn: 碰，撞；（尤指）碰倒，撞倒，敲动

ext.ext_en: She accidentally knocked the tea tin off the shelf...

ext.ext_en: The baby was knocked from his father's arms...

defs.def_en: If you knock something, you touch or hit it roughly, especially so that it falls or moves.

ext.ext_en: They decided to knock the two rooms into one...

ext.ext_en: The spacious kitchen was achieved by knocking together three small rooms.

defs.def_en: If someone knocks two rooms or buildings into one, or knocks them together, they make them form one room or building by removing a wall.

ext.ext_en: The third wave was so strong it knocked me backwards...

ext.ext_en: They were knocked to the ground and robbed of their wallets...

defs.def_en: To knock someone into a particular position or condition means to hit them very hard so that they fall over or become unconscious.

defs.def_cn: 使失去（某种品质或特征）

defs.def_en: To knock a particular quality or characteristic out of someone means to make them lose it.

ext.ext_en: What they said was a real knock to my self-confidence...

ext.ext_en: The art market has suffered some severe knocks during the past two years.

ext.ext_en: The King made major concessions to end the confrontation with his people.

ext.ext_en: The government has granted concessions to three private telephone companies.

ext.ext_cn: 唐纳德，有些事还是不说为好。

defs.def_en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

ext.ext_cn: 那个消息给了投资者信心。
ext.ext_en: Investors were encouraged by the news...

ext.ext_en: We want to encourage people to go fishing, not put them off...

ext.ext_cn: 促进细胞生长的天然物质
ext.ext_en: ...a natural substance that encourages cell growth...

ext.ext_cn: 如此保密的做法滋生并加剧了人们的恐惧和疑虑。
ext.ext_en: Such secrecy breeds and encourages fear and suspicion...

ext.ext_cn: 关于发情的母狗和牡鹿的笑话

ext.ext_en: The officer cited the federation's rule on affiliation.

defs.def_en: If one group has an affiliation with another group, it has a close or official connection with it.

defs.def_cn: （个人之间或个人与组织之间的）联系，从属关系

ext.ext_cn: 约翰逊就职于耐克鞋业公司
ext.ext_en: ...Johnson's affiliation with shoe company Nike...

ext.ext_cn: 他们询问她属于哪个政党。
ext.ext_en: They asked what her political affiliations were.

defs.def_en: If you have an affiliation with a group or another person, you have a close or official connection with them.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (建筑、家具等)现代化的，摩登的

ext.ext_cn: 作为城市办公楼的现代化大楼
ext.ext_en: ...the modernistic building that housed the city offices.

defs.def_en: A modernistic building or piece of furniture looks very modern.

ext.ext_cn: 各种财政计划的计算机打印资料
ext.ext_en: ...a computer printout of various financial projections.

defs.def_en: A printout is a piece of paper on which information from a computer or similar device has been printed.
An emanation is a form of energy or a mass of tiny particles that comes from something.

ext.ext_cn: 红桃A
ext.ext_en: ...the ace of hearts.

defs.def_en: An ace is a playing card with a single symbol on it. In most card games, the ace of a particular suit has either the highest or the lowest value of the cards in that suit.

defs.def_cn: （在运动等方面）成绩超群的人，佼佼者

ext.ext_cn: 前一流赛车手斯特林·莫斯
ext.ext_en: ...former motor-racing ace Stirling Moss.

ext.ext_cn: 王牌恐怖片制片人劳伦斯·伍尔西
ext.ext_en: ...ace horror-film producer Lawrence Woolsey.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone such as a sports player as an ace, you mean that they are very good at what they do.

ext.ext_cn: 精彩绝伦的电影
ext.ext_en: ...a really ace film.

defs.def_en: If you say that something is ace, you think that it is good and you like it a lot.

ext.ext_cn: 这位美国选手在该盘首局有三次发球直得。
ext.ext_en: The American served three aces in the opening game of the set.

defs.def_en: In tennis, an ace is a serve which is so fast that the other player cannot reach the ball.

defs.def_cn: 占绝对优势；占尽天时地利人和

ext.ext_cn: “当我还是个毛头小伙儿时，”一个31岁的男人说，“我觉得完全是女孩子说了算。”
ext.ext_en: 'When I was an adolescent,' says a thirty-one-year-old man, 'I thought girls held all the aces.'

defs.def_en: If you say that someone holds all the aces, you mean that they have all the advantages in a contest or situation.

defs.def_cn: 秘藏的王牌;应急的绝招;锦囊妙计

ext.ext_cn: 我们超众的技术是我们的法宝。
ext.ext_en: Our superior technology is our ace in the hole.

defs.def_en: Something that is an ace in the hole is an advantage which you have over an opponent or rival, and which you can use if necessary.

ext.ext_cn: 他一心想杀人并且差点就得逞了。
ext.ext_en: He was intent on murder and he came within an ace of succeeding.

defs.def_en: If you come within an ace of doing something, or you are within an ace of doing something, you very nearly do or experience it.

defs.def_cn: 繁缕，卷耳(开白色小花，贴地生长)
defs.def_en: Chickweed is a plant with small leaves and white flowers which grows close to the ground.

defs.def_cn: 把…和…作比较;把…对照…来看

ext.ext_cn: 和她在许多其他方面的专业知识相比，这些相对来说都不算什么。
ext.ext_en: These are relatively small points when set against her expertise on so many other issues...

ext.ext_cn: 在当时 5,000 英镑是相当大的一笔数目，特别是和最高工资相比。
ext.ext_en: £5,000 was a considerable sum in those days and particularly when set against the maximum wage.

defs.def_en: If one argument or fact is set against another, it is considered in relation to it.

ext.ext_cn: 这件事使得村里邻里间反目成仇。
ext.ext_en: The case has set neighbour against neighbour in the village.

defs.def_en: To set one person against another means to cause them to become enemies or rivals.

ext.ext_cn: 两片黑麦面包
ext.ext_en: ...two slices of rye bread.

defs.def_en: Rye bread is brown bread made with rye flour.

ext.ext_cn: 他们无力支付这些账单。
ext.ext_en: They couldn't afford to pay the bills...

ext.ext_cn: 他立即支付了订报费。
ext.ext_en: He paid his bill for the newspapers promptly.

defs.def_en: A bill is a written statement of money that you owe for goods or services.  →see usage note at:account

ext.ext_cn: 你们会给我开这个的账单吗？
ext.ext_en: Are you going to bill me for this?

defs.def_en: If you bill someone for goods or services you have provided them with, you give or send them a bill stating how much money they owe you for these goods or services.
The bill in a restaurant is a piece of paper on which the price of the meal you have just eaten is written and which you are given before you pay.

ext.ext_cn: 大量的美钞
ext.ext_en: ...a large quantity of US dollar bills.

defs.def_en: A bill is a piece of paper money.

ext.ext_cn: 这是十年来国会通过的最严厉的一项刑事法案。
ext.ext_en: This is the toughest crime bill that Congress has passed in a decade...

ext.ext_cn: 这项法案得到了绝大多数人的支持。
ext.ext_en: The bill was approved by a large majority.

defs.def_en: In government, a bill is a formal statement of a proposed new law that is discussed and then voted on.
The bill of a show or concert is a list of the entertainers who will take part in it.

ext.ext_cn: 海报宣传她会扮演《白雪公主》中的“红王后”。
ext.ext_en: She was billed to play the Red Queen in Snow White.

defs.def_en: If someone is billed to appear in a particular show, it has been advertised that they are going to be in it.

defs.def_cn: 宣传（某人或某物有某种特质或能力）

ext.ext_cn: 他们宣称它是英国最有趣的博物馆。
ext.ext_en: They bill it as Britain's most exciting museum.

defs.def_en: If you bill a person or event as a particular thing, you advertise them in a way that makes people think they have particular qualities or abilities.
A bird's bill is its beak.

ext.ext_cn: 如果你符合要求，就寄一份简历给丽贝卡·里斯。
ext.ext_en: If you fit the bill, send a CV to Rebecca Rees.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone or something fits the bill or fills the bill, you mean that they are suitable for a particular job or purpose.

ext.ext_cn: 谁会为她奢侈的假日买单？
ext.ext_en: Who is footing the bill for her extravagant holiday?

defs.def_en: If you have to foot the bill for something, you have to pay for it.

ext.ext_cn: 巴黎的医生们告诉75岁的密特朗总统，他的身体非常健康。
ext.ext_en: President Mitterrand, 75, has been given a clean bill of health by doctors in Paris.

defs.def_en: If a doctor gives you a clean bill of health, they tell you that you are fit and healthy.

ext.ext_cn: 双下巴
ext.ext_en: ...a double chin...

ext.ext_cn: 他揉搓着下巴上灰白的胡茬。
ext.ext_en: He rubbed the gray stubble on his chin.

defs.def_en: Your chin is the part of your face that is below your mouth and above your neck.

defs.def_cn: 坦然面对，欣然接受(令人不快或困难的局面)

ext.ext_cn: 警察赶来时，他坦然为自己给他们造成的麻烦表示歉意。
ext.ext_en: When the police arrived he took it on the chin and apologised for the trouble he'd caused them.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone took something on the chin, you mean that they accepted an unpleasant or difficult situation bravely and without making a lot of fuss about it.

ext.ext_cn: 我刚买了栋新房子。
ext.ext_en: I've just bought a new house...

ext.ext_cn: 这两个人只不过才刚刚认识。
ext.ext_en: The two had only just met...

defs.def_en: You use just to say that something happened a very short time ago, or is starting to happen at the present time. For example, if you say that someone has just arrived, you mean that they arrived a very short time ago.

ext.ext_cn: 我正在弄花椰菜的调味汁呢。
ext.ext_en: I'm just making the sauce for the cauliflower...

ext.ext_cn: 我正打算沿这条小巷往南走，去寄几封信。
ext.ext_en: I'm  just going to walk down the lane now and post some letters...

defs.def_en: If you say that you are just doing something, you mean that you are doing it now and will finish it very soon. If you say that you are just about to do something, or just going to do it, you mean that you will do it very soon.

defs.def_cn: （用于强调）正，就，恰恰（在某个时刻）

ext.ext_cn: 兰德尔这个时候应该正在拿周日的报纸。
ext.ext_en: Randall would just now be getting the Sunday paper...

ext.ext_cn: 正在那时，电话响了。
ext.ext_en: Just then the phone rang...

defs.def_en: You can use just to emphasize that something is happening at exactly the moment of speaking or at exactly the moment that you are talking about.

defs.def_cn: （尤用于纠正错误的观点）只是，仅仅是

ext.ext_cn: 这只是个建议。
ext.ext_en: It's just a suggestion...

ext.ext_cn: 这不仅仅是资金的问题。
ext.ext_en: It's not just a financial matter...

defs.def_en: You use just to indicate that something is no more important, interesting, or difficult, for example, than you say it is, especially when you want to correct a wrong idea that someone may get or has already got.

defs.def_cn: （用于强调所谈的只是一小部分而非全部）仅仅是，只不过是

ext.ext_cn: 这只不过是你可以做的各种试验中的一例罢了。
ext.ext_en: That's just one example of the kind of experiments you can do...

ext.ext_cn: 这些只不过是众多可能的选择中的几个。
ext.ext_en: These are just a few of the many options available.

defs.def_en: You use just to emphasize that you are talking about a small part, not the whole of an amount.

defs.def_cn: （用于强调数量少或时间短）只是，仅仅

ext.ext_cn: 斯蒂法妮和戴维仅仅花了3天就把一个房间装饰一新。
ext.ext_en: Stephanie and David redecorated a room in just three days...

ext.ext_cn: 记住，他才14岁。
ext.ext_en: Remember he's just fourteen years old.

defs.def_en: You use just to emphasize how small an amount is or how short a length of time is.

defs.def_cn: （用于动词前表示事情的结果糟糕，很可能导致局面恶化）只（会），只不过

ext.ext_cn: 像我那样一走了之只会让事情变得更糟。
ext.ext_en: Leaving like I did just made it worse...

ext.ext_cn: 他们只是伤害了他们社区的居民，并没有真正解决任何问题。
ext.ext_en: They just hurt the people in their community, they didn't really solve any problem.

defs.def_en: You can use just in front of a verb to indicate that the result of something is unfortunate or undesirable and is likely to make the situation worse rather than better.

defs.def_cn: （用于表示情况在很小的程度上属实）刚刚，勉强，差一点就不

ext.ext_cn: 借着起居室的灯光，勉强能看见她的手。
ext.ext_en: Her hand was just visible by the light from the sitting room...

ext.ext_cn: 那是科林的声音，勉强能听得见。
ext.ext_en: It was Colin's voice, only just audible...

defs.def_en: You use just to indicate that what you are saying is the case, but only by a very small degree or amount.

defs.def_cn: （与might，may和could连用，表示稍有可能）可能，也许

ext.ext_cn: 这是个老掉牙的把戏了，不过也许会有用。
ext.ext_en: It's an old trick but it just might work...

ext.ext_cn: 那也许有可能。
ext.ext_en: It may just be possible.

defs.def_en: You use just with 'might,' 'may,' and 'could', when you mean that there is a small chance of something happening, even though it is not very likely.

defs.def_cn: （用于加强语气，表示生气、赞美、肯定等）硬是，就是，简直

ext.ext_cn: 她就是放松不下来。
ext.ext_en: She just won't relax...

ext.ext_cn: 我知道你会在这儿的。我就是知道。
ext.ext_en: I knew you'd be here. I just knew...

defs.def_en: You use just to emphasize the following word or phrase, in order to express feelings such as annoyance, admiration, or certainty.

defs.def_cn: （用于指示、礼貌的请求或表示意图的陈述，用来弱化语气）请，只要，只管…就好了

ext.ext_cn: 能否请您向我们描述一下您的猫？
ext.ext_en: Could you just give us a description of your cat?...

ext.ext_cn: 你把桌子抬起来一下好吗？
ext.ext_en: Can you just lift the table for a second?...

defs.def_en: You use just with instructions, polite requests, or statements of intention, to make your request or statement seem less difficult.

ext.ext_cn: “让我进来，迪。”——“好的。稍等一下。”
ext.ext_en: 'Let me in, Di.' — 'Okay. Just a minute.'

defs.def_en: You use just in expressions such as just a minute and just a moment to ask someone to wait for a short time.

defs.def_cn: （用于打断某人，以表示不同意、解释某事或让其保持冷静）稍等一下，且慢

ext.ext_cn: 嗯，且慢，我并不完全同意这个前提。
ext.ext_en: Well, now just a second, I don't altogether agree with the premise.

defs.def_en: You can use just in expressions such as just a minute and just a moment to interrupt someone, for example in order to disagree with them, explain something, or calm them down.

defs.def_cn: （用于否定附加问句，表示完全赞同）难道不是吗，确实如此

ext.ext_cn: “那简直是疯了，”我说。“谁说不是呢？”他说。
ext.ext_en: 'That's crazy,' I said. 'Isn't it just?' he said...

ext.ext_cn: “经理将要作一些非常艰难的决定。”——“确实如此。”
ext.ext_en: 'The manager's going to have some tough decisions to make.' — 'Won't he just.'

defs.def_en: You can use just with negative question tags, for example 'isn't he just?' and 'don't they just!', to say that you agree completely with what has been said.

defs.def_cn: （表示完全可以想象）完全，简直

ext.ext_cn: 要是我们开始凑在一起交头接耳，我简直能想象到你那种令人讨厌的怀疑的目光了。
ext.ext_en: I can just see the nasty suspicious looks I'd be getting from you if we started whispering together...

ext.ext_cn: 我简直能听到她和她的朋友们说，“哎呀，都是他妈妈的错！”
ext.ext_en: I can just hear her telling her friends, 'Well, I blame his mother!'

defs.def_en: If you say that you can just see or hear something, you mean that it is easy for you to imagine seeing or hearing it.

ext.ext_cn: 他为何成为社会党人的确切原因实际上还不清楚。
ext.ext_en: It is really not clear just why he became a Socialist...

ext.ext_cn: 没有统计数字表明具体将有多少人不参加投票。
ext.ext_en: There are no statistics about just how many people won't vote...

defs.def_en: You use just to mean exactly, when you are specifying something precisely or asking for precise information.

ext.ext_cn: 猕猴桃作为有益健康的零食是再好不过了。
ext.ext_en: Kiwi fruit are just the thing for a healthy snack...

ext.ext_cn: “我们找个地方喝杯咖啡吧。”——“我知道个好地方。”
ext.ext_en: 'Let's get a coffee somewhere.'—'I know just the place.'

defs.def_en: You use just to emphasize that a particular thing is exactly what is needed or fits a particular description exactly.

ext.ext_cn: 在那副外表背后，他们和我们大家是完全一样的。
ext.ext_en: Behind the facade they are just like the rest of us...

ext.ext_cn: 他和所有人一样非常努力。
ext.ext_en: He worked just as hard as anyone...

defs.def_en: You use just in expressions such as just like ,just as...as, and just the same when you are emphasizing the similarity between two things or two people.

ext.ext_cn: 有一些人认为尼克·普赖斯几乎就是世界上最优秀的高尔夫球运动员了。
ext.ext_en: There are those who believe that Nick Price is just about the best golfer in the world...

ext.ext_cn: 她看些什么书？几乎什么都看。
ext.ext_en: What does she read? Just about everything...

defs.def_en: You use just about to indicate that what you are talking about is so close to being the case that it can be regarded as being the case.

ext.ext_cn: 当时我差一点就忍受不了了。
ext.ext_en: I can just about tolerate it at the moment...

ext.ext_cn: 我们刚刚有足够的时间赶到那里。
ext.ext_en: We've got just about enough time to get there.

defs.def_en: You use just about to indicate that what you are talking about is in fact the case, but only by a very small degree or amount.

defs.def_cn: （用于表示接近于某一具体数量）几乎，差不多

ext.ext_cn: 伊夫眯着眼瞥了一下钟，看到差不多是早上7点钟。
ext.ext_en: Eve, squinting at the clock, saw it was just on 7 a.m...

ext.ext_cn: 许多都是退休的人，其中差不多有五分之一年龄在五十多岁。
ext.ext_en: Many were retired people, and just on a fifth were in their fifties.

defs.def_en: Just on is used in mentioning an almost exact number or amount.

ext.ext_cn: “她在梅费尔有个大公寓。”——“正是。”
ext.ext_en: 'She has a large flat in Mayfair.' — 'Just so.'

defs.def_en: Just so is used to agree with or confirm a statement that has been made.

ext.ext_cn: 我必须得按她的要求为她做头发。
ext.ext_en: I do her hair, and it has to be just so.

defs.def_en: If things are just so, they are done or arranged exactly as they should be or exactly as someone wants them.

defs.def_cn: （用于弱化抱怨、给出建议或理由时的语气）只不过，只是

ext.ext_cn: 很抱歉我打了你。我不是有意的，只不过我当时气极了。
ext.ext_en: I'm sorry I struck you. I didn't mean to. It's just that I was so mad...

ext.ext_cn: 你的头发挺好的；只是你需要剪剪了。
ext.ext_en: Your hair is all right; it's just that you need a haircut.

defs.def_en: You use the expression it's just that when you are making a complaint, suggestion, or excuse, so that the person you are talking to will not get annoyed with you.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 公正的；正当的；正义的；合理的

ext.ext_cn: 在一个公正的社会中，一定会有一套人们可以通过法庭寻求赔偿的体制。
ext.ext_en: In a just society there must be a system whereby people can seek redress through the courts...

ext.ext_cn: 她为了正义的事业和自由而光明正大地斗争。
ext.ext_en: She fought honestly for a just cause and for freedom...

defs.def_en: If you describe a situation, action, or idea as just, you mean that it is right or acceptable according to particular moral principles, such as respect for all human beings.

ext.ext_cn: 内斯追上小偷，按住他，一直等到警察赶到。
ext.ext_en: Ness chased the thief down and held him until police arrived...

ext.ext_cn: 狩猎是数千年中人类从事的主要活动。
ext.ext_en: For thousands of years chasing down game was the main activity in which humans were involved.

defs.def_en: If you chase someone down, you run after them or follow them quickly and catch them.

ext.ext_cn: 就是那时候，我找到了她，让她在我的乐队里担任歌手。
ext.ext_en: That's when I chased her down to be the singer in my band...

ext.ext_cn: 银行官员称，他们没有义务追踪每个贷款户的每笔资产。
ext.ext_en: Bank officials argued that it is not their job to chase down every asset of every bank debtor.

defs.def_en: If you chase someone or something down, you manage to find them after searching for them.

defs.def_cn: (教授有钱人家或上流社会年轻女孩礼仪及其他社交技能的)女子精修学校，淑女学堂

ext.ext_cn: 一所瑞士女子精修学校
ext.ext_en: ...a Swiss finishing school.

ext.ext_cn: 威尔士王妃上精修学校的地方
ext.ext_en: ...where the Princess of Wales attended finishing school.

defs.def_en: A finishing school is a private school where rich or upper-class young women are taught manners and other social skills that are considered to be suitable for them.
Philology is the study of words, especially the history and development of the words in a particular language or group of languages.

defs.def_cn: (解决长期存在的争端的)最后决战，决出胜负的较量

ext.ext_cn: 首相正准备和部长们摊牌。
ext.ext_en: The Prime Minister is preparing for a showdown with Ministers.

defs.def_en: A showdown is a big argument or conflict which is intended to settle a dispute that has lasted for a long time.

ext.ext_cn: 美国顶级公司经理人
ext.ext_en: ...top US corporate executives.

ext.ext_cn: 英国企业界
ext.ext_en: ...the UK corporate sector.

defs.def_en: Corporate means relating to business corporations or to a particular business corporation.

defs.def_cn: 患贪食症的；食欲过盛的

ext.ext_cn: 患贪食症的病人
ext.ext_en: ...bulimic patients...

ext.ext_cn: 我既有厌食症又有贪食症。
ext.ext_en: I was anorexic and bulimic.

defs.def_en: If someone is bulimic, they are suffering from bulimia.

ext.ext_cn: 在任何国家的犯罪者中，十几二十几岁的青年男性都占了很高的比例。
ext.ext_en: A high proportion of crime in any country is perpetrated by young males in their teens and twenties...

ext.ext_cn: 对最贫穷和最没有特权的人们犯下了大量罪行。
ext.ext_en: Tremendous wrongs were being perpetrated on the poorest and least privileged human beings...

defs.def_en: If someone perpetrates a crime or any other immoral or harmful act, they do it.
A bridegroom is a man who is getting married.
The windshield of a car or other vehicle is the glass window at the front through which the driver looks.

ext.ext_cn: 她咽下一大口咖啡。
ext.ext_en: She gulped down a mouthful of coffee...

ext.ext_cn: 将每一口充分咀嚼后，再吃下一口。
ext.ext_en: Chew each mouthful fully before the next bite.

defs.def_en: A mouthful of drink or food is the amount that you put or have in your mouth.

defs.def_cn: 冗长而拗口的词（或短语）;难读的词（或短语）

defs.def_en: If you are anxious to do something or anxious that something should happen, you very much want to do it or very much want it to happen.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: A friend of mine is a very anxious person.

defs.def_en: If you are anxious, you are nervous or worried about something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: The Prime Minister faces anxious hours before the votes are counted tomorrow night.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他似乎有一股近乎疯狂的劲头。
ext.ext_en: He seemed to have an almost manic energy.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as manic, you mean that they do things extremely quickly or energetically, often because they are very excited or anxious about something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: （微笑、笑声或幽默）过度的，失常的

ext.ext_cn: 傻笑
ext.ext_en: ...a manic grin.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone's smile, laughter, or sense of humour as manic, you mean that it seems excessive or strange, as if they were insane.

ext.ext_cn: 他被飞驰而来的火车头撞死了。
ext.ext_en: He was killed by an onrushing locomotive.

ext.ext_cn: 河水汹涌奔流的咆哮声
ext.ext_en: ...the roar of the onrushing water.

defs.def_en: Onrushing describes something such as a vehicle that is moving forward so quickly or forcefully that it would be very difficult to stop.

ext.ext_en: ...the moronic and insensitive interjections of the disc jockey.

defs.def_en: An interjection is something you say which interrupts someone else who is speaking.
In grammar, an interjection is a word or expression which you use to express a strong feeling such as surprise, pain, or horror.
A hyphen is the punctuation sign used to join words together to make a compound, as in 'left-handed'. People also use a hyphen to show that the rest of a word is on the next line.

ext.ext_cn: 很多雄鸟进化出鲜艳的羽毛是为了吸引雌鸟。
ext.ext_en: The bright plumage of many male birds has evolved to attract females...

ext.ext_en: Maize evolved from a wild grass in Mexico.

defs.def_en: When animals or plants evolve, they gradually change and develop into different forms.

ext.ext_cn: 最终发展成巴基斯坦国际航空公司的一家小型航空公司
ext.ext_en: ...a tiny airline which eventually evolved into Pakistan International Airlines...

ext.ext_cn: 流行音乐从民歌演变而来。
ext.ext_en: Popular music evolved from folk songs...

defs.def_en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

defs.def_cn: 不能容忍的;难以忍受的

ext.ext_cn: 他很讨厌，真令人受不了。
ext.ext_en: He was an insufferable bore.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone or something is insufferable, you are emphasizing that they are very unpleasant or annoying.

defs.def_cn: （尤指犯罪后或为逃避某人的）逃跑，逃走，离开

ext.ext_cn: 他们骑上偷来的摩托车沿着人行道逃走了。
ext.ext_en: They made their getaway along a pavement on a stolen motorcycle.

ext.ext_cn: 窃贼逃跑时所驾驶的汽车
ext.ext_en: ...the burglar's  getaway car.

defs.def_en: If someone makes a getaway, they leave a place quickly, especially after committing a crime or when trying to avoid someone.

defs.def_en: A getaway is a short holiday somewhere.

A corporate raider is a person or organization that tries to take control of a company by buying a large number of its shares.

defs.def_cn: 非正式地讨论；随便谈谈

ext.ext_cn: 他们开始讨论弄一个电铲。
ext.ext_en: They started to kick around the idea of an electric scraper.

defs.def_en: If you kick around ideas or suggestions, you discuss them informally.

ext.ext_cn: 我认为没人敢再欺负我了。
ext.ext_en: I don't feel that anyone can kick me around anymore.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone kicks you around, you do not like the way that they treat you because it is unfair.

defs.def_cn: 雪花莲(一种初春开放的小白花)

ext.ext_cn: 被剥夺了夫妻权的男子
ext.ext_en: ...a man deprived of his conjugal rights.

defs.def_en: Conjugal means relating to marriage and the relationship between a husband and wife, especially their sexual relationship.

defs.def_cn: 无线的;用无线电波传送的

ext.ext_cn: 迅速扩张的无线通讯市场
ext.ext_en: ...the fast-growing wireless communication market.

defs.def_cn: 无线电;无线电收发系统

ext.ext_en: They confirmed by wireless that she was picking up survivors.

defs.def_en: Wireless is a system by which messages are sent over a distance by radio signals.
A wireless or wireless set is a radio.

defs.def_cn: (批评那些不满诸如新道路、住宅区或监狱建在居住地附近的人们)邻避效应，“别在我家后院”观点

ext.ext_en: ...the usual nimby protests from local residents.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone has a nimby attitude, you are criticizing them because they do not want something such as a new road, housing estate, or prison built near to where they live. Nimby is an abbreviation for (缩略=) 'not in my backyard'.

ext.ext_cn: 高声推销的销售代表
ext.ext_en: ...a razzle-dazzle marketing man.

defs.def_en: Razzle-dazzle is the same as razzmatazz .

defs.def_en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, although they do not want to.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

defs.def_en: If you think that someone behaves or lives in a way that is morally good, you can say that they are righteous. People sometimes use righteous to express their disapproval when they think someone is only behaving in this way so that others will admire or support them.

ext.ext_en: I am happy and free, in good health, gay and cheerful.

defs.def_en: A gay person is fun to be with because they are lively and cheerful.

In former times, a fob was a short chain or piece of cloth which fastened a man's watch to his clothing.

defs.def_en: If someone fobs you off, they tell you something just to stop you asking questions.

ext.ext_en: Everything she says is a little off beam.

ext.ext_en: ...the alarming increase in crime.

defs.def_en: Something that is alarming makes you feel afraid or anxious that something unpleasant or dangerous might happen.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is philosophizing, you mean that they are talking or thinking about important subjects, sometimes instead of doing something practical.

defs.def_en: Skiffle is a type of music, popular in the 1950s, played by a small group using household objects as well as guitars and drums.

ext.ext_en: ...the paucity of good British women sprinters.

ext.ext_cn: 就像子女一样，父母也常常很注重保护他们的私生活。
ext.ext_en: Like their children, parents are often defensive about their private lives.

ext.ext_en: She heard the blustering, defensive note in his voice and knew that he was ashamed.

defs.def_en: Someone who is defensive is behaving in a way that shows they feel unsure or threatened.

defs.def_cn: 处于防御姿态;处于守势

ext.ext_cn: 谴责很可能会引发对方自我防卫的反应。
ext.ext_en: Accusations are likely to put the other person on the defensive...

ext.ext_en: He smiled, not wanting to put the man on the defensive.

defs.def_en: If someone is on the defensive, they are trying to protect themselves or their interests because they feel unsure or threatened.

ext.ext_en: I'd always played a defensive game, waiting for my opponent to make a mistake.

defs.def_cn: 转移注意力的;使人分心的

ext.ext_cn: 犯人纵火以转移注意力。
ext.ext_en: Fires were started by the prisoners as a diversionary tactic...

ext.ext_cn: 他们要求英国在北部海岸发动佯攻。
ext.ext_en: They asked the British to launch a diversionary attack on the north coast.

defs.def_en: A diversionary activity is one intended to attract people's attention away from something which you do not want them to think about, know about, or deal with.

defs.def_cn: 永无止境的;永无休止的;永恒的

ext.ext_cn: 一系列无休止的丑闻
ext.ext_en: ...a never-ending series of scandals...

ext.ext_cn: 恐怖主义活动没完没了，不断升级。
ext.ext_en: The spiral of terrorism becomes never-ending.

defs.def_en: If you describe something bad or unpleasant as never-ending, you are emphasizing that it seems to last a very long time.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_en: It could get suddenly nippy in the evenings.

defs.def_en: If the weather is nippy, it is rather cold.

ext.ext_en: This nippy new car has fold down rear seats...

ext.ext_cn: 巴纳比可能15岁了，但他动作敏捷，适合打羽毛球。
ext.ext_en: Barnaby may be 15, but he's nippy and suited to badminton.

defs.def_en: If you describe something or someone as nippy, you mean that they can move very quickly over short distances.

ext.ext_cn: 法国末代国王是1848年逊位的路易·菲力普。
ext.ext_en: The last French king was Louis Philippe, who abdicated in 1848.

defs.def_en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

ext.ext_cn: 许多父母对孩子简直是完全撒手不管。
ext.ext_en: Many parents simply abdicate all responsibility for their children.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone has abdicated responsibility for something, you disapprove of them because they have refused to accept responsibility for it any longer.

defs.def_cn: (表示愤怒或恼火)他妈的，该死的
defs.def_en: Fuck is used to express anger or annoyance.

To fuck around or fuck about means to behave in a way that is silly, stupid, or unnecessary.
Telling someone to fuck off is an insulting way of telling them to go away.
If you fuck something up, you make a mistake or do something badly.

ext.ext_cn: 腐败的投机分子
ext.ext_en: ...a corrupt, opportunistic chancer.

defs.def_en: You can refer to someone as a chancer if you think they use opportunities for their own advantage and often pretend to have skills they do not have.

ext.ext_cn: 挥之不散的腐臭
ext.ext_en: ...the lingering stench of putrefaction.

defs.def_en: Putrefaction is the process of decay.

defs.def_cn: (通常因无处可去而在不舒适的地方)睡觉，过夜

ext.ext_en: ...young people dossing in the streets of our cities.

ext.ext_en: When we had eaten, we dossed down in the lounge.

defs.def_en: If someone dosses somewhere, they sleep in a place which is uncomfortable, usually because they have nowhere else to live.

defs.def_cn: 视察(或督察)人员;检查团

ext.ext_cn: 核设施检查团
ext.ext_en: ...the Nuclear Installations Inspectorate.

defs.def_en: An inspectorate is a group of inspectors who work on the same issue or area.

defs.def_cn: 糖渍白芷（可用于做蛋糕或糖果）

defs.def_en: The Wild West is used to refer to the western part of the United States during the time when Europeans were first settling there.
Meths is the same as methylated spirits .

ext.ext_en: Haig was desperately eager for an affirmative answer...
