ext.ext_cn: 你之所以妒忌是因为唱片公司拒绝接受你的想法。
ext.ext_en: You're jealous because the record company rejected your idea.

defs.def_en: If you are jealous of another person's possessions or qualities, you feel angry or bitter because you do not have them.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 精神错乱的;发狂的;发癫的

ext.ext_cn: 一个精神失常的男子开枪打死了 14 人。
ext.ext_en: A deranged man shot and killed 14 people.

defs.def_en: Someone who is deranged behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way, often as a result of mental illness.

ext.ext_cn: 玛格达莱娜把过去看作毫不相干的累赘。
ext.ext_en: Magdalena considered the past an irrelevant encumbrance.

defs.def_en: An encumbrance is something or someone that encumbers you.

ext.ext_cn: 有人看见休跟旧情人约会。
ext.ext_en: Sue was seen dating an old flame...

ext.ext_cn: 朱莉娅·塞缪尔是安德鲁王子的旧欢之一。
ext.ext_en: Julia Samuel was one of Prince Andrew's old flames.

defs.def_en: An old flame is someone with whom you once had a romantic relationship.

defs.def_cn: 非人的;不齿于人类的;无人性的

ext.ext_cn: 旧时希腊人不把女人当人看。
ext.ext_en: The Greeks treated women as subhuman...

ext.ext_cn: 非人的工作环境不久就导致了身体状况的恶化。
ext.ext_en: The subhuman conditions of work soon caused physical deterioration.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone or their situation as subhuman, you mean that they behave or live in a much worse way than human beings normally do.

ext.ext_cn: 疾病在这一区域的迅速蔓延
ext.ext_en: ...the rapid spread of disease in the area.

ext.ext_cn: 诸如心脏病之类的疾病
ext.ext_en: ...illnesses such as heart disease...

defs.def_en: A disease is an illness which affects people, animals, or plants, for example one which is caused by bacteria or infection.

defs.def_cn: （尤指社会某一群体的）弊病，积习，恶习

ext.ext_cn: 侵蚀着我们社会核心的种族主义恶疾
ext.ext_en: ...the wretched disease of racism eating away at the core of our society.

defs.def_en: You can refer to a bad attitude or habit, usually one that a group of people have, as a disease.
A sash window is a window which consists of two frames placed one above the other. The window can be opened by sliding one frame over the other.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 令人吃惊的;令人惊奇的

ext.ext_cn: 小孩子识字的速度不同,这不足为奇。
ext.ext_en: It is not surprising that children learn to read at different rates...

ext.ext_cn: 每天点同一种三明治的顾客多得惊人。
ext.ext_en: A surprising number of customers order the same sandwich every day.

defs.def_en: Something that is surprising is unexpected or unusual and makes you feel surprised.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 将会有充足的机会去放松、游泳和晒太阳。
ext.ext_en: There'll be ample opportunity to relax, swim and soak up some sun...

ext.ext_cn: 底层的设计为建一个大厨房提供了充足的空间。
ext.ext_en: The design of the ground floor created ample space for a good-sized kitchen.

defs.def_en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 丰满的怀里抱着婴儿的年轻妈妈
ext.ext_en: ...a young mother with a baby resting against her ample bosom.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone's figure as ample, you mean that they are large in a pleasant or attractive way.
Jewellery is ornaments that people wear, for example rings, bracelets, and necklaces. It is often made of a valuable metal such as gold, and sometimes decorated with precious stones.

ext.ext_cn: 我们教训他时，他从来不听。
ext.ext_en: He never listened to us when we told him off...

ext.ext_cn: 我笨手笨脚的，总挨训。
ext.ext_en: I'm always being told off for being so awkward...

defs.def_en: If you tell someone off, you speak to them angrily or seriously because they have done something wrong.

ext.ext_cn: 艾伦退缩了，说他无意冒犯他们。
ext.ext_en: Allen back-pedalled, saying that he had had no intention of offending them...

ext.ext_cn: 他看起来想要收回声明中说过的话。
ext.ext_en: He appeared to back-pedal on that statement.

defs.def_en: If you back-pedal, you express a different or less forceful opinion about something from the one you have previously expressed.

defs.def_cn: 变卦；出尔反尔；背弃诺言

ext.ext_cn: 她已经两次变卦了。
ext.ext_en: She's backpedaled twice already...

ext.ext_cn: 内阁可能背弃这些承诺。
ext.ext_en: The cabinet may backpedal on these commitments.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone back-pedals, you disapprove of their behaviour because they are not doing what they promised.

ext.ext_cn: 这些问题让我沮丧。
ext.ext_en: These questions frustrated me...

ext.ext_cn: 观众在剧场里要受到如此多的限制，这难道不令人恼火吗？
ext.ext_en: Doesn't it frustrate you that audiences in the theatre are so restricted?

defs.def_en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to do anything about the problems it creates.

ext.ext_cn: 政府故意阻挠他为自己的外籍员工申请工作许可证的努力。
ext.ext_en: The government has deliberately frustrated his efforts to gain work permits for his foreign staff.

ext.ext_cn: 她竞选州长的受挫之举
ext.ext_en: ...her frustrated attempt to become governor.

defs.def_en: If someone or something frustrates a plan or attempt to do something, they prevent it from succeeding.

defs.def_cn: 再分配，再配置（金钱或资源）

ext.ext_cn: 为节约成本在公司内部进行的人力和资源再分配方案
ext.ext_en: ...a cost-cutting program to reallocate people and resources within the company...

ext.ext_cn: 将不再资助其他地区，以便资金可以重新分配给饱受矿井关闭影响的城镇。
ext.ext_en: Other areas are to lose aid so that money can be reallocated to towns devastated by pit closures.

defs.def_en: When organizations reallocate money or resources, they decide to change the way they spend the money or use the resources.

defs.def_cn: 同上，同前(旧用法，ditto 的省略形式)
defs.def_en: do. is an old-fashioned written abbreviation for (书面缩略=) ditto .
A burglar alarm is an electric device that makes a bell ring loudly if someone tries to enter a building by force.

ext.ext_cn: 这座动物园需要更好的管理，而不是更多的资金。
ext.ext_en: The zoo needed better management rather than more money...

ext.ext_cn: 这场争论围绕着工资、工作条件以及矿业管理展开。
ext.ext_en: The dispute is about wages, working conditions and the management of the mining industry.

defs.def_en: Management is the control and organizing of a business or other organization.

ext.ext_cn: 管理部门正在竭尽全力改善局面。
ext.ext_en: The management is doing its best to improve the situation...

ext.ext_cn: 我们需要让更多的女性进入高层管理。
ext.ext_en: We need to get more women into top management...

defs.def_en: You can refer to the people who control and organize a business or other organization as the management .

ext.ext_cn: 她对自己职业生涯的规划
ext.ext_en: ...her management of her professional life.

ext.ext_cn: 聪明的理财手法，例如尽量按月支付大宗的账单
ext.ext_en: ...intelligent money management, for example paying big bills monthly where possible.

defs.def_en: Management is the way people control different parts of their lives.
A barn is a building on a farm in which crops or animal food can be kept.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 不完全利他的动机和抱负
ext.ext_en: ...motives and ambitions that are not entirely altruistic.

defs.def_en: If your behaviour or motives are altruistic, you show concern for the happiness and welfare of other people rather than for yourself.

ext.ext_cn: 这会造成漏气，破坏罐子的密封性。
ext.ext_en: This would permit air to enter, breaking the hermetic seal of the jar.

defs.def_en: If a container has a hermetic seal, the seal is very tight so that no air can get in or out.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 与外界隔绝的;不受外界干扰的

ext.ext_cn: 其电影产业以它奇特的与世隔绝的方式运作。
ext.ext_en: Its film industry operates in its own curiously hermetic way...

ext.ext_cn: 他们的工作比任何时候都要更加安逸，更加不受外界干扰。
ext.ext_en: Their work is more cosily hermetic than ever.

defs.def_en: You use hermetic to describe something which you disapprove of because it seems to be totally separate from other people and things in society.

defs.def_cn: 销售点；售货点（缩略形式为POS）

ext.ext_cn: 需求环节的管理层会捕捉销售点顾客购物行为的信息，然后把信息再反馈给供应环节。
ext.ext_en: Demand-chain management captures information on consumer behaviour at the point of sale and feeds it up the supply chain.

defs.def_en: The point of sale is the place in a shop where a product is passed from the seller to the customer. The abbreviation POS is also used.

defs.def_cn: （用作修饰成分）销售点,售货点（缩略形式为POS）

ext.ext_cn: 引进销售点电子系统提高了效率。
ext.ext_en: Introduction of electronic point-of-sale systems is improving efficiency.

ext.ext_cn: 售货处的商品广告
ext.ext_en: ...point-of-sale advertising.

defs.def_en: Point of sale is used to describe things which occur or are located or used at the place where you buy something. The abbreviation POS is also used.
If you talk about the ubiquity of something, you mean that it seems to be everywhere.
A drover is someone whose job is to make sheep or cattle move from one place to another in groups.

ext.ext_cn: 别靠近我。
ext.ext_en: Don't come near me...

ext.ext_cn: 她的孩子们每年都回去，住在小屋边的农舍里。
ext.ext_en: Her children went back every year to stay in a farmhouse near the cottage...

defs.def_en: If something is near a place, thing, or person, it is a short distance from them.

defs.def_cn: 接近(某一状态);几乎;差不多

ext.ext_cn: 战后，哈迪家族濒于破产。
ext.ext_en: After the war, The House of Hardie came near to bankruptcy...

ext.ext_cn: 对哈夫纳机器的修理即将结束。
ext.ext_en: The repairs to the Hafner machine were near to completion...

defs.def_en: If someone or something is near to a particular state, they have almost reached it.

ext.ext_cn: 近乎恶心的难受感觉
ext.ext_en: ...a sickening sensation that was near to nausea.

ext.ext_cn: 她的感情常常是恨而不是爱。
ext.ext_en: Often her feelings were nearer hatred than love.

defs.def_en: If something is similar to something else, you can say that it is near to it.

defs.def_cn: (与…)最相似的;(和…)几乎差不多的

ext.ext_cn: 司法行业看来是最不易受经济萧条影响的领域了。
ext.ext_en: It would appear that the legal profession is the nearest thing to a recession-proof industry...

ext.ext_cn: 他是英国在阿尔贝维尔冬奥会上最有希望夺取金牌的选手。
ext.ext_en: He is the nearest to a dead cert that Britain has in Albertville.

defs.def_en: You describe the thing most similar to something as the nearest thing to it when there is no example of the thing itself.

ext.ext_cn: 我离开日本的日子一天天近了。
ext.ext_en: The time for my departure from Japan was drawing nearer every day.

defs.def_en: If a time or event draws near, it will happen soon.

ext.ext_cn: 凌晨3点至5点表现最差，近中午时分最好。
ext.ext_en: Performance is lowest between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m., and reaches a peak near midday...

ext.ext_cn: “自从隐居到这里，”他在生命即将结束时写道，“我一直没有离开过这些大山。”
ext.ext_en: 'Since I retired to this place,' he wrote near the end of his life, 'I have never been out of these mountains.'...

defs.def_en: If something happens near a particular time, it happens just before or just after that time.

defs.def_cn: (指数量或数字)接近于，左右，上下

ext.ext_cn: 将轿车年产量从250万辆左右增加到接近475万辆
ext.ext_en: ...to increase manufacturing from about 2.5 million cars a year to nearer 4.75 million...

ext.ext_cn: 英镑去年年终降到了接近全年最低点的水平，预计今天将再度面临汇价下跌的压力。
ext.ext_en: The pound, which ended last year near its annual low, is expected to come under renewed pressure today.

defs.def_en: You use near to say that something is a little more or less than an amount or number stated.

ext.ext_cn: 他绝对不会去医院。
ext.ext_en: He will absolutely not go near a hospital...

ext.ext_cn: 我很生她的气,有一个星期没见她了。
ext.ext_en: I'm so annoyed with her that I haven't been near her for a week.

defs.def_en: You can say that someone will not go near a person or thing when you are emphasizing that they refuse to see them or go there.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 矗立在林间小块空地近侧的一棵高大的山毛榉树
ext.ext_en: ...a mighty beech tree on the near side of the little clearing...

ext.ext_cn: 简一只脚就近蹬上马镫，转脸看着陌生人。
ext.ext_en: Jane put one foot in the near stirrup and turned to look at the stranger.

defs.def_en: The near one of two things is the one that is closer.

ext.ext_cn: 据信她在法国里维埃拉去世时几乎身无分文。
ext.ext_en: She was believed to have died in near poverty on the French Riviera.

ext.ext_cn: 被调来帮助银行摆脱濒临破产困境的48岁的新任
ext.ext_en: ...the 48-year-old who was brought in to rescue the bank from near collapse.

defs.def_en: You use near to indicate that something is almost the thing mentioned.

defs.def_cn: (在竞赛中)实力接近的，旗鼓相当的

ext.ext_cn: 他比劲敌乔纳森·福特少用了大概3秒钟完成了漫长的赛程。
ext.ext_en: He completed the lengthy course some three seconds faster than his nearest rival, Jonathon Ford...

ext.ext_cn: 本场胜利使乌克兰人甩开了最强有力的对手，莫斯科迪那摩队。
ext.ext_en: That victory put the Ukrainians beyond the reach of their nearest challengers, Dynamo Moscow.

defs.def_en: In a contest, your nearest rival or challenger is the person or team that is most likely to defeat you.

ext.ext_cn: 接近马厩时，他勒马缓行，轻拍它的脖颈。
ext.ext_en: As he neared the stable, he slowed the horse and patted it on the neck...

ext.ext_cn: 我们在驶近通往 Tsagochen Thang 的垭口时，货车噼啪几声熄火了。
ext.ext_en: We were nearing the top of the pass to Tsagochen Thang when the van spluttered and died.

defs.def_en: When you near a place, you get quite near to it.

defs.def_cn: 接近，临近(某一阶段或某一点)

ext.ext_cn: 很难猜测他的年龄，他一定快50了。
ext.ext_en: His age was hard to guess — he must have been nearing fifty...

ext.ext_cn: 培训快结束了，你还没有参加任何评估测试。
ext.ext_en: You are nearing the end of your training and you haven't attempted any assessments yet...

defs.def_en: When someone or something nears a particular stage or point, they will soon reach that stage or point.

ext.ext_cn: 临近中场休息时，哈迪曼差点梅开二度。
ext.ext_en: As half time neared, Hardyman almost scored twice...

ext.ext_cn: 随着选举日的临近，这一因素将愈发重要。
ext.ext_en: This factor will come increasingly to the fore as election day nears.

defs.def_en: You say that an important time or event nears when it is going to occur quite soon.

defs.def_cn: 最亲近的人;最亲密的人;至亲

ext.ext_cn: 甚至不向最亲近的人流露自己情感的英国社会习俗
ext.ext_en: ...that English convention of not showing your feelings, even to your nearest and dearest.

defs.def_en: People sometimes refer to their close relatives and friends as their nearest and dearest .

ext.ext_cn: 人们会从四面八方聚到一起。
ext.ext_en: People would gather from near and far...

ext.ext_cn: 没几个月他就远近闻名了。
ext.ext_en: Within months his reputation spread near and far.

defs.def_en: You use near and far to indicate that you are referring to a very large area or distance.

ext.ext_cn: 关于维生素C的争议短期内不可能平息。
ext.ext_en: The controversy regarding vitamin C is unlikely to be resolved in the near future.

defs.def_en: If you say that something will happen in the near future, you mean that it will happen quite soon.

defs.def_cn: 一点儿也不;完全不;远不

ext.ext_cn: 他们还远不够好。
ext.ext_en: They are nowhere near good enough...

ext.ext_cn: 这远不如戴维所料想的那么痛苦。
ext.ext_en: It was nowhere near as painful as David had expected...

defs.def_en: You use nowhere near and not anywhere near to emphasize that something is not the case.

defs.def_cn: 几乎丝毫不差地，几乎一样地(英国英语中亦作 as near as dammit)

ext.ext_cn: 我几乎是以一英镑一件的价钱买下了它们。
ext.ext_en: I bought them for a pound apiece, near enough...

ext.ext_cn: 它们几乎是新的。
ext.ext_en: They are as near as dammit new...

defs.def_en: If you want to indicate that something is almost true, you can use the expressions near enough and damned near. In British English, you can also say as near as dammit.

defs.def_cn: 差点，险些(发生某事)(英国英语中亦作 as near as dammit)

ext.ext_cn: 他险些把我骗了。
ext.ext_en: He damned near fooled me...

ext.ext_cn: 像他随后告诉米兰达的那样，他几乎没碰它。
ext.ext_en: As he was to tell Miranda later, he as near as dammit left it there.

defs.def_en: If you want to indicate that something almost happened, you can use the expression damned near. In British English, you can also say as near as dammit .
A paper clip is a small piece of bent wire that is used to fasten papers together.

defs.def_cn: (长途旅程中暂时停留休息的）小站
defs.def_en: A way station is a place where people stop to eat and rest when they are on a long journey.
A way station is a small station between two large stations on a railway.

ext.ext_cn: 支持者们充满了期待。
ext.ext_en: The supporters had a tremendous air of expectancy.

defs.def_en: See also:life expectancy;Expectancy is the feeling or hope that something exciting, interesting, or good is about to happen.

ext.ext_cn: “拜托！”多特反驳道，“它们又便宜又管用。”
ext.ext_en: 'For heaven's sake!' Dot expostulated. 'They're cheap and they're useful.'...

ext.ext_cn: 那一刻，我以为她要提出异议。
ext.ext_en: For a moment I thought she was going to expostulate...

defs.def_en: If you expostulate, you express strong disagreement with someone.
A falconer is someone who trains and uses falcons for hunting.

ext.ext_cn: 其他部长在攻击诋毁他。
ext.ext_en: Ministerial colleagues were briefing against him.

defs.def_en: If someone, especially a politician, briefs against another person, he or she tries to harm the other person's reputation by saying something unfavourable about them.

ext.ext_cn: 4月零售总额的下降
ext.ext_en: ...a fall in April's retail sales stats.

defs.def_en: Stats are facts which are obtained from analysing information expressed in numbers. Stats is an abbreviation for (缩略=) 'statistics'.
Stats is a branch of mathematics concerned with the study of information that is expressed in numbers.
A parkway is a wide road with trees and grass on both sides.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 被缠住的;纠结在一起的

ext.ext_cn: 被捕蟹网缠住的鲸鱼
ext.ext_en: ...a whale that became entangled in crab nets.

defs.def_en: If something is entangled in something such as a rope, wire, or net, it is caught in it very firmly.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 这件事肯定会在国际政坛上纠缠不清。
ext.ext_en: This case was bound to get entangled in international politics.

defs.def_en: If you become entangled in problems or difficulties, you become involved in problems or difficulties from which it is hard to escape.

ext.ext_cn: 古典音乐
ext.ext_en: ...classical music.

ext.ext_cn: 乔治·格什温的音乐作品
ext.ext_en: ...the music of George Gershwin.

defs.def_en: Music is the pattern of sounds produced by people singing or playing instruments.

ext.ext_cn: 他继续学习音乐，主攻单簧管。
ext.ext_en: He went on to study music, specialising in the clarinet.

ext.ext_cn: 音乐课
ext.ext_en: ...a music lesson.

defs.def_en: Music is the art of creating or performing music.

ext.ext_cn: 他一直都不识谱。
ext.ext_en: He's never been able to read music.

defs.def_en: See also:sheet music;Music is the symbols written on paper which represent musical sounds.

defs.def_cn: 悦耳的声音;佳音;中听的话

ext.ext_cn: 大众的支持对任何一名政界人士来说都是佳音。
ext.ext_en: Popular support—it's music to the ears of any politician.

defs.def_en: If something that you hear is music to your ears, it makes you feel very happy.

defs.def_cn: 承担自己行为的后果;接受批评（或惩罚）

ext.ext_cn: 迟早我得自己承担后果。
ext.ext_en: Sooner or later, I'm going to have to face the music.

defs.def_en: If you face the music, you put yourself in a position where you will be criticized or punished for something you have done.

defs.def_cn: (设有可开启和关闭的水闸的)泄洪道，泄水道
defs.def_en: A sluice is a passage that carries a current of water and has a barrier, called a sluice gate, which can be opened and closed to control the flow of water.

ext.ext_en: He sluiced the bath and filled it...

defs.def_en: A telephone or piece of electrical equipment that is dead is no longer functioning, for example because it no longer has any electrical power.

defs.def_cn: (体育运动中的球）界外的，死的
defs.def_en: In sport, when a ball is dead, it has gone outside the playing area, or a situation has occurred in which the game has to be temporarily stopped, and none of the players can score points or gain an advantage.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (声音)沉闷的;(颜色)暗淡的，不鲜亮的

ext.ext_cn: “没错，梅格。”他用冰冷、阴沉的声音答道。
ext.ext_en: 'That is correct, Meg,' he answered in his cold, dead voice...

ext.ext_cn: 接着他听见深井里回响起一声刺耳的尖叫，然后是砰的一声闷响，再之后就什么也听不见了。
ext.ext_en: Then he heard a piercing scream echoing down the deep well, ending in a dull, dead thud.

defs.def_en: A dead sound or colour is dull rather than lively or bright.

defs.def_cn: 完全的，绝对的（尤用于修饰 centre, silence 和 stop）

ext.ext_cn: 他调整每颗棋子，使它们立于格子的正中央。
ext.ext_en: He adjusted each chesspiece so that it stood dead centre in its square...

ext.ext_cn: 他们匆匆地走来走去，一言不发，面露焦急之色。
ext.ext_en: They hurried about in dead silence, with anxious faces...

defs.def_en: Dead is used to mean 'complete' or 'absolute', especially before the words 'centre', 'silence', and 'stop'.

ext.ext_cn: 可以看得见火星，就在望远镜的正中央。
ext.ext_en: Mars was visible, dead in the centre of the telescope...

ext.ext_cn: 他们的箭正中靶心。
ext.ext_en: Their arrows are dead on target...

defs.def_en: Dead means 'precisely' or 'exactly'.

ext.ext_cn: 去梅多霍尔购物中心也非常方便。
ext.ext_en: Meadowhall is also dead easy for people to get to...

ext.ext_cn: 实际上，他的诗听起来非常乏味。
ext.ext_en: His poems sound dead boring, actually...

defs.def_en: Dead is sometimes used to mean 'very'.

ext.ext_cn: “我们请她来吃晚饭吧。”——“除非我死了！”
ext.ext_en: 'Let's invite her to dinner.' — 'Over my dead body!'

defs.def_en: If you reply 'Over my dead body' when a plan or action has been suggested, you are emphasizing that you dislike it, and will do everything you can to prevent it.

defs.def_cn: 完全了结的;彻底过去的

ext.ext_cn: 我以为这整件事已经完全了结了。
ext.ext_en: I thought the whole business was dead and buried...

ext.ext_cn: 英国煤炭工业只消两年就将彻底瓦解。
ext.ext_en: In two years, the British coal industry will be dead and buried.

defs.def_en: If you say that something such as an idea or situation is dead and buried, you are emphasizing that you think that it is completely finished or past, and cannot happen or exist again in the future.

ext.ext_cn: 他猝死在码头区。
ext.ext_en: He dropped dead on the quayside.

defs.def_en: If you say that a person or animal dropped dead or dropped down dead, you mean that they died very suddenly and unexpectedly.

defs.def_cn: 去死吧;见鬼去吧;别再烦人

ext.ext_cn: 在他电话联系的公司里，75% 都怀有敌意，让他“见鬼去吧”。
ext.ext_en: 75% of the firms he called were hostile and told him to 'drop dead.'

defs.def_en: See also:drop-dead;If you tell someone to drop dead, you are insulting them, rudely disagreeing with them, or refusing to do something, or telling them to stop bothering you.

ext.ext_cn: 天才往往在离开人世之后才得到认可。
ext.ext_en: Often a genius is recognized only after he is dead and gone.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is dead and gone, you are emphasizing that they are dead, and thinking about what happened or will happen after their death.

ext.ext_cn: 经过那趟旅程之后,你看上去真是累坏了。
ext.ext_en: You looked half dead after that journey...

ext.ext_cn: 我觉得自己现在几乎快要死了。
ext.ext_en: I feel pretty dead right now.

defs.def_en: If you say that you feel dead or are half dead, you mean that you feel very tired or ill and very weak.

defs.def_cn: 在夜晚万籁俱寂之时/在隆冬

ext.ext_cn: 我不能在深夜乘飞机非法进入一个国家。
ext.ext_en: I couldn't fly illegally into a country in the dead of night...

ext.ext_cn: 我们在夜深人静的时候把它埋到了花园里。
ext.ext_en: We buried it in the garden at dead of night...

defs.def_en: If something happens in the dead of night ,at dead of night, or in the dead of winter, it happens in the middle part of the night or the winter, when it is darkest or coldest.
When Christians say that Jesus Christ rose from the dead or raised someone from the dead, they mean that Jesus came back to life after he had died, or brought a dead person back to life.

defs.def_cn: 卷土重来;重新活跃起来（或获得成功）

ext.ext_cn: 从一切迹象来看，这是一家已经起死回生的公司。
ext.ext_en: This was a company that, by all appearances, had risen from the dead...

ext.ext_cn: 福尔多重整旗鼓，赢得了他的第三个高尔夫球公开赛冠军。
ext.ext_en: Faldo came back from the dead to win his third Open golf championship.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone or something rises or comes back from the dead, you mean that they become active or successful again after being inactive for a while.

defs.def_cn: 死也（不会），绝对（不会）（穿某种衣服、去某个地方或处于某种境地)

ext.ext_cn: 我死也不会戴草帽。
ext.ext_en: I wouldn't be seen dead in a straw hat.

ext.ext_cn: 死也不会去推婴儿车的男人们
ext.ext_en: ...men who wouldn't be seen dead pushing a pram...

defs.def_en: If you say that you wouldn't be seen dead or be caught dead in particular clothes, places, or situations, you are expressing strong dislike or disapproval of them.

ext.ext_cn: 我们一下子全都停了下来看着它。
ext.ext_en: We all stopped dead and looked at it...

ext.ext_cn: 她本打算悄悄进去，但谈话却突然中断了。
ext.ext_en: She had meant to make a discreet entrance, but conversation stopped dead...

defs.def_en: To stop dead means to suddenly stop happening or moving. To stop someone or something dead means to cause them to suddenly stop happening or moving.

defs.def_cn: 败局已定的;不太可能成功的

ext.ext_cn: 一张否决票可能就会使这个条约胎死腹中。
ext.ext_en: A 'no' vote would have left the treaty dead in the water.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone or something is dead in the water, you are emphasizing that they have failed, and that there is little hope of them being successful in the future.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 不确定的；迟疑的；无把握的

ext.ext_cn: 他拿不准他哥哥的意图是什么。
ext.ext_en: He was uncertain about his brother's intentions...

ext.ext_cn: 他们还不确定这笔交易的总价值是多少。
ext.ext_en: They were uncertain of the total value of the transaction...

defs.def_en: If you are uncertain about something, you do not know what you should do, what is going to happen, or what the truth is about something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 未知的；不明了的；不确定的

ext.ext_cn: 然而，这些共和国究竟能够提供多少切实可行的帮助还未可知。
ext.ext_en: How far the republics can give practical help, however, is uncertain...

ext.ext_cn: 还不确定他们是否会接受这一方案。
ext.ext_en: It's uncertain whether they will accept the plan...

defs.def_en: If something is uncertain, it is not known or definite.

ext.ext_cn: 她明白无误地叫他离她远远的。
ext.ext_en: She told him in no uncertain terms to go away.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone tells a person something in no uncertain terms, you are emphasizing that they say it strongly and clearly so that there is no doubt about what they mean.

ext.ext_cn: 你还记得那时候大家都有些厌倦电子音乐的嘈杂声而拔掉电子乐器回归到原声状态吗？
ext.ext_en: Do you remember when everyone got a bit tired of electronic clutter and went unplugged and acoustic?

defs.def_en: If a pop group or musician performs unplugged, they perform without any electric instruments.

ext.ext_cn: 让她恼火的是，那个陌生人并没有走。
ext.ext_en: To her annoyance the stranger did not go away...

ext.ext_cn: 他否认其他欧盟委员会委员对英国人有不满。
ext.ext_en: He denied there was any annoyance with the British among other EC members.

defs.def_en: Annoyance is the feeling that you get when someone makes you feel fairly angry or impatient.

defs.def_cn: 令人烦恼的事物；令人厌烦的事物

ext.ext_cn: 不为他人着想的邻居会非常惹人厌。
ext.ext_en: Inconsiderate neighbours can be more than an annoyance.

defs.def_en: An annoyance is something that makes you feel angry or impatient.

ext.ext_cn: 他从口袋里掏出一个相当大的米色信封。
ext.ext_en: He took a largish buff envelope from his pocket.

defs.def_en: Something that is buff is pale brown in colour.

ext.ext_cn: 拉尼尔法官是个真正的影迷。
ext.ext_en: Judge Lanier is a real film buff...

ext.ext_cn: 任何一个有点儿水平的电脑行家都能在几分钟内为你解决这个问题。
ext.ext_en: Any competent computer buff should be able to do it for you in a few minutes.

defs.def_en: You use buff to describe someone who knows a lot about a particular subject. For example, if you describe someone as a film buff, you mean that they know a lot about films.

ext.ext_cn: 他已经在擦汽车轮毂了。
ext.ext_en: He was already buffing the car's hubs.

defs.def_en: If you buff the surface of something, for example your car or your shoes, you rub it with a piece of soft material in order to make it shine.

ext.ext_cn: 我收到一个很要好的朋友的来信。
ext.ext_en: I had received a letter from a very close friend.

ext.ext_cn: 辞职信
ext.ext_en: ...a letter of resignation...

defs.def_en: If you write a letter to someone, you write a message on paper and send it to them, usually by post.

ext.ext_cn: 字母表中的字母
ext.ext_en: ...the letters of the alphabet.

ext.ext_cn: 字母E
ext.ext_en: ...the letter E.

defs.def_en: Letters are written symbols which represent one of the sounds in a language.

defs.def_cn: （校队队衣的）校名首字母标志（以嘉许优秀运动员）

ext.ext_cn: 瓦莱丽在排球、篮球和曲棍球三个项目上获得了佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉。
ext.ext_en: Valerie earned letters in three sports: volleyball, basketball, and field hockey.

defs.def_en: If a student earns a letter in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.

defs.def_cn: 赢得佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉

ext.ext_cn: 伯考思在足球上获得了佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉。
ext.ext_en: Burkoth lettered in soccer.

defs.def_en: If a student letters in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.

ext.ext_cn: 他们死抠法律字眼。依我看他们应该感到惭愧。
ext.ext_en: They had stuck to the letter of the law and in my view they should be ashamed.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone keeps to the letter of the law, you mean that they act according to what is actually written in the law, rather than according to the general principles of it, especially when you disapprove of this.

defs.def_cn: （执行指示）毫厘不爽地，不折不扣地

ext.ext_cn: 她分毫不差地遵照他的吩咐去做。
ext.ext_en: She obeyed his instructions to the letter.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone carries out instructions to the letter, you mean that they do exactly what they are told to do, paying great attention to every detail.

ext.ext_cn: 对讲机发出嗡嗡声，他按下了相应的开关。
ext.ext_en: The intercom buzzed and he pressed down the appropriate switch...

ext.ext_cn: 武装直升机嗡嗡地飞过城市上空。
ext.ext_en: Attack helicopters buzzed across the city.

defs.def_en: If something buzzes or buzzes somewhere, it makes a long continuous sound, like the noise a bee makes when it is flying.

defs.def_cn: 匆忙地走动；忙得团团转

ext.ext_cn: 几个观光客在匆匆游览。
ext.ext_en: A few tourists were buzzing about...

ext.ext_cn: 拍卖行里乱哄哄谈生意的商人们令她望而生畏。
ext.ext_en: She was intimidated by the number of businessmen buzzing around the saleroom.

defs.def_en: If people are buzzing around, they are moving around quickly and busily.

ext.ext_cn: 还有很多问题在我的脑海里翻腾。
ext.ext_en: Many more questions were buzzing around in my head...

ext.ext_cn: 高级时尚顾问会使你的头脑充满新鲜想法。
ext.ext_en: Top style consultants will leave you buzzing with new ideas.

defs.def_en: If questions or ideas are buzzing around your head, or if your head is buzzing with questions or ideas, you are thinking about a lot of things, often in a confused way.

defs.def_cn: 充满嘈杂的（谈话、活动）声

ext.ext_cn: 大家在吃午饭，排练室里很是嘈杂。
ext.ext_en: The rehearsal studio is buzzing with lunchtime activity.

ext.ext_cn: 首都到处流传着可能发生游行示威的流言。
ext.ext_en: The capital is buzzing with rumours of possible demonstrations.

defs.def_en: If a place is buzzing with activity or conversation, there is a lot of activity or conversation there, especially because something important or exciting is about to happen.

ext.ext_cn: 当被告被带进来的时候，整个法庭的人都激动起来，一片嘈杂。
ext.ext_en: A buzz of excitement filled the courtroom as the defendant was led in.

ext.ext_cn: 兴奋嘈杂的说话声
ext.ext_en: ...the excited buzz of conversation.

defs.def_en: You can use buzz to refer to a long continuous sound, usually caused by lots of people talking at once.

ext.ext_cn: 表演仍然能让他兴奋不已。
ext.ext_en: Performing still gives him a buzz...

ext.ext_cn: 制造冲突让他感到幸灾乐祸。
ext.ext_en: He got a buzz from creating confrontations.

defs.def_en: If something gives you a buzz, it makes you feel very happy or excited for a short time.

defs.def_cn: 热闹有趣的气氛；时尚氛围

ext.ext_cn: 姑娘们在前几次的游览中就爱上了都柏林，她们说她们喜欢这个城市的时尚氛围。
ext.ext_en: The girls fell in love with Dublin on previous visits. They said that what they liked was the buzz about the place.

defs.def_en: If a place or event has a buzz, it has a lively, interesting and modern atmosphere.

ext.ext_cn: 园艺设计圈里的最新流行词语
ext.ext_en: ...the latest buzz phrase in garden design circles...

ext.ext_cn: 性教育在学校是个热议话题。
ext.ext_en: Sex education in schools was the buzz topic.

defs.def_en: You can use buzz to refer to a word, idea, or activity which has recently become extremely popular.

defs.def_cn: （用内线）给…打电话；（用蜂鸣器）呼叫

ext.ext_cn: 那天上午晚些时候朱丽给我打来了电话。
ext.ext_en: Later that morning Julie buzzed me.

ext.ext_cn: 我们到了梅贝里街的时候会给他打电话。
ext.ext_en: We'll give him a buzz when we get to Maybury Street.

defs.def_en: If you buzz someone, you call them, usually using an internal telephone line or a buzzer.

ext.ext_cn: 美国战斗机低飞掠过城市。
ext.ext_en: American fighter planes buzzed the city.

defs.def_en: If an aircraft buzzes a place, it flies low over it, usually in a threatening way.

defs.def_cn: （语法中的）分词（包括过去分词和现在分词）
defs.def_en: In grammar, a participle is a form of a verb that can be used in compound tenses of the verb. There are two participles in English: the past participle, which usually ends in '-ed', and the present participle, which ends in '-ing'.
A weather station is a place where facts about the weather are recorded and studied.

ext.ext_cn: 如果不输血，患者必死无疑。
ext.ext_en: Without a transfusion, the victim's probability of dying was 100%...

ext.ext_cn: 在有些情况下，犯罪或受害的几率要相对更高。
ext.ext_en: The probabilities of crime or victimization are higher with some situations than with others...

defs.def_en: The probability of something happening is how likely it is to happen, sometimes expressed as a fraction or a percentage.

ext.ext_cn: 除非立即采取行动，否则管道很有可能冻住。
ext.ext_en: There's an excellent probability that unless action is quickly taken, pipes will freeze...

ext.ext_cn: 如果一处房产已经拥有多年，有可能它已经增值了。
ext.ext_en: If you've owned property for several years, the probability is that values have increased...

defs.def_en: You say that there is a probability that something will happen when it is likely to happen.

ext.ext_cn: 共和党人最好习惯他们很有可能失败的事实。
ext.ext_en: The Republicans had better get used to the fact that in all probability, they are going to lose...

ext.ext_cn: 很可能再过数月他们才会转运。
ext.ext_en: In all probability, the final upturn in their fortunes is some months away yet.

defs.def_en: If you say that something will happen in all probability, you mean that you think it is very likely to happen.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 性爱的;（引起）性欲的；撩人的

ext.ext_cn: 这听起来可能像是异想天开，但是绝对不是什么性体验。
ext.ext_en: It might sound like some kind of wild fantasy, but it wasn't an erotic experience at all.

ext.ext_cn: 摆出撩人姿势的裸体女人的照片
ext.ext_en: ...photographs of nude women in erotic poses.

defs.def_en: If you describe something as erotic, you mean that it involves sexual feelings or arouses sexual desire.

ext.ext_cn: 色情画也变成了一种艺术。
ext.ext_en: Erotic paintings also became a fine art.

defs.def_en: Erotic art shows naked people or sexual acts, and is intended to produce feelings of sexual pleasure.

ext.ext_cn: 她坐上车，发动了引擎。
ext.ext_en: She got in and started the motor.

defs.def_en: The motor in a machine, vehicle, or boat is the part that uses electricity or fuel to produce movement, so that the machine, vehicle, or boat can work.

defs.def_cn: 机动的;由发动机驱动的

ext.ext_cn: 机动车辆偷盗案上升了15.9%。
ext.ext_en: Theft of motor vehicles is up by 15.9%.

defs.def_en: Motor vehicles and boats have a petrol or diesel engine.

ext.ext_cn: 英国汽车工业的未来
ext.ext_en: ...the future of the British motor industry...

ext.ext_cn: 他是一名汽车修理工。
ext.ext_en: He worked as a motor mechanic.

defs.def_en: Motor is used to describe activities relating to vehicles such as cars and buses.
Some people refer to a car as a motor .

ext.ext_cn: 我从柴郡一路南下开过来。
ext.ext_en: I had motored down from Cheshire.

defs.def_en: If you motor somewhere, you travel there in a car, usually for pleasure.

ext.ext_cn: 我们重新启动马达，沿河而下。
ext.ext_en: Restarting the engine, we motored downriver.

defs.def_en: If people in a small sailing boat motor somewhere, they use the boat's motor rather than the power of the wind to get there.

defs.def_cn: 有色眼镜，眼罩（比喻观点狭隘，不考虑他人的想法）

ext.ext_cn: 就数学家们来说，用学者的眼光来看问题不无裨益。
ext.ext_en: As far as mathematicians are concerned, there's a certain virtue in wearing intellectual blinkers...

ext.ext_cn: 至少你现在已经摘下了有色眼镜，能够看清这段关系了。
ext.ext_en: At least you have removed your blinkers and can now see the relationship in its true colours.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as wearing blinkers, you think that they have a narrow point of view and are not taking other people's opinions into account.

defs.def_cn: （系于马眼旁使其只能直视的）马眼罩
defs.def_en: Blinkers are two pieces of leather which are placed at the side of a horse's eyes so that it can only see straight ahead.

ext.ext_cn: 利率下调让数百万抵押贷款还款人感到高兴。
ext.ext_en: Lower interest rates pleased millions of mortgage payers.

defs.def_en: See also:ratepayer;taxpayer;You can refer to someone as a payer if they pay a particular kind of bill or fee. For example, a mortgage payer is someone who pays a mortgage.

ext.ext_cn: 我一直及时付款，从未欠债。
ext.ext_en: I have always been a good payer and have never gone into debt...

ext.ext_cn: 该事务所被拖欠了约30万英镑。
ext.ext_en: The firm was owed around £300,000 by late payers.

defs.def_en: A good payer pays you quickly or pays you a lot of money. A bad payer takes a long time to pay you, or does not pay you very much.

ext.ext_cn: 委员会一致通过再次选举他为党的领袖。
ext.ext_en: The council re-elected him unopposed as party leader...

ext.ext_cn: 次日，第一军的装甲车畅通无阻地驶进突尼斯。
ext.ext_en: The next day, 1st Army armoured cars drove unopposed into Tunis.

defs.def_en: In something such as an election or a war, if someone is unopposed, there are no opponents competing or fighting against them.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 紫杉的各个部分都有毒，包括浆果。
ext.ext_en: All parts of the yew tree are poisonous, including the berries.

ext.ext_cn: 一大团有毒气体
ext.ext_en: ...a large cloud of poisonous gas.

defs.def_en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you swallow or absorb it.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 毒蜘蛛和毒蛇成百上千。
ext.ext_en: There are hundreds of poisonous spiders and snakes.

defs.def_en: An animal that is poisonous produces a poison that will kill you or make you ill if the animal bites you.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 极令人厌恶的；会造成危害的；恶毒的

ext.ext_cn: 恶毒的评论
ext.ext_en: ...poisonous comments.

ext.ext_cn: 醒着躺了半宿，为卑劣的猜疑所折磨
ext.ext_en: ...lying awake half the night tormented by poisonous suspicions.

defs.def_en: If you describe something as poisonous, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and likely to spoil or destroy a good relationship or situation.

ext.ext_cn: 报告中包含很多统计资料。
ext.ext_en: The report contains a great deal of statistical information...

ext.ext_cn: 我们需要用统计数据来证实那一猜测。
ext.ext_en: We need to back that suspicion up with statistical proof.

defs.def_en: Statistical means relating to the use of statistics.

ext.ext_cn: 昨天，他被捉拿归案。
ext.ext_en: The law caught up with him yesterday.

defs.def_en: When people catch up with someone who has done something wrong, they succeed in finding them in order to arrest or punish them.

defs.def_cn: 和…算旧账；使…最终尝到苦果

ext.ext_cn: 尽管后来他成了事业有成的生意人，以前的犯罪前科终究让他尝到了苦果。
ext.ext_en: Although he subsequently became a successful businessman, his criminal past caught up with him.

defs.def_en: If something catches up with you, you are forced to deal with something unpleasant that happened or that you did in the past, which you have been able to avoid until now.

ext.ext_cn: 夏天我的皮肤有时候会出油。
ext.ext_en: During the summer, my skin sometimes gets greasy...

ext.ext_cn: 有时候，我觉得他不喜欢我。
ext.ext_en: Sometimes I think he dislikes me...

defs.def_en: You use sometimes to say that something happens on some occasions rather than all the time.

defs.def_cn: （重症病人的血压、体温等）生命体征
defs.def_en: The vital signs of a seriously ill person are the things such as their blood pressure and temperature which show that they are alive.

ext.ext_cn: 我顺着走廊看了一眼9号房。
ext.ext_en: I looked down the hallway to room number nine...

ext.ext_cn: 她转头看他。
ext.ext_en: She  turned to look at him...

defs.def_en: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

ext.ext_cn: 你只要看一下第3幕最后那部分。
ext.ext_en: You've  just got to look at the last bit of Act Three.

ext.ext_cn: 大致浏览一下周一的英国报纸就会发现，国外新闻还真不少。
ext.ext_en: A quick look at Monday's British newspapers shows that there's plenty of interest in foreign news.

defs.def_en: If you look at a book, newspaper, or magazine, you read it fairly quickly or read part of it.

ext.ext_cn: 您能看一下我的背吗？我觉得有点儿不对劲。
ext.ext_en: Can you look at my back? I think something's  wrong.

ext.ext_cn: 这辆车最近跑起来一直不是很顺，只好请修理工来看了一下。
ext.ext_en: The car has not been running very well and a mechanic had to come over to have a look at it.

defs.def_en: If someone, especially an expert, looks at something, they examine it, and then deal with it or say how it should be dealt with.

ext.ext_cn: 她认真地看着他说：“你不介意吗？”
ext.ext_en: She looked at him earnestly. 'You don't mind?'

ext.ext_cn: 他面无表情地看了她一眼，仿佛根本不认识她一样。
ext.ext_en: He gave her a blank look, as if he had no idea who she was...

defs.def_en: If you look at someone in a particular way, you look at them with your expression showing what you are feeling or thinking.

ext.ext_cn: 我在找一个小孩。我相信你丈夫可以帮我找到她。
ext.ext_en: I'm looking for a child. I believe your husband can help me find her...

ext.ext_cn: 我去了缅因州找工作。
ext.ext_en: I had gone to Maine looking for a place to work...

defs.def_en: If you look for something, for example something that you have lost, you try to find it.

defs.def_cn: 寻找，寻求，谋求（解决方案或新的方法）

ext.ext_cn: 工作小组将寻求切实可行的方案，以解决医生们遇到的难题。
ext.ext_en: The working group will be looking for practical solutions to the problems faced by doctors...

ext.ext_cn: 他正在想办法摆脱这一纷争。
ext.ext_en: He's looking for a way out from this conflict.

defs.def_en: If you are looking for something such as the solution to a problem or a new method, you want it and are trying to obtain it or think of it.

ext.ext_cn: 下学期咱们会研究二战时期…
ext.ext_en: Next term we'll  be looking at the Second World War period...

ext.ext_cn: 安妮·霍尔克负责权衡你房屋改造的利与弊。
ext.ext_en: Anne Holker looks at the pros and cons of making changes to your property...

defs.def_en: If you look at a subject, problem, or situation, you think about it or study it, so that you know all about it and can perhaps consider what should be done in relation to it.

ext.ext_cn: 布赖恩看她时变得多了一分尊重。
ext.ext_en: Brian had learned to look at her with new respect...

ext.ext_cn: 这要看你怎么看待它。
ext.ext_en: It depends how you look at it.

defs.def_en: If you look at a person, situation, or subject from a particular point of view, you judge them or consider them from that point of view.

defs.def_cn: （用于唤起他人注意）瞧，听着，听我说

ext.ext_cn: 哎，对不起。我不是故意的。
ext.ext_en: Look, I'm sorry. I didn't  mean it...

ext.ext_cn: 现在听好啦，情况眼下是这样的。
ext.ext_en: Now, look, here is how things stand.

defs.def_en: You say look when you want someone to pay attention to you because you are going to say something important.

defs.def_cn: （用于让他人注意令人惊讶、重要或使人厌烦的事）瞧，看看

ext.ext_cn: 嘿，看看都几点啦？咱们晚上再讨论，好不好？
ext.ext_en: Hey, look at the time! We'll talk about it tonight. All right?...

ext.ext_cn: 我是说，你瞧看电视的有多少人，看书的又有几个。
ext.ext_en: I mean, look at how many people watch television and how few read books...

defs.def_en: You can use look to draw attention to a particular situation, person, or thing, for example because you find it very surprising, significant, or annoying.

defs.def_cn: （建筑物、窗户等）面向，朝向对着

ext.ext_cn: 城堡俯瞰一片私家绿地。
ext.ext_en: The castle looks over private parkland...

ext.ext_cn: 家家大门对大门，中间隔着一条窄巷。
ext.ext_en: Each front door looks across a narrow alley to the front door opposite.

defs.def_en: If something such as a building or window looks somewhere, it has a view of a particular place.

ext.ext_cn: 我们没打算大赚一笔。
ext.ext_en: We're not looking to make a fortune.

ext.ext_cn: 生完孩子后打算瘦身的年轻妈妈们
ext.ext_en: ...young mums looking to get fit after having kids.

defs.def_en: If you are looking to do something, you are aiming to do it.

defs.def_cn: 从此一帆风顺；此后蒸蒸日上

ext.ext_cn: 我在儿子亚当出世后开始从事自由职业，自此一帆风顺。
ext.ext_en: I went freelance when my son Adam was born, and have never looked back.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone did something and then never looked back, you mean that they were very successful from that time on.

ext.ext_cn: 他不敢直视她的眼睛。
ext.ext_en: He could not look her in the eye.

defs.def_en: If you look someone in the eye or look them in the face, you look straight at their eyes in a bold and open way, for example in order to make them realize that you are telling the truth.

ext.ext_cn: 法官和政客对警察虐待或杀人之事常常装聋作哑。
ext.ext_en: Judges and politicians routinely looked the other way while people were tortured or killed by police.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone looks the other way, you are critical of them because they pay no attention to something unpleasant that is happening, when they should be dealing with it properly.

defs.def_cn: （尤用于对某人言行感到恼火时）喂，你听我说

ext.ext_cn: 你听我说，蒂姆，你这种反应真的没必要。
ext.ext_en: Now look here, Tim, there really is no need for that kind of reaction.

defs.def_en: You say look here when you are going to say something important to someone, especially when you are angry at what they have done or said.

ext.ext_cn: 卡车冲向大海时，有人大喊“当心！”
ext.ext_en: 'Look out!' somebody shouted, as the truck started to roll toward the sea.

defs.def_en: If you say or shout 'look out!' to someone, you are warning them that they are in danger.

ext.ext_cn: 那个女店员对我上下打量了一番后，叫我不要试穿那条裙子，因为她认为我穿不上。
ext.ext_en: The sales assistant looked me up and down and told me not to try the dress on because she didn't think I would get into it.

defs.def_en: If someone looks you up and down, they direct their eyes from your head to your feet, in a rude and superior way and often as though they disapprove of you.

ext.ext_cn: 希拉看上去愁眉苦脸的。
ext.ext_en: Sheila was looking miserable...

ext.ext_cn: 我要用这笔钱把家里搞得漂漂亮亮的。
ext.ext_en: I shall use the money to make my home look lovely...

defs.def_en: You use look when describing the appearance of a person or thing or the impression that they give.

ext.ext_cn: 她一副遭人遗弃和背叛的样子。
ext.ext_en: She had the look of someone deserted and betrayed...

ext.ext_cn: 装修厨房的时候，肯尼思选择的是一种亲切质朴的田园风格。
ext.ext_en: When he came to decorate the kitchen, Kenneth opted for a friendly rustic look...

defs.def_en: If someone or something has a particular look, they have a particular appearance or expression.

ext.ext_cn: 我从不以貌取人。
ext.ext_en: I never chose people just because of their looks.

ext.ext_cn: 健康、美丽的年轻女子
ext.ext_en: ...a young woman with wholesome good looks.

defs.def_en: When you refer to someone's looks, you are referring to how beautiful or ugly they are, especially how beautiful they are.

ext.ext_cn: 他有很多时间考虑将来，但情况似乎并不乐观。
ext.ext_en: He had lots of time to think about the future, and it didn't look good...

ext.ext_cn: 看来，英国已下决心要派遣一支配备有百余坦克和支援装备的主力部队。
ext.ext_en: Britain looks set to send a major force of over 100 tanks and supporting equipment...

defs.def_en: You use look when indicating what you think will happen in the future or how a situation seems to you.

ext.ext_cn: 外表看来，他不太健康。
ext.ext_en: He was not a well man by the look of him...

ext.ext_cn: 照目前的情况看，斯通先生他们还有的忙。
ext.ext_en: By the look of things, Mr Stone and company will stay busy.

defs.def_en: You use expressions such as by the look of him and by the looks of it when you want to indicate that you are giving an opinion based on the appearance of someone or something.

ext.ext_cn: 看那些云的样子，我觉得可能要下雨。
ext.ext_en: I don't like the look of those clouds.

defs.def_en: If you don't like the look of something or someone, you feel that they may be dangerous or cause problems.
If you ask what someone or something looks like, you are asking for a description of them.
A salt cellar is a small container for salt with a hole or holes in the top for shaking salt onto food.

ext.ext_cn: 720 瓦以下的设备使用3安培的保险丝。
ext.ext_en: Use a 3 amp fuse for equipment up to 720 watts.

ext.ext_cn: 100 瓦的灯泡
ext.ext_en: ...a 100-watt lightbulb.

defs.def_en: A watt is a unit of measurement of electrical power.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (常指在生理上，有时也指在精神上)生病的，有病的

ext.ext_cn: 他病得很厉害，需要药物治疗。
ext.ext_en: He's very sick. He needs medication...

ext.ext_cn: 她发觉自己有两个年幼的孩子和一个有病在身的丈夫，却没钱养活他们。
ext.ext_en: She found herself with two small children, a sick husband, and no money...

defs.def_en: If you are sick, you are ill. Sick usually means physically ill, but it can sometimes be used to mean mentally ill.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 她起身在洗手池里吐了起来。
ext.ext_en: She got up and was sick in the handbasin...

ext.ext_cn: 一想到食物他就恶心。
ext.ext_en: The very thought of food made him feel sick...

defs.def_en: If you are sick, the food that you have eaten comes up from your stomach and out of your mouth. If you feel sick, you feel as if you are going to be sick.
Sick is vomit.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我厌倦了听这些人大发牢骚。
ext.ext_en: I am sick and tired of hearing all these people moaning...

ext.ext_cn: 这儿的大多数人都厌恶暴力。
ext.ext_en: Most people here are sick of violence.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are sick of something or sick and tired of it, you are emphasizing that you are very annoyed by it and want it to stop.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: (笑话、故事等)令人毛骨悚然的，病态的，不健康的

ext.ext_cn: 关于猫的一则令人毛骨悚然的笑话
ext.ext_en: ...a sick joke about a cat...

ext.ext_cn: 那真够吓人的。
ext.ext_en: That's really sick.

defs.def_en: If you describe something such as a joke or story as sick, you mean that it deals with death or suffering in an unpleasantly humorous way.

ext.ext_cn: 一些人屡屡犯罪却从未受到惩戒，这真让我气愤。
ext.ext_en: It makes me sick that people commit offences and never get punished...

ext.ext_cn: 英国新闻界让我很反感。
ext.ext_en: The British press makes me sick.

defs.def_en: If you say that something or someone makes you sick, you mean that they make you feel angry or disgusted.

ext.ext_cn: 我们请病假的时候只能拿一半薪水。
ext.ext_en: When we are off sick, we only receive half pay.

defs.def_en: If you are off sick, you are not at work because you are ill.

ext.ext_cn: 对于我们双方的母亲会说什么他十分担心。
ext.ext_en: He was worried sick about what our mothers would say.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are worried sick, you are emphasizing that you are extremely worried.
Shortcrust pastry is a kind of pastry that is used to make pies and tarts.

ext.ext_cn: 自然现象的科学解释
ext.ext_en: ...scientific explanations of natural phenomena...

ext.ext_cn: 这种形式的非暴力反抗并不是特别新的现象。
ext.ext_en: This form of civil disobedience isn't a particularly new phenomenon.

defs.def_en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 充满活力的；精神饱满的

ext.ext_cn: 她朝气蓬勃，充满活力。
ext.ext_en: She was bouncy and full of energy.

ext.ext_cn: 悦耳、轻快的流行歌曲
ext.ext_en: ...good, bouncy pop songs.

defs.def_en: Someone or something that is bouncy is very lively.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 有许多弹跳玩具的儿童乐园
ext.ext_en: ...a children's paradise filled with bouncy toys.

ext.ext_cn: 婴儿摇椅
ext.ext_en: ...a bouncy chair.

defs.def_en: A bouncy thing can bounce very well or makes other things bounce well.

defs.def_cn: 图书馆馆长；图书馆管理员
defs.def_en: A librarian is a person who is in charge of a library or who has been specially trained to work in a library.

ext.ext_cn: 数世纪以来，媒人一直在犹太人社区扮演着重要角色。
ext.ext_en: The matchmaker has been an important member of Jewish communities for centuries...

ext.ext_cn: 一些朋友牵线搭桥，把我们两个都请去赴宴。
ext.ext_en: Some friends played matchmaker and had us both over to dinner.

defs.def_en: A matchmaker is someone who tries to encourage people they know to form a romantic relationship or to get married.

ext.ext_cn: 工程师注意到管道并没有如预期那样膨胀。
ext.ext_en: Engineers noticed that the pipes were not expanding as expected...

ext.ext_cn: 截至9月，当年的货币供应增加了14.6％。
ext.ext_en: The money supply expanded by 14.6 per cent in the year to September...

defs.def_en: If something expands or is expanded, it becomes larger.

ext.ext_cn: 到19世纪中期，大众制陶业得到了发展。
ext.ext_en: The popular ceramics industry expanded towards the middle of the 19th century...

ext.ext_cn: 利率正在降低，我可以扩大公司或者维持经营。
ext.ext_en: The interest rate's coming down. I'll be able to expand or stay in business...

defs.def_en: If something such as a business, organization, or service expands, or if you expand it, it becomes bigger and includes more people, goods, or activities.

defs.def_cn: 巡回访问;巡回演出；巡回比赛

ext.ext_cn: 乐队目前正在欧洲进行为期两个月的巡回演出。
ext.ext_en: The band are currently on a two-month tour of Europe...

ext.ext_cn: 这将是 22 年来南非首次正式的板球巡回赛。
ext.ext_en: It will be the first official cricket tour of South Africa for 22 years.

defs.def_en: A tour is an organized trip that people such as musicians, politicians, or theatre companies go on to several different places, stopping to meet people or perform.

defs.def_cn: 作巡回活动(或演出、比赛)

ext.ext_cn: 几年前他们在全国作了巡回演出。
ext.ext_en: A few years ago they toured the country in a roadshow...

ext.ext_cn: 他巡回演出了近两年，500场演出场场爆满。
ext.ext_en: He toured for nearly two years and played 500 sell-out shows...

defs.def_en: When people such as musicians, politicians, or theatre companies tour, they go on a tour, for example in order to perform or to meet people.

ext.ext_cn: 那是我在欧洲主要城市游历的第 5 周。
ext.ext_en: It was week five of my tour of the major cities of Europe.

defs.def_en: A tour is a journey during which you visit several places that interest you.

ext.ext_cn: 由导游带领游览苏格兰荒废城堡
ext.ext_en: ...a guided tour of a ruined Scottish castle.

defs.def_en: A tour is a short trip that you make round a place, for example round a historical building, so that you can look at it.

ext.ext_cn: 您也可以乘坐配有视频设备的现代化长途汽车游览那处遗址。
ext.ext_en: You can also tour the site on modern coaches equipped with videos...

ext.ext_cn: 我们游览了米兰的街道。
ext.ext_en: We toured the streets of Milan.

defs.def_en: If you tour a place, you go on a journey or trip round it.

defs.def_cn: （每面通常播放约25分钟的）密纹唱片，LP唱片

ext.ext_cn: 他自1986年以来的首张大碟
ext.ext_en: ...his first LP since 1986.

defs.def_en: An LP is a record which usually has about 25 minutes of music or speech on each side. LP is an abbreviation for (缩略=)'long-playing record'.
A structural engineer is an engineer who works on large structures such as roads, bridges, and large buildings.
Gruel is a food made by boiling oats with water or milk.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我们被藏匿到房间里一个隐蔽的角落。
ext.ext_en: We were tucked away in a secluded corner of the room...

ext.ext_cn: 我们又前行了几英里，发现了一处僻静的海滩。
ext.ext_en: We found a secluded beach a few miles further on.

defs.def_en: A secluded place is quiet and private.
A CD-RW is a CD which is capable of recording sound and images, for example from another CD or from the Internet. CD-R is an abbreviation for (缩略=) 'compact disc rewritable'.

ext.ext_cn: 法国人在从敦克尔刻到杜埃的英吉利海峡沿岸修筑了一系列要塞。
ext.ext_en: The French constructed a series of fortresses from Dunkirk on the Channel coast to Douai...

ext.ext_cn: 这些箱子应该用粗锯木料来做。
ext.ext_en: The boxes should be constructed from rough-sawn timber...

defs.def_en: If you construct something such as a building, road, or machine, you build it or make it.

defs.def_cn: 构想，构筑，构思(思想、作品、体系等)

ext.ext_cn: 你会发现不先把自己的开销记录下来就很难制订支出计划。
ext.ext_en: You will find it difficult to construct a spending plan without first recording your spending...

ext.ext_cn: 他最终构筑起了一个延伸至泰国和新加坡的商业帝国。
ext.ext_en: He eventually constructed a business empire which ran to Thailand and Singapore...

defs.def_en: If you construct something such as an idea, a piece of writing, or a system, you create it by putting different parts together.

defs.def_cn: 复杂的构想(或思想);观念

ext.ext_cn: 影响行动和行为的根本思想(信仰、处世哲学等)
ext.ext_en: ...the underlying constructs (beliefs, philosophy, etc.) which influence action and behaviour...

ext.ext_cn: 这是为奴隶制辩护的同一思想观念的再现。
ext.ext_en: It was a re-enactment of the same mental construct under which slavery was justified.

defs.def_en: A construct is a complex idea.

ext.ext_cn: 随着这轻薄的东西向上飞升，这些人慢慢放出细绳，直到风筝飞到三四千英尺高。
ext.ext_en: As the flimsy constructs soared, the men paid out twine until the kites reached three or four thousand feet...

ext.ext_cn: 这个国家是靠武力和恐吓维系达七十余年的人治政权。
ext.ext_en: The country was an artificial construct held together by force and intimidation for more than 70 years.

defs.def_en: A construct is something that is built, made, or created.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他是个为了正义不知疲倦地工作的人。
ext.ext_en: He was a tireless worker for justice.

ext.ext_cn: 德肋撒修女孜孜不倦帮助穷人的努力
ext.ext_en: ...Mother Teresa's tireless efforts to help the poor.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone or their efforts as tireless, you approve of the fact that they put a lot of hard work into something, and refuse to give up or take a rest.

ext.ext_cn: 一杯茶

defs.def_en: If one person or group does battle with another, they take part in a battle or contest against them. You can also say that two people or groups do battle .
