ext.ext_en: They are stacked neatly in piles of three.

defs.def_en: If you stack a number of things, you arrange them in neat piles.

ext.ext_cn: 如果这个工作真有那么好，你将会赚很多钱。
ext.ext_en: If the job's that good, you'll have stacks of money.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone has stacks of something, you mean that they have a lot of it.

defs.def_cn: 在(某组织机构中)安插(对自己有利的人员)

ext.ext_cn: 他们说将会往法院中安排一些反对堕胎的法官。
ext.ext_en: They said they were going to stack the court with anti-abortion judges...

ext.ext_cn: 该委员会中安插进了几位来自能源生产州的成员。
ext.ext_en: The committee is stacked with members from energy-producing states.

defs.def_en: If someone in authority stacks an organization or body, they fill it with their own supporters so that the decisions it makes will be the ones they want it to make.

ext.ext_cn: 平民难以得到公正的审判。
ext.ext_en: The odds are stacked against civilians getting a fair trial...

ext.ext_cn: 一切好像都对我们不利。
ext.ext_en: Everything seems to be stacked against us.

defs.def_en: If you say that the odds are stacked against someone, or that particular factors are stacked against them, you mean that they are unlikely to succeed in what they want to do because the conditions are not favourable.

ext.ext_cn: 你得拆开这个钻头。
ext.ext_en: You'll have to disassemble the drill.

defs.def_en: To disassemble something means to take it to pieces.
Lateral thinking is a method of solving problems by using your imagination to help you think of solutions that are not obvious at first.

ext.ext_cn: 她穿着白色的连体泳衣。
ext.ext_en: She wore a one-piece white bathing costume.

defs.def_en: A bathing costume is a piece of clothing that is worn for swimming, especially by women and girls.
If pupils or students undergo continuous assessment, they get qualifications partly or entirely based on the work they do during the year, rather than on exam results.

defs.def_cn: 全面质量管理(缩略形式为TQM)

ext.ext_cn: 他是个极力主张全面质量管理的人。
ext.ext_en: He is a firm believer in total quality management.

defs.def_en: Total quality management is a set of management principles aimed at improving performance throughout a company, especially by involving employees in decision-making. The abbreviation TQM is also used.

ext.ext_cn: 在多瑙河上建坝的计划
ext.ext_en: ...plans to build a dam on the Danube River.

ext.ext_cn: 阿斯旺大坝
ext.ext_en: ...the Aswan Dam.

defs.def_en: A dam is a wall that is built across a river in order to stop the water flowing and to make a lake.

ext.ext_cn: 在附近的特拉华河上筑坝的计划
ext.ext_en: ...plans to dam the nearby Delaware River...

ext.ext_cn: 这个水库是通过在布莱斯河上筑坝形成的。
ext.ext_en: This reservoir was formed by damming the River Blith.

defs.def_en: To dam a river means to build a dam across it.
In the breeding of farm animals, an animal's dam is its mother.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 有自我约束力的;能律己的

ext.ext_cn: 多数宗教教导人们要真诚和律己。
ext.ext_en: Most religions teach you to be truthful and self-disciplined.

defs.def_en: Someone who is self-disciplined has the ability to control themselves and to make themselves work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell them what to do.

ext.ext_cn: 我去售酒商店买几瓶威士忌。
ext.ext_en: I'm going to the off-licence to buy some whisky.

defs.def_en: An off-licence is a shop which sells beer, wine, and other alcoholic drinks.

ext.ext_cn: 大多数传统社会都为青春期的孩子举行成人礼。
ext.ext_en: Most traditional societies have transition rites at puberty.

ext.ext_cn: 丰收仪式
ext.ext_en: ...a fertility rite.

defs.def_en: See also:last rites;A rite is a traditional ceremony that is carried out by a particular group or within a particular society.
Rickets is a disease that children can get when their food does not contain enough Vitamin D. It makes their bones soft and causes their liver and spleen to become too large.

ext.ext_cn: 政府必须重建支离破碎的经济。
ext.ext_en: The government must reconstruct the shattered economy...

ext.ext_cn: 他做了整形手术以修复其严重受伤的面部。
ext.ext_en: He had plastic surgery to help reconstruct his badly damaged face...

defs.def_en: If you reconstruct something that has been destroyed or badly damaged, you build it and make it work again.

ext.ext_cn: 她实际上想要重建国家，改造社会。
ext.ext_en: She actually wanted to reconstruct the state and transform society...

ext.ext_cn: 重要的是，要想想在我们自己的社会里如何对这些机构进行改造。
ext.ext_en: It is important to think about how these institutions might be reconstructed in our own societies.

defs.def_en: To reconstruct a system or policy means to change it so that it works in a different way.

defs.def_cn: 使（过去的事件）重现，使再现

ext.ext_cn: 他开始再现1988年12月21日的103次航班失踪事件。
ext.ext_en: He began to reconstruct the events of 21 December 1988, when flight 103 disappeared...

ext.ext_cn: 为重现当时的情景，他们做了大量细致的工作。
ext.ext_en: Elaborate efforts were made to reconstruct what had happened.

defs.def_en: If you reconstruct an event that happened in the past, you try to get a complete understanding of it by combining a lot of small pieces of information.

defs.def_cn: 生产（新产品）；（尤指）出版，推出（图书或CD）

ext.ext_cn: 他当了一辈子新闻记者，如今已出了一本书。
ext.ext_en: A journalist all his life, he's now brought out a book.

defs.def_en: When a person or company brings out a new product, especially a new book or CD, they produce it and put it on sale.

defs.def_cn: 使（某种通常不易显露的行为或情感）显现；激发

ext.ext_cn: 他全身心地投入，最大限度地激发学生的潜能。
ext.ext_en: He is totally dedicated and brings out the best in his pupils.

defs.def_en: Something that brings out a particular kind of behaviour or feeling in you causes you to show it, especially when it is something you do not normally show.

defs.def_cn: 大幅报纸（一般认为是内容较严肃的报纸）
defs.def_en: A broadsheet is a newspaper that is printed on large sheets of paper. Broadsheets are generally considered to be more serious than other newspapers.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 无所顾忌的；肆无忌惮的

ext.ext_cn: 他们在自己的双性恋问题上无所顾忌，毫不为意。
ext.ext_en: They're quite brazen about their bisexuality, it doesn't worry them.

defs.def_en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are very bold and do not care what other people think about them or their behaviour.

ext.ext_cn: 我不知道那个地方的名字。
ext.ext_en: I don't know the name of the place...

ext.ext_cn: 我知道你在二战期间率领一个步枪排。
ext.ext_en: I know that you led a rifle platoon during the Second World War...

defs.def_en: If you know a fact, a piece of information, or an answer, you have it correctly in your mind.

ext.ext_cn: 吉福德是我的一位朋友。我和他认识9年了。
ext.ext_en: Gifford was a friend. I'd known him for nine years...

ext.ext_cn: 你们俩互相认识吗？
ext.ext_en: Do you two know each other?...

defs.def_en: If you know someone, you are familiar with them because you have met them and talked to them before.

ext.ext_cn: 我们听说过这件事，但对详情不是很清楚。
ext.ext_en: We know of the incident but have no further details...

ext.ext_cn: 总统承认据他所知迄今为止还没有反叛者投降。
ext.ext_en: The president admitted that he did not know of any rebels having surrendered so far...

defs.def_en: If you say that you know of something, you mean that you have heard about it but you do not necessarily have a lot of information about it.

ext.ext_cn: 雇佣有经验、了解房地产业的人。
ext.ext_en: Hire someone with experience, someone who knows about real estate...

ext.ext_cn: 虽然她对音乐一无所知，但却爱唱歌。
ext.ext_en: She didn't know anything about music but she liked to sing.

defs.def_en: If you know about a subject, you have studied it or taken an interest in it, and understand part or all of it.

ext.ext_cn: 如果你想读懂一些抒情诗，学点法语和克里奥尔语是有帮助的。
ext.ext_en: It helps to know French and Creole if you want to understand some of the lyrics...

ext.ext_cn: 雷切尔掌握的德语词汇已经和她掌握的英语词汇一样多了。
ext.ext_en: Rachel already knows as many words in German as she does in English...

defs.def_en: If you know a language, you have learned it and can understand it.

ext.ext_cn: 不管你对巴黎多么熟悉，也很容易迷路。
ext.ext_en: No matter how well you know Paris, it is easy to get lost...

ext.ext_cn: 我不了解这部剧，只是来看看。
ext.ext_en: I don't know the play, I've just come to see it.

defs.def_en: If you know something such as a place, a work of art, or an idea, you have visited it, seen it, read it, or heard about it, and so you are familiar with it.

ext.ext_cn: 卫生部门现在知道如何对付这种病了。
ext.ext_en: The health authorities now know how to deal with the disease...

ext.ext_cn: 我们知道如何让它起作用。
ext.ext_en: We know what to do to make it work.

defs.def_en: If you know how to do something, you have the necessary skills and knowledge to do it.

ext.ext_cn: 后来我看到大厅的桌子下有一把枪，我就意识到有些不对劲儿。
ext.ext_en: Then I saw a gun under the hall table so I knew that something was wrong...

ext.ext_cn: 当我从救护车中苏醒过来时才知道发生了什么事。
ext.ext_en: The first I knew about it was when I woke up in the ambulance.

defs.def_en: You can say that someone knows that something is happening when they become aware of it.

ext.ext_cn: 如果她在大街上看到你，能认出你吗？
ext.ext_en: Would she know you if she saw you on the street?...

ext.ext_cn: 我觉得在哪里听过这声音。
ext.ext_en: I thought I knew the voice.

defs.def_en: If you know something or someone, you recognize them when you see them or hear them.

ext.ext_cn: 这种疾病更通俗的名称是疯牛病。
ext.ext_en: The disease is more commonly known as Mad Cow Disease...

ext.ext_cn: 他本名为约翰·伯克斯·吉莱斯皮，但人人都叫他“小迷糊”。
ext.ext_en: He was born as John Birks Gillespie, but everyone knew him as Dizzy...

defs.def_en: If someone or something is known as a particular name, they are called by that name.

ext.ext_cn: 很多人认为她是个非常善良的女人。
ext.ext_en: Lots of people know her as a very kind woman...

ext.ext_cn: 我们认为对性状的这些描述是不准确的，且会使人产生误解。
ext.ext_en: We know them as inaccurate and misleading property descriptions...

defs.def_en: If you know someone or something as a person or thing that has particular qualities, you consider that they have those qualities.

ext.ext_cn: 我们大多数人认识她是因为她曾主持过电视新闻节目。
ext.ext_en: Most of us know her as the woman who used to present the television news...

ext.ext_cn: 那些士兵——我们都视之为邻居的人——站在四周用枪指着我们。
ext.ext_en: The soldiers — all of whom we knew as neighbours — stood around pointing guns at us.

defs.def_en: If you know someone as a person with a particular job or role, you are familiar with them in that job or role, rather than in any other.

defs.def_cn: 现行的；我们熟悉的；我们熟知的

ext.ext_cn: 他计划终止现行的福利制度。
ext.ext_en: He planned to end the welfare system as we know it.

ext.ext_cn: 我们文化中那些构成我们所熟悉的文明社会之根基的价值观
ext.ext_en: ...those values of our culture that are essential to civilisation as we know it.

defs.def_en: If you talk about a thing or system as we know it, you are referring to the form in which it exists now and which is familiar to most people.

ext.ext_cn: 新邻居之间正在互相了解。
ext.ext_en: The new neighbours were getting to know each other...

ext.ext_cn: 我很愿意再次见到你并且更多地了解你。
ext.ext_en: I'd really like to see you again and get to know you better.

defs.def_en: If you get to know someone, you find out what they are like by spending time with them.

ext.ext_cn: “他是谁？”——“天晓得。”
ext.ext_en: 'Who's he?' — 'God knows.'

ext.ext_cn: 老贡嘎会说很多种语言，天晓得有多少种。
ext.ext_en: Old Gunga spoke God knows how many languages...

defs.def_en: People use expressions such as goodness knows ,Heaven knows, and God knows when they do not know something and want to suggest that nobody could possibly know it.

defs.def_cn: （表示同意）我理解，我有同感，我知道

ext.ext_cn: “这个国家太糟糕了。”——“的确是，的确是。”
ext.ext_en: 'This country is so awful.' — 'I know, I know.'

defs.def_en: You say 'I know' to show that you agree with what has just been said.

ext.ext_cn: “有直接从剑桥开出的列车。”——“我知道，但也不快。”
ext.ext_en: 'There are trains straight from Cambridge.' — 'I know, but it's no quicker.'

defs.def_en: You say 'I know' to show that you accept that something is true, but think that it is not very important or relevant.

defs.def_cn: （表示同情和理解）我理解，我知道

ext.ext_cn: 我很遗憾，乔治。我理解你的感受。
ext.ext_en: I'm sorry, George. I know how you feel...

ext.ext_cn: 我知道你正在经受什么样的煎熬。
ext.ext_en: I know what you're going through.

defs.def_en: You use 'I know' to express sympathy and understanding towards someone.

defs.def_cn: 不知道，不认为（表示不完全同意或不认为是真的）

ext.ext_cn: “他就该辞职。”——“我不知道。”
ext.ext_en: 'He should quite simply resign.' — 'I don't know about that.'

ext.ext_cn: 我不认为这对作出决定有丝毫帮助。
ext.ext_en: I don't know that it's made the decision any easier.

defs.def_en: You can use I don't know to indicate that you do not completely agree with something or do not really think that it is true.

defs.def_cn: 我不知道你（们）怎么想（表示将表达自己想法并想知道他人的看法）

ext.ext_cn: 我不知道你们怎么样，但我是饿了。
ext.ext_en: I don't know about the rest of you, but I'm hungry...

ext.ext_cn: 我不知道你怎么想，但我已经受够了。
ext.ext_en: I don't know about you, but I've had just about enough of this.

defs.def_en: You can say 'I don't know about you' to indicate that you are going to give your own opinion about something and you want to find out if someone else feels the same.

defs.def_cn: （表示批评某人的行为）真想不到，真不知道

ext.ext_cn: 真想不到他竟对自己的女儿这样。
ext.ext_en: I don't know how he could do this to his own daughter...

ext.ext_cn: 真想不到你竟说那话。
ext.ext_en: I don't know how you can say that...

defs.def_en: You use I don't know in expressions which indicate criticism of someone's behaviour. For example, if you say that you do not know how someone can do something, you mean that you cannot understand or accept them doing it.

defs.def_cn: 我要是知道就好了；我根本不知道

ext.ext_cn: “那都是关于什么的？”——“我要知道就好了。”
ext.ext_en: 'What was that all about?' — 'Damned if I know.'

ext.ext_cn: 我压根不知道他在那方面有什么计划。
ext.ext_en: I'm damned if I know what plans he has in that direction.

defs.def_en: People sometimes use expressions such as I'm blessed if I know or damned if I know to emphasize the fact that they do not know something.

defs.def_cn: 知情；（尤指）熟悉内幕，掌握内情

ext.ext_cn: 了解重要人物的一些内幕真令人高兴。
ext.ext_en: It was gratifying to be in the know about important people...

ext.ext_cn: 他没有咨询相关知情人士就作了重要的决定。
ext.ext_en: He takes crucial decisions without consulting people in the know.

defs.def_en: If you are in the know about something, especially something that is not known about or understood by many people, you have information about it.

defs.def_cn: （表示所说的话对方理解）你是知道的，你知道我的意思

ext.ext_cn: 我们都没呆太久。我的意思是，气氛并不是——唔，你知道我的意思。
ext.ext_en: None of us stayed long. I mean, the atmosphere wasn't — well, you know what I mean...

ext.ext_cn: 她有点自命不凡，你明白我的意思吧?
ext.ext_en: She was a bit stuck up, know what I mean?

defs.def_en: You can use expressions such as you know what I mean and if you know what I mean to suggest that the person listening to you understands what you are trying to say, and so you do not have to explain any more.

defs.def_cn: （指可能会发生好事）很难说，很难预料

ext.ext_cn: 很难说，我也许会交好运呢。
ext.ext_en: You never know, I might get lucky...

ext.ext_cn: 可能还有个比这还要大的——我觉得有点悬，但也很难说。
ext.ext_en: There might be an even bigger one — I doubt it, but you never know.

defs.def_en: You say 'You never know' or 'One never knows' to indicate that it is not definite or certain what will happen in the future, and to suggest that there is some hope that things will turn out well.

ext.ext_cn: “他结婚了吗？”——“据我所知没有。”
ext.ext_en: 'Is he married?' — 'Not that I know of.'

defs.def_en: You say 'Not that I know of' when someone has asked you whether or not something is true and you think the answer is 'no' but you cannot be sure because you do not know all the facts.

ext.ext_cn: 我怎么知道你会这么突然就回来?
ext.ext_en: How was I to know you'd return so suddenly?...

ext.ext_cn: 你不会知道——实际上，我想我是唯一真正知道的人。
ext.ext_en: You weren't to know — in fact, I think I'm the only person who does know.

defs.def_en: You can say 'How was I to know?', or in British English 'I wasn't to know', to mean that you cannot be blamed or criticized for something you did, because you did not have enough information to realize that it was wrong.

defs.def_cn: （某人）知道什么，懂什么（表示其没有资格评论）

ext.ext_cn: 别听他的，他知道什么？
ext.ext_en: Don't listen to him, what does he know?...

ext.ext_cn: 我感觉他总是那种“你懂什么？”的态度。
ext.ext_en: I always felt his attitude was, 'What do you know about it?'

defs.def_en: You can use expressions such as What does she know? and What do they know? when you think that someone has no right to comment on a situation because they do not understand it.

defs.def_cn: （表示惊讶）你看怪不怪，真没想到

ext.ext_cn: 哎呀，真没想到！
ext.ext_en: Well, what do you know!

defs.def_en: People sometimes say 'What do you know!' when they are very surprised about something.

defs.def_cn: （加强语气或引起注意）你要知道

ext.ext_cn: 你要知道，那里的条件很艰苦。
ext.ext_en: The conditions in there are awful, you know...

ext.ext_cn: 你要知道，这实在让我担心。
ext.ext_en: You know, it does worry me.

defs.def_en: You use you know to emphasize or to draw attention to what you are saying.

defs.def_cn: （表示不确定要说的话或考虑接着说什么）你知道

ext.ext_cn: 他很大方而且，你知道，很友善，很有礼貌。
ext.ext_en: He's generous and, you know, very nice, very polite...

ext.ext_cn: 我想我应该，呃，和你谈谈。
ext.ext_en: I thought I'd, you know, have a chat with you.

defs.def_en: People use you know when they are uncertain about what they are saying or what they are going to say next.

defs.def_cn: （表示进一步解释）你是知道的，你难道不知道

ext.ext_cn: 穿那件白裙，你知道的，上面有黑色刺绣的那件。
ext.ext_en: Wear the white dress, you know, the one with all the black embroidery.

defs.def_en: You use you know when you are trying to explain more clearly what you mean, by referring to something that the person you are talking to knows about.

defs.def_cn: （加强语气）你不知道，你都想不到

ext.ext_cn: 你不知道和家乡来的人说说话感觉有多好。
ext.ext_en: You don't know how good it is to speak to somebody from home.

defs.def_en: You can say 'You don't know' in order to emphasize how strongly you feel about the remark you are going to make.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_en: Someone who is bookish spends a lot of time reading serious books.

ext.ext_cn: 它长约1米。
ext.ext_en: It is about a metre in length.

ext.ext_cn: 鱼的身长
ext.ext_en: ...the length of the fish...

defs.def_en: The length of something is the amount that it measures from one end to the other along the longest side.

ext.ext_cn: 一百多页厚的书
ext.ext_en: ...a book of at least 100 pages in length...

ext.ext_cn: 段落的长短取决于它所传达的信息量。
ext.ext_en: The length of a paragraph depends on the information it conveys.

defs.def_en: The length of something such as a piece of writing is the amount of writing that is contained in it.

ext.ext_cn: 每一阶段的确切时长可能会有所不同。
ext.ext_en: The exact length of each period may vary...

ext.ext_cn: 他这部片长逾两个小时的电影对家庭生活进行了巧妙的剖析。
ext.ext_en: His film, over two hours in length, is a subtle study of family life.

defs.def_en: The length of an event, activity, or situation is the period of time from beginning to end for which something lasts or during which something happens.

defs.def_cn: （绳、布、木头等的）一段，一节，一截

ext.ext_cn: 一根30英尺长的绳子
ext.ext_en: ...a 30ft length of rope...

ext.ext_cn: 你可以在玻璃后面挂几条织品。
ext.ext_en: You can hang lengths of fabric behind the glass.

defs.def_en: A length of rope, cloth, wood, or other material is a piece of it that is intended to be used for a particular purpose or that exists in a particular situation.

ext.ext_cn: 他居然花了那么长时间才拿定主意，许多人都对此感到吃惊。
ext.ext_en: Many have been surprised at the length of time it has taken him to make up his mind...

ext.ext_cn: 我也注意到她的手指很长。
ext.ext_en: I noticed, too, the length of her fingers.

defs.def_en: The length of something is its quality of being long.

ext.ext_cn: 我每天游20个来回。
ext.ext_en: I swim 40 lengths a day.

defs.def_en: If you swim a length in a swimming pool, you swim the distance from one end to the other.

defs.def_cn: （赛艇中的）艇位；（赛马中的）马位，马身长度

ext.ext_en: It is wise to start infilling with a layer of gravel for drainage.

ext.ext_en: There is room for infill between the new outer suburbs.

ext.ext_cn: 看看我的新上衣。
ext.ext_en: Look at my new top.

defs.def_en: A top is a piece of clothing that you wear on the upper half of your body, for example a blouse or shirt.

ext.ext_en: The vehicles have a top speed of 80 kilometres per hour.

defs.def_en: You can use top to indicate that something or someone is at the highest level of a scale or measurement.

ext.ext_en: For $50, the guests got three courses of top nosh, fizz, wine, and beer.

defs.def_en: You can use top to say that you think something is excellent.

defs.def_cn: 最高层;最高地位(或职位)

ext.ext_en: We started from the bottom and we had to work our way up to the top.

ext.ext_en: ...his dramatic rise to the top of the military hierarchy.

defs.def_en: The top of an organization or career structure is the highest level in it.

ext.ext_en: So you want to be a top model…

ext.ext_cn: 总统今天下午会见了他最得力的军事顾问。
ext.ext_en: The President met this afternoon with his top military advisers...

ext.ext_cn: 工党以 46% 的得票数高居首位。
ext.ext_en: Labour was top of the poll with forty-six percent.

defs.def_en: If someone is at the top of a table or league or is the top of the table or league, their performance is better than that of all the other people involved.

ext.ext_en: Cleaning up the water supply is their top priority...

ext.ext_en: On arrival, a six-course meal was top of the agenda.

defs.def_en: You can use top to indicate that something is the first thing you are going to do, because you consider it to be the most important.

ext.ext_en: He was Italy's top scorer during the World Cup matches...

ext.ext_en: Management consultancy was the top choice of career among 11,500 students in a survey this year…

defs.def_en: You can use top to indicate that someone does a particular thing more times than anyone else or that something is chosen more times than anything else.

defs.def_en: To top a list means to be mentioned or chosen more times than anyone or anything else.

ext.ext_en: Imports topped £10 billion last month...

ext.ext_cn: 这 5 所学校的成绩在该州居前 5%，其中一所的成绩高于全州所有其他学校。

defs.def_en: If something tops a particular amount, it is larger than that amount.

ext.ext_en: The publisher expected the book to sell 1,500 copies, tops...

ext.ext_en: The United States was tops in finance and services…

defs.def_en: If you say that something is tops or is the tops, you mean that it is better or more successful than anything else.

ext.ext_en: Belatedly, the government has acknowledged the problem...

defs.def_en: She'll is the usual spoken form of 'she will'.

ext.ext_cn: 现在专家们都在赞美其貌不扬的马铃薯的种种好处。
ext.ext_en: Now experts are extolling the virtues of the humble potato...

ext.ext_cn: 他们不停地赞美我的管理技能。
ext.ext_en: They kept extolling my managerial skills.

defs.def_en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

ext.ext_cn: 他在罗马学习了古典建筑学和设计。
ext.ext_en: He studied classical architecture and design in Rome.

defs.def_en: Architecture is the art of planning, designing, and constructing buildings.

ext.ext_cn: 现代建筑式样
ext.ext_en: ...modern architecture.

ext.ext_cn: 摩洛哥建筑风格的典范
ext.ext_en: ...a fine example of Moroccan architecture.

defs.def_en: The architecture of a building is the style in which it is designed and constructed.

ext.ext_cn: 现代社会处于崩溃边缘的知识结构
ext.ext_en: ...the crumbling intellectual architecture of modern society.

ext.ext_cn: 肌肉纤维的结构
ext.ext_en: ...the architecture of muscle fibres.

defs.def_en: The architecture of something is its structure.

ext.ext_cn: 货车又开始颠簸起来。
ext.ext_en: The wagon jolted again...

ext.ext_cn: 火车猛地一颠，开动了。
ext.ext_en: The train jolted into motion...

defs.def_en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

defs.def_cn: 使震惊；使惊慌；使慌乱不安

ext.ext_cn: 火辣辣的一巴掌打在脸上，她惊呆了。
ext.ext_en: A stinging slap across the face jolted her...

ext.ext_cn: 亨德森听到这个消息一时目瞪口呆。
ext.ext_en: Henderson was momentarily jolted by the news.

defs.def_en: If something jolts someone, it gives them an unpleasant surprise or shock.

defs.def_cn: （采取戏剧、海报等艺术形式以进一步达到政治目的的）宣传鼓动
defs.def_en: Agit-prop is the use of artistic forms such as drama or posters to further political aims.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他们登上铺着俗艳的紫色地毯的楼梯。
ext.ext_en: They climbed the garish purple-carpeted stairs.

ext.ext_cn: 餐馆花哨的烫金招牌
ext.ext_en: ...the restaurant's garish, illuminated signs.

defs.def_en: You describe something as garish when you dislike it because it is very bright in an unattractive, showy way.
Woodworm are very small creatures which make holes in wood by eating it.

defs.def_cn: （尤指房子木建部分或家具的）木蛀虫害，木蠹虫害

ext.ext_cn: 处理房子一层的木蛀虫害
ext.ext_en: ...treating the ground floor of a house for woodworm.

defs.def_en: Woodworm is damage caused to wood, especially to the wooden parts of a house or to furniture, by woodworm making holes in the wood.
A telephonist is someone who works at a telephone exchange or whose job is to answer the telephone for a business or other organization.

ext.ext_cn: 有段时间，他考虑去当军医。
ext.ext_en: For a time he contemplated a career as an army medical doctor...

ext.ext_cn: 她考虑为了孩子而离开。
ext.ext_en: She contemplates leaving for the sake of the kids.

defs.def_en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

defs.def_cn: 深思熟虑;沉思;苦思冥想

ext.ext_cn: 那天晚上，他躺在医院的病床上，想到未来，他哭了起来。
ext.ext_en: As he lay in his hospital bed that night, he cried as he contemplated his future...

ext.ext_cn: 那让人难以认真思考这个可能，即目前的政策也许并不能持续下去。
ext.ext_en: That makes it difficult to contemplate the idea that the present policy may not be sustainable.

defs.def_en: If you contemplate an idea or subject, you think about it carefully for a long time.

ext.ext_cn: 他盯着自己的双手，眉头紧锁。
ext.ext_en: He contemplated his hands, still frowning.

defs.def_en: If you contemplate something or someone, you look at them for a long time.

ext.ext_cn: 在希腊神话里，主神宙斯化作天鹅引诱了勒达。
ext.ext_en: In Greek mythology, the god Zeus took the form of a swan to seduce Leda...

ext.ext_cn: 这一点在很多文化的神话故事里都得到了充分的证明。
ext.ext_en: This is well illustrated in the mythologies of many cultures.

defs.def_en: Mythology is a group of myths, especially all the myths from a particular country, religion,  or culture.

ext.ext_cn: 奥尔特曼戳穿了电影产业的虚伪面具以及普遍存在的一些错误认识，揭露了其作为一个产业，跟其他任何一个产业都一样。
ext.ext_en: Altman strips away the pretence and mythology to expose the film industry as a business like any other.

defs.def_en: You can use mythology to refer to the beliefs or opinions that people have about something, when you think that they are false or untrue.

ext.ext_cn: 他的体格和精力比得上年龄只有他一半大的人。
ext.ext_en: He has the physique and energy of a man half his age.

ext.ext_cn: 体格强壮的男子
ext.ext_en: ...men of powerful physique.

defs.def_en: Someone's physique is the shape and size of their body.

ext.ext_cn: 低于要价15％的报价不大可能被接受。
ext.ext_en: Offers 15% below the asking price are unlikely to be accepted.

defs.def_en: The asking price of something is the price which the person selling it says that they want for it, although they may accept less.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 无法辨认的；无法识别的

ext.ext_cn: 听不清的狂呼乱喊声
ext.ext_en: ...unidentifiable howling noises...

ext.ext_cn: 所有的尸体都完全无法辨认。
ext.ext_en: All the bodies were totally unidentifiable.

defs.def_en: If something or someone is unidentifiable, you are not able to say exactly what it is or who they are.

ext.ext_cn: 该计划遭受了一个打击。
ext.ext_en: The schedule has suffered a knockback...

ext.ext_cn: 我一定已经打过100多个电话了，而且还没遭到过拒绝。
ext.ext_en: I must have made more than 100 phone calls and I didn't get a single knockback.

defs.def_en: A knockback is a problem or a rejection which delays your progress or which reverses some of the progress you have made.

ext.ext_cn: 我们恳求政府不要削减这项预算。
ext.ext_en: We beg the Government on bended knees not to cut this budget.

defs.def_en: If you ask someone for something on bended knee, you ask them very seriously for it.

ext.ext_cn: 粗麻布袋子
ext.ext_en: ...a burlap sack.

defs.def_en: Burlap is a thick, rough fabric that is used for making sacks.

ext.ext_cn: 贸易失衡可能会在1990年再次加剧。因此需要很快采取一系列新的政策行动。
ext.ext_en: The trade imbalance is likely to rise again in 1990. Hence a new set of policy actions will be required soon...

ext.ext_cn: 任何隐藏的东西都是有害的（所以披露就等于安全）。
ext.ext_en: Whatever is hidden is harmful (hence revelation equals security)...

defs.def_en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.

ext.ext_cn: 可能正导致地球变暖的那些气体，其主要影响将在多年后显现。
ext.ext_en: The gases that may be warming the planet will have their main effect many years hence.

ext.ext_cn: 计划5个月后部署完毕的更大规模的维和部队
ext.ext_en: ...the much larger peacekeeping force that is meant to be fully deployed five months hence.

defs.def_en: You use hence in expressions such as 'several years hence' or 'six months hence' to refer to a time in the future, especially a long time in the future.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他有本事连续几个小时一动不动，像雕塑一样。
ext.ext_en: He has this ability of being able to remain as motionless as a statue, for hours on end...

ext.ext_cn: 她双手静止不动。
ext.ext_en: Her hands were motionless...

defs.def_en: Someone or something that is motionless is not moving at all.

ext.ext_cn: 他在 1970 年自己 50 岁生日时退了休。
ext.ext_en: He retired in 1970, on his fiftieth birthday.

defs.def_en: The fiftieth item in a series is the one that you count as number fifty.

defs.def_cn: 为减轻罪责；为从轻处置；为了开脱

ext.ext_cn: 御用大律师基兰·库南对法官说这些罪行情节较轻，希望能够从宽判决。
ext.ext_en: Kieran Coonan QC told the judge in mitigation that the offences had been at the lower end of the scale...

ext.ext_cn: 作为开脱的理由也罢，应该指出酿造举世无双的葡萄酒并没有什么实际的好处。
ext.ext_en: In mitigation, it should be pointed out that there wasn't much incentive to make world-beating wine.

defs.def_en: If someone, especially in a court, is told something in mitigation, they are told something that makes a crime or fault easier to understand and excuse.

ext.ext_cn: 身心状况的缓和或痊愈
ext.ext_en: ...the mitigation or cure of a physical or mental condition.

defs.def_en: Mitigation is a reduction in the unpleasantness, seriousness, or painfulness of something.

ext.ext_cn: 当他们开始对开战表示不满时，我很恼火。
ext.ext_en: It pisses me off when they start moaning about going to war.

defs.def_en: If someone or something pisses you off, they annoy you.

defs.def_cn: （对政策、事业、信仰等的）支持，拥护

ext.ext_cn: 斯洛文尼亚领导层对广受欢迎的改革事业和民族主义信念的支持
ext.ext_en: ...the Slovene leadership's espousal of the popular causes of reform and nationalism.

defs.def_en: A government's or person's espousal of a particular policy, cause, or belief is their strong support of it.

ext.ext_cn: 他长得像圣诞老人。
ext.ext_en: He looks like Father Christmas...

ext.ext_cn: 凯茜是个很好的伙伴，我们亲如姐妹。
ext.ext_en: Kathy is a great mate, we are like sisters...

defs.def_en: If you say that one person or thing is like another, you mean that they share some of the same qualities or features.

ext.ext_cn: 保加利亚是个怎样的地方？
ext.ext_en: What was Bulgaria like?...

ext.ext_cn: 她长什么样子？
ext.ext_en: What did she look like?...

defs.def_en: If you talk about what something or someone is like, you are talking about their qualities or features.

ext.ext_cn: 过去12年里，纽约等大城市受到了极大的冷遇。
ext.ext_en: The neglect that large cities like New York have received over the past 12 years is tremendous...

ext.ext_cn: 他能用法语说“我们去开车吧”或“我们去散步吧”之类的话。
ext.ext_en: He could say things like, 'Let's go to the car' or 'Let us go for a walk' in French.

defs.def_en: You can use like to introduce an example of the set of things or people that you have just mentioned.

ext.ext_cn: 它也打动了那些像我一样年纪太轻而没有经历过战争的人。
ext.ext_en: It also moved those who, like me, are too young to have lived through the war...

ext.ext_cn: 像德国很多城市一样，它不得不在第二次世界大战后进行重建。
ext.ext_en: Like many cities in Germany, it had to recreate itself after the second world war.

defs.def_en: You can use like to say that someone or something is in the same situation as another person or thing.

defs.def_cn: （表示行为如同…一样）像孩子一样哭泣/像老鹰一样监视

ext.ext_cn: 我像风中的落叶一样浑身发抖。
ext.ext_en: I was shaking all over, trembling like a  leaf...

ext.ext_cn: 格林菲尔德表现得像一个不负责任的白痴。
ext.ext_en: Greenfield was behaving like an irresponsible idiot.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is behaving like something or someone else, you mean that they are behaving in a way that is typical of that kind of thing or person. Like is used in this way in many fixed expressions, for example to cry like a baby and to watch someone like a hawk.

defs.def_cn: （表示行为符合…的特点）她就是这么个人/这一点也不像他

ext.ext_cn: 你应该早告诉我们的。不过你就是这么个人，把事情都藏在心里。
ext.ext_en: You should have told us. But it's just like you not to share...

ext.ext_cn: 他为什么要做这样的傻事呢？这可一点都不像他。
ext.ext_en: Why does he want to do a mad thing like that? It's not like him.

defs.def_en: You can use like in expressions such as that's just like her and it wasn't like him to indicate that the person's behaviour is or is not typical of their character.

defs.def_cn: 好像，似乎（但事实并非如此）（一些人认为此用法不正确）

ext.ext_cn: 他的胳膊看起来好像不堪手套重负要折断了一样。
ext.ext_en: His arms look like they might snap under the weight of his gloves...

ext.ext_cn: 坐在开往滑铁卢的火车上，我觉得自己好像正踏上一趟冒险旅程。
ext.ext_en: On the train up to Waterloo, I felt like I was going on an adventure.

defs.def_en: Like is sometimes used as a conjunction in order to say that something appears to be the case when it is not. Some people consider this use to be incorrect.

defs.def_cn: 如同（一些人认为此用法不正确）

ext.ext_cn: 人们在闲逛，给孩子们买冰激凌，就像每个星期天一样。
ext.ext_en: People are strolling, buying ice cream for their children, just like they do every Sunday...

ext.ext_cn: 他的话跟我的一模一样。
ext.ext_en: He spoke exactly like I did...

defs.def_en: Like is sometimes used as a conjunction in order to indicate that something happens or is done in the same way as something else. Some people consider this use to be incorrect.

defs.def_cn: （用于否定短语中强调以…为最）没有什么能比得上它/没有什么地方能比得上它

ext.ext_cn: 再没什么比烛光更能营造浪漫气氛了。
ext.ext_en: There's nothing like candlelight for creating a romantic mood...

ext.ext_cn: 天底下没有比这更好的感觉了。
ext.ext_en: There was no feeling like it in the world.

defs.def_en: You can use like in negative expressions such as nothing like it and no place like it to emphasize that there is nothing as good as the situation, thing, or person mentioned.

ext.ext_cn: 3亿美元远远不够。
ext.ext_en: Three hundred million dollars will be nothing like enough...

ext.ext_cn: 根本不像表面上看起来这么糟糕。
ext.ext_en: It's really not anything like as bad as it looks.

defs.def_en: You can use like in expressions such as nothing like to make an emphatic negative statement.

defs.def_cn: （表示思考下面的话或用作口头禅）嗯，这个（一些人不喜欢此用法）

ext.ext_cn: 我决定我要去，嗯，拍一张他的冲凉照。
ext.ext_en: I decided that I'd go and, like, take a picture of him while he was in the shower.

defs.def_en: Some people say like when they are thinking about what to say next or because it has become their habit to say it. Some people do not like this use.

defs.def_cn: （用于重述自己或他人当时的话或自己当时的想法）说，想（一些人不喜欢此用法）

ext.ext_cn: 他说，“我对你有好感。”我当时的反应是，“你开玩笑的吧！”
ext.ext_en: He said 'I'm attracted to you.' I'm like 'You're  kidding!'

ext.ext_cn: 我爸爸当时在那儿，就说，“对，对，我想来。”
ext.ext_en: My dad was there and he's like: 'Yeah. Yeah. I want to come.'

defs.def_en: Some people say like when they are reporting what they or another person said, or what they thought about something. Some people do not like this use.

ext.ext_cn: 他喜欢棒球。
ext.ext_en: He likes baseball...

ext.ext_cn: 我不明白为什么格雷丝不喜欢我。
ext.ext_en: I can't  think why Grace doesn't like me...

defs.def_en: If you like something or someone, you think they are interesting, enjoyable, or attractive.

ext.ext_cn: 你觉得美国怎么样？
ext.ext_en: How do you like America?...

ext.ext_cn: 这趟旅行感觉如何？
ext.ext_en: How did you like the trip?

defs.def_en: If you ask someone how they like something, you are asking them for their opinion of it and whether they enjoy it or find it pleasant.

ext.ext_cn: 我翻过那本烹饪书。我喜欢它的版式设计。
ext.ext_en: I've been looking at the cookery book. I like the way it is set out...

ext.ext_cn: 美国政府希望看到战争能以和谈方式解决。
ext.ext_en: The US administration would like to see a negotiated settlement to the war...

defs.def_en: If you like something such as a particular course of action or way of behaving, you approve of it.

ext.ext_cn: 我习惯早早地赶到机场。
ext.ext_en: I like to get to airports in good time...

ext.ext_cn: 我听说玛丽的丈夫希望她6点前就回到家里。
ext.ext_en: I hear Mary's husband likes her to be home no later than six o'clock.

defs.def_en: If you say that you like to do something or that you like something to be done, you mean that you prefer to do it or prefer it to be done as part of your normal life or routine.

ext.ext_cn: 我想洗个澡。
ext.ext_en: I'd like a bath...

ext.ext_cn: 如果你不介意的话，我想我要回家了。
ext.ext_en: If you don't mind, I think I'd like to go home.

defs.def_en: If you say that you would like something or would like to do something, you are indicating a wish or desire that you have.

ext.ext_cn: 我想道歉。
ext.ext_en: I'd like to apologize...

ext.ext_cn: 我想借此机会向您介绍我们推出的一项新服务。
ext.ext_en: I would like to take this opportunity of telling you about a new service which we are offering.

defs.def_en: You can say that you would like to say something to indicate that you are about to say it.

ext.ext_cn: 这是找您的钱。您需要一个袋子吗？
ext.ext_en: Here's your change. Would you like a bag?...

ext.ext_cn: 也许在您等候时，您可以去酒吧喝点东西。
ext.ext_en: Perhaps while you wait you would like a drink at the bar...

defs.def_en: If you ask someone if they would like something or would like to do something, you are making a polite offer or invitation.

ext.ext_cn: 我希望有人能解释一下。
ext.ext_en: I'd like an explanation...

ext.ext_cn: 请您四处看看，告诉我们是不是缺了什么东西。
ext.ext_en: We'd like you to look around and tell us if anything is missing...

defs.def_en: If you say to someone that you would like something or you would like them to do something, or ask them if they would like to do it, you are politely telling them what you want or what you want them to do.

defs.def_cn: 同样（或相似）的人（或事物）

ext.ext_cn: 你必须确保是在进行同类比较。
ext.ext_en: You have to make sure you're comparing like with like...

ext.ext_cn: 顺势疗法是基于“以毒攻毒”的原理。
ext.ext_en: Homeopathic treatment is based on the 'like cures like' principle.

defs.def_en: You can use like in expressions such as like attracts like, when you are referring to two or more people or things that have the same or similar characteristics.

ext.ext_cn: 我原以为我了解杰玛的一切：她的好恶爱憎，她的政治观点。
ext.ext_en: I thought that I knew everything about Jemma: her likes and dislikes, her political viewpoints.

defs.def_en: Someone's  likes are the things that they enjoy or find pleasant.

ext.ext_cn: 很多学生还通过慢跑、有氧体操、负重训练等方式来健身。
ext.ext_en: Many students are also keeping fit through jogging, aerobics, weight training, and the like.

defs.def_en: If you mention particular things or people and then add and the like, you are indicating that there are other similar things or people that can be included in what you are saying.

defs.def_cn: （用于非正式地提出或同意建议）如果你乐意的话

ext.ext_cn: 如果你愿意，可以呆在这里。
ext.ext_en: You can stay here if you like...

ext.ext_cn: “我们不说她了好不好？”——“听你的。”
ext.ext_en: 'Shall we stop talking about her?' —  'If you like.'

defs.def_en: You say if you like when you are making or agreeing to an offer or suggestion in a casual way.

ext.ext_cn: 这更像是首付，也可以说是定金。
ext.ext_en: This is more like a downpayment, or a deposit, if you like.

defs.def_en: You say if you like when you are expressing something in a different way, or in a way that you think some people might disagree with or find strange.

ext.ext_cn: 他眼下正在拼命地工作。
ext.ext_en: He's  working like mad at the moment.

defs.def_en: You can use the expressions like anything ,like crazy, or like mad to emphasize that someone is doing something or something is happening in a very energetic or noticeable way.

ext.ext_cn: 像她那样的人为什么要跟我这样的人共度一个晚上呢？
ext.ext_en: Why would somebody like her want to spend an evening with the likes of me?...

ext.ext_cn: 她去了剑桥，交往的都是像萧伯纳这样的人物。
ext.ext_en: She went to Cambridge and rubbed shoulders with the likes of George Bernard Shaw.

defs.def_en: You can talk about the likes of someone or something to refer to people or things of a particular type.

ext.ext_cn: 他们会来的，也许还会带邻居来。
ext.ext_en: They'd come and bring their neighbours, like as not.

defs.def_en: If you say that something will happen like as not or as like as not, you mean that it will probably happen.

ext.ext_cn: 不管我们愿不愿意，家庭环境会影响我们人生的发展方向，使我们变成现在的样子。
ext.ext_en: Like it or not, our families shape our lives and make us what we are...

ext.ext_cn: 喜欢也好，不喜欢也罢，我们今晚要在这里过夜了。
ext.ext_en: We're going to have to spend the night here whether we like it or not.

defs.def_en: If you say that something will happen or is true like it or not, or whether someone likes it or not, you mean that although the situation may be unpleasant, it has to be faced.

defs.def_cn: （用于展示过程）像这样/像那样/照这样

ext.ext_cn: 这个能开能关，就像这样。
ext.ext_en: It opens and closes, like this.

defs.def_en: You say like this ,like that, or like so when you are showing someone how something is done.

defs.def_cn: （用于吸引注意力）像这样/像那样

ext.ext_cn: 很抱歉这样来打扰你。
ext.ext_en: I'm sorry to intrude on you like this...

ext.ext_cn: 别再那样走来走去了。
ext.ext_en: Stop pacing like that.

defs.def_en: You use like this or like that when you are drawing attention to something that you are doing or that someone else is doing.

ext.ext_cn: 这是公司的建议——嗯，更确切地说是命令。
ext.ext_en: It's  on company advice — well, orders, more like.

defs.def_en: You use the expression more like when mentioning an amount, name, or description that in your opinion is more accurate than one that has already been mentioned.

ext.ext_cn: 他们一年能挣到3,000英镑左右。
ext.ext_en: They can get something like £3,000 a year...

ext.ext_cn: “大概会在什么时候？星期一？”——“差不多吧。”
ext.ext_en: 'When roughly would this be? Monday?' — 'Something like that.'

defs.def_en: You use the expression something like with an amount, number, or description to indicate that it is approximately accurate.

ext.ext_cn: 这才对了嘛，你现在慢慢开始熟悉情况了。
ext.ext_en: That's more like it, you're getting into the swing of things now.

defs.def_en: If you say that's more like it, you mean that the thing that you are referring to is more satisfactory than it was on earlier occasions.

defs.def_cn: 前所未有（或闻所未闻）的事物

ext.ext_cn: 只存在于前人梦想中的惊人科技进步
ext.ext_en: ...technological advances the like of which the world had previously only dreamed of...

ext.ext_cn: 我们面临的疫情规模在本世纪尚属空前。
ext.ext_en: We are dealing with an epidemic the likes of which we have never seen in this century.

defs.def_en: If you refer to something the like of which or the likes of which has never been seen before, you are emphasizing how important, great, or noticeable the thing is.

defs.def_cn: 非常想得到;为…不惜一切代价

ext.ext_cn: 她有一份我们大多数人都非常眼热的工作。
ext.ext_en: She has the job most of us would give our eye teeth for.

defs.def_en: If you say that you would give your eye teeth for something, you mean that you want it very much and you would do anything to get it.

ext.ext_cn: 我正在努力忘掉这一切。
ext.ext_en: I'm trying to clear my mind of all this...

ext.ext_cn: 在他看来，这个人无疑是认真的。
ext.ext_en: There was no doubt in his mind that the man was serious...

defs.def_en: You refer to someone's mind when talking about their thoughts. For example, if you say that something is in your mind, you mean that you are thinking about it, and if you say that something is at the back of your mind, you mean that you are aware of it, although you are not thinking about it very much.

defs.def_cn: 头脑，大脑(指思考和推理的能力)

ext.ext_cn: 你有聪明的头脑。
ext.ext_en: You have a good mind...

ext.ext_cn: 学习拓展了我的思路，启发我去思考问题。
ext.ext_en: Studying stretched my mind and got me thinking about things.

defs.def_en: Your mind is your ability to think and reason.

ext.ext_cn: 安德鲁，你太多疑了。
ext.ext_en: Andrew, you have a very suspicious mind...

ext.ext_cn: 他成功的关键在于他擅长逻辑思维。
ext.ext_en: The key to his success is his logical mind.

defs.def_en: If you have a particular type of mind, you have a particular way of thinking which is part of your character, or a result of your education or professional training.

defs.def_cn: 有才智的人;富有想象力的人;精英

ext.ext_cn: 她搬到了伦敦，遇见了她那个时代最有头脑的一些人。
ext.ext_en: She moved to London, meeting some of the best minds of her time.

defs.def_en: You can refer to someone as a particular kind of mind as a way of saying that they are clever, intelligent, or imaginative.

ext.ext_cn: 要牢记一点：在比较偏远的地方加油站很少见。
ext.ext_en: Bear in mind that petrol stations are scarce in the more remote areas...

ext.ext_cn: 想到她所属的那个党派，我对她的一些评论并不感到惊讶。
ext.ext_en: I should not be surprised about some of her comments, bearing in mind the party she belongs to.

defs.def_en: If you tell someone to bear something in mind or to keep something in mind, you are reminding or warning them about something important which they should remember.

ext.ext_cn: 那使我记起了里奥金的一首很赞的诗。
ext.ext_en: That brings to mind a wonderful poem by Riokin...

ext.ext_cn: 许多英国设计师的命运令人想起了龟兔赛跑的故事。
ext.ext_en: The fate of many British designers calls to mind the fable of the tortoise and the hare.

defs.def_en: If something brings another thing to mind or calls another thing to mind, it makes you think of that other thing, usually because it is similar in some way.

ext.ext_cn: 回想一下1978年福里斯特赢得冠军称号的时候。
ext.ext_en: Cast your mind back to 1978, when Forest won the title.

defs.def_en: If you cast your mind back to a time in the past, you think about what happened then.

defs.def_cn: 对…不予考虑;对…置若罔闻

ext.ext_cn: 她不再去想去年遭受的创伤。
ext.ext_en: She has closed her mind to last year's traumas.

defs.def_en: If you close your mind to something, you deliberately do not think about it or pay attention to it.

ext.ext_cn: 我原本准备投他的票，后来却改变了主意，把票投给了里根。
ext.ext_en: I was going to vote for him, but I changed my mind and voted for Reagan...

ext.ext_cn: 她很年轻，对于自己想要做的事情也许会改变主意。
ext.ext_en: She's very young. She might change her mind about what she wants to do...

defs.def_en: If you change your mind, or if someone or something changes your mind, you change a decision you have made or an opinion that you had.

defs.def_cn: 突然想起;(想法)一下子冒出来

ext.ext_cn: 谈到这个人的时候自然会想起“正直”、“诚实”这样的字眼。
ext.ext_en: Integrity and honesty are words that spring to mind when talking of the man.

defs.def_en: If something comes to mind or springs to mind, you think of it without making any effort.

defs.def_cn: (想法)掠过心头，被想到，进入脑海

ext.ext_cn: 他从未想过可能会有问题存在。
ext.ext_en: It had never crossed his mind that there might be a problem...

ext.ext_cn: 我的确想过有失败的可能。
ext.ext_en: The possibility of failure did cross my mind.

defs.def_en: If you say that an idea or possibility never crossed your mind, you mean that you did not think of it.

ext.ext_cn: 他能在脑海里想象出将会达到的效果。
ext.ext_en: In his mind's eye, he can imagine the effect he's having.

defs.def_en: If you see something in your mind's eye, you imagine it and have a clear picture of it in your mind.

ext.ext_cn: 警卫队长看上去似乎想向他们挑战。
ext.ext_en: The captain of the guard looked as if he had a mind to challenge them...

ext.ext_cn: 如果他们愿意的话，可以那样理解。
ext.ext_en: They could interpret it that way if they'd a mind to.

defs.def_en: If you have a mind to do something, you want, intend, or choose to do it.

defs.def_cn: 很想做(作为一种警告或声明，实际很可能不会做)

ext.ext_cn: 他还在大发脾气，叫嚷着真想辞职不干了。
ext.ext_en: He raged on about how he had a good mind to resign.

defs.def_en: If you say that you have a good mind to do something or have half a mind to do it, you are threatening or announcing that you have a strong desire to do it, although you probably will not do it.

ext.ext_cn: “也许今晚我们可以庆祝一下。”——“你有何打算？”
ext.ext_en: 'Maybe we could celebrate tonight.' — 'What did you have in mind?'

defs.def_en: If you ask someone what they have in mind, you want to know in more detail about an idea or wish they have.

ext.ext_cn: 柯林斯·哈维尔公司打算出版一本帕斯捷尔纳克的小诗集。
ext.ext_en: Collins Harvill had it in mind to publish a short volume about Pasternak.

defs.def_en: If you have it in mind to do something, you intend or want to do it.

defs.def_cn: 以…为目标(或理由、基础);考虑到

ext.ext_cn: 这些家庭需要帮助。为此35位专家组成的小组上周末会面进行了商谈。
ext.ext_en: These families need support. With this in mind a group of 35 specialists met last weekend.

defs.def_en: If you do something with a particular thing in mind, you do it with that thing as your aim or as the reason or basis for your action.

defs.def_cn: (疾病等)只是凭空想象的，完全由心理引起的

ext.ext_cn: 它可能是种病毒性疾病，也可能纯属心理作用。
ext.ext_en: It could be a virus, or it could be all in the mind.

defs.def_en: If you say that something such as an illness is all in the mind, you mean that it relates to someone's feelings or attitude, rather than having any physical cause.
If you know your own mind, you are sure about your opinions, and are not easily influenced by other people.

ext.ext_cn: 有时候我觉得自己快要疯掉了。
ext.ext_en: Sometimes I feel I'm losing my mind.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is losing their mind, you mean that they are becoming mad.

ext.ext_cn: 一旦他下定决心做某件事，就没有什么能够阻止他。
ext.ext_en: Once he made up his mind to do something, there was no stopping him...

ext.ext_cn: 他就是拿不定主意。
ext.ext_en: He simply can't make his mind up...

defs.def_en: If you make up your mind or make your mind up, you decide which of a number of possible things  you will have or do.

defs.def_cn: 思想支配物质(指某人似乎能够用其思想控制事情、物体或自身身体状况)

ext.ext_cn: 身体健康只不过是一个心态至上的问题。
ext.ext_en: Good health is simply a case of mind over matter.

defs.def_en: You can use the expression mind over matter to describe situations in which a person seems to be able to control events, physical objects, or the condition of their own body using their mind.

ext.ext_cn: 和其他志同道合的残疾人帆船运动员接触会有帮助。
ext.ext_en: Contact with other disabled yachtsmen of like mind would be helpful...

ext.ext_cn: 对于这些新规定，各食品公司意见不一。
ext.ext_en: The food companies are not of one mind about these new regulations.

defs.def_en: If a number of people are of one mind ,of like mind, or of the same mind, they all agree about something.

defs.def_cn: 不再忧虑;心中的石头落地
defs.def_en: If you say that something that happens is a load off your mind or a weight off your mind, you mean that it causes you to stop worrying, for example because it solves a problem that you had.

ext.ext_cn: 整整一个星期，我都在为这次比赛紧绷着一根弦。
ext.ext_en: This game has been on my mind all week...

ext.ext_cn: 我完全忘了，我脑子里的事太多了。
ext.ext_en: I just forgot. I've had a lot on my mind.

defs.def_en: If something is on your mind, you are worried or concerned about it and think about it a lot.

ext.ext_cn: 上学的时候，我老是惹麻烦——我的心思从来不在学业上。
ext.ext_en: At school I was always in trouble—my mind was never on my work.

defs.def_en: If your mind is on something or you have your mind on something, you are thinking about that thing.

defs.def_cn: 开明的思想;无先入之见的心态

ext.ext_cn: 尽管我努力不妄下定论，但此事很难有其他的见解。
ext.ext_en: It's hard to see it any other way, though I'm trying to keep an open mind.

defs.def_en: If you have an open mind, you avoid forming an opinion or making a decision until you know all the facts.

defs.def_cn: 使思想开放；使更愿意接受(或尝试)(新事物)

ext.ext_cn: 她还激发了他的好奇心，使他愿意了解其他文化。
ext.ext_en: She also stimulated his curiosity and opened his mind to other cultures.

defs.def_en: If something opens your mind to new ideas or experiences, it makes you more willing to accept them or try them.

ext.ext_cn: 你在干什么？你疯了吗？
ext.ext_en: What are you doing? Are you out of your mind?

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is out of their mind, you mean that they are mad or very foolish.
If you say that someone is out of their mind with a feeling such as worry or fear, you are emphasizing that they are extremely worried or afraid.

defs.def_cn: 烦得要命/吓得丢了魂/在毒品作用下变得飘飘然
defs.def_en: If you say that someone is, for example, bored out of their mind ,scared out of their mind, or stoned out of their mind, you are emphasizing that they are extremely bored, scared, or affected by drugs.

ext.ext_cn: 如果认真去做，任何事都可以做好。
ext.ext_en: You could do fine in the world if you put your mind to it.

defs.def_en: If you put your mind to something, you start making  an effort to do it.

defs.def_cn: 使想起，使联想起(类似或相关的事)

ext.ext_cn: 这使我想起多年前帕特里克曾说过的话。
ext.ext_en: This put me in mind of something Patrick said many years ago.

defs.def_en: If something puts you in mind of something else, it reminds you of it because it is similar to it or is associated with it.

defs.def_cn: 读懂…的思想;看出…的心思

ext.ext_cn: 别指望别人会看出你的心思。
ext.ext_en: Don't expect others to read your mind.

defs.def_en: If you can read someone's mind, you know what they are thinking without them saying anything.

ext.ext_cn: 最好验一下血，好让你自己放心。
ext.ext_en: It may be advisable to have a blood test to put your mind at rest...

ext.ext_cn: 她可以告诉你事实的真相以让你放心。
ext.ext_en: She could set your mind at rest by giving you the facts.

defs.def_en: To put someone's mind at rest or set their mind at rest means to stop them worrying about something.

defs.def_cn: 心智正常(而不会做某事)

ext.ext_cn: 没有哪个心智正常的人会连问都不问就花这么一大笔钱买东西。
ext.ext_en: No one in her right mind would make such a major purchase without asking questions.

defs.def_en: If you say that nobody in their right mind would do a particular thing, you are emphasizing that it is an irrational thing to do and you would be surprised if anyone did it.

ext.ext_cn: 我妻子一旦下定决心做某事，就总能设法完成。
ext.ext_en: When my wife sets her mind on something, she invariably finds a way to achieve it.

defs.def_en: If you set your mind on something or have your mind set on it, you are determined to do it or obtain it.

ext.ext_cn: 我刚想提这件事，却又忘了。
ext.ext_en: I was going to mention it, but it slipped my mind.

defs.def_en: If something slips your mind, you forget it.

ext.ext_cn: 玛蒂娜·纳芙拉蒂洛娃从来不害怕说实话。
ext.ext_en: Martina Navratilova has never been afraid to speak her mind.

defs.def_en: If you speak your mind, you say firmly and honestly what you think about a situation, even if this may offend or upset people.

defs.def_cn: 被牢记在心；印在脑海中

ext.ext_cn: 我一直喜爱诗歌，有一首诗总是牢记在我心间。
ext.ext_en: I've always been fond of poetry and one piece has always stuck in my mind.

defs.def_en: If something sticks in your mind, it remains firmly in your memory.

defs.def_cn: 使暂时忘记(某一问题或不愉快的情况)

ext.ext_cn: “打一场网球怎么样？”艾伦建议说，“那样会让你暂时忘掉烦心事。”
ext.ext_en: 'How about a game of tennis?' suggested Alan. 'That'll take your mind off things.'

defs.def_en: If something takes your mind off a problem or unpleasant situation, it helps you to forget about it for a while.

ext.ext_cn: 这出戏里有些场面在我看来过于暴力。
ext.ext_en: There are scenes in this play which to my mind are incredibly violent.

defs.def_en: You say or write to my mind to indicate that the statement you are making is your own opinion.

defs.def_cn: （尤指在两种行动选择间）犹豫不决，拿不定主意（亦可使用of two minds，尤见于美国英语）

ext.ext_cn: 跟许多家长一样，我对是否该穿校服也拿不定主意。
ext.ext_en: Like many parents, I am in two minds about school uniforms...

ext.ext_cn: 对于是否要去一趟奥斯陆，罗奇犹豫不决。
ext.ext_en: Roche was in two minds whether to make the trip to Oslo.

defs.def_en: If you are in two minds, you are uncertain about what to do, especially when you have to choose between two courses of action. The expression of two minds is also used, especially in American English.

ext.ext_cn: 我并不介意白天的噪音。
ext.ext_en: I don't mind the noise during the day...

ext.ext_cn: 你介意独处吗？
ext.ext_en: Do you mind being alone?...

defs.def_en: If you do not mind something, you are not annoyed or bothered by it.

defs.def_cn: (征求对方同意或者请求对方做某事时的礼貌说法)你是否介意

ext.ext_cn: 您不介意我再问您一个问题吧？
ext.ext_en: Do you mind if I ask you one more thing?...

ext.ext_cn: 您不介意他们四处看看吧？
ext.ext_en: You don't mind if they take a look round, do you?...

defs.def_en: You use mind in the expressions 'do you mind?' and 'would you mind?' as a polite way of asking permission or asking someone to do something.

ext.ext_cn: 玩什么我都不反对，真的。
ext.ext_en: I don't mind what we play, really...

ext.ext_cn: 我想为顶级俱乐部踢球，至于在哪里踢无所谓。
ext.ext_en: I want to play for a top club and I don't mind where it is...

defs.def_en: If someone does not mind what happens or what something is like, they do not have a strong preference for any particular thing.

ext.ext_cn: 小心那辆自行车！
ext.ext_en: Mind that bike!

defs.def_en: If you tell someone to mind something, you are warning them to be careful not to hurt themselves or other people, or damage something.

ext.ext_cn: 注意别把那些香肠给烤焦了。
ext.ext_en: Mind you don't burn those sausages.

defs.def_en: You use mind when you are reminding someone to do something or telling them to be careful not to do something.

ext.ext_cn: 我不在的时候吉姆·库尔特斯会照看店铺的。
ext.ext_en: Jim Coulters will mind the store while I'm away.

defs.def_en: If you mind a child or something such as a shop or luggage, you look after it, usually while the person who owns it or is usually responsible for it is somewhere else.

ext.ext_cn: “你想要这里面的哪一个？”——“都可以。”
ext.ext_en: 'Which one of these do you want?' — 'I don't mind.'

defs.def_en: If you are offered something or offered a choice and you say 'I don't mind', you are saying politely that you will be happy with any of the things offered.

defs.def_cn: (接受某人给予的东西，尤指接受饮料或食物时)好的，可以
defs.def_en: You can say 'I don't mind if I do' as a way of accepting something that someone has offered you, especially food or drink.

defs.def_cn: (用于认为自己在场可能使某人尴尬时)不用考虑我，不用在意我
defs.def_en: You say 'Don't mind me' to apologize for your presence when you think that it might embarrass someone, and to tell them to carry on with what they were doing or about to do.

defs.def_cn: (认为别人的行为可能冒犯谈话的对象时，为别人的行为表示道歉)别在意(他或他们)

ext.ext_cn: 不要在意这个老太太，她有点儿老糊涂了。
ext.ext_en: Don't mind the old lady. She's getting senile.

defs.def_en: You use don't mind in expressions such as don't mind him or don't mind them to apologize for someone else's behaviour when you think it might have offended the person you are speaking to.
Some people say 'Mind how you go' when they are saying goodbye to someone who is leaving.

defs.def_cn: (尤用于生气地拒绝提议或表示不愿做某事)如果你不介意

ext.ext_cn: “坐下吧。”——“如果你不介意的话，我想站一会儿。”
ext.ext_en: 'Sit down.' — 'I prefer standing for a while, if you don't mind.'...

ext.ext_cn: 如果可以的话，我们就不要再谈论这件事情了。
ext.ext_en: If you don't mind, we won't talk about it any more.

defs.def_en: People use the expression if you don't mind when they are rejecting an offer or saying that they do not want to do something, especially when they are annoyed.

defs.def_cn: (用于强调补充信息，尤指新信息对之前所说的话进行解释或形成对比)请注意

ext.ext_cn: 他们付全价，请注意，他们是付得起的。
ext.ext_en: They pay full rates. Mind you, they can afford it...

ext.ext_cn: 我损失惨重，请注意，我用了两年时间才恢复过来。
ext.ext_en: I got substantial damages. It took two years, mind you...

defs.def_en: You use mind you to emphasize a piece of information that you are adding, especially when the new information explains what you have said or contrasts with it. Some people use mind in a similar way.

defs.def_cn: (尤指对小孩说的话)注意语言/注意说话/注意态度
defs.def_en: If you tell someone, especially a child, to mind their language ,mind their tongue, or mind their manners, you are telling them to speak or behave properly and politely.
You say never mind when you are emphasizing that something is not serious or important, especially when someone is upset about it or is  saying sorry to you.

defs.def_cn: 不用了;不必担心;不用着急

ext.ext_cn: “我保证马上就上来。”——“没关系，”我叹了口气说，“我自己来。”
ext.ext_en: 'I'll go up in one second, I promise.' — 'Never mind,' I said with a sigh. 'I'll do it.'...

ext.ext_cn: “他是叫戴维吗？”——“不，我想不是的，不过不要紧，继续吧。”
ext.ext_en: 'Was his name David?'  — 'No I don't think it was, but never mind, go on.'...

defs.def_en: You use never mind to tell someone that they need not do something or worry about something, because it is not important or because you will do it yourself.

defs.def_cn: (常用于否定陈述句后)更不用说

ext.ext_cn: 我自己都不会相信，更别提说服别人了。
ext.ext_en: I'm not going to believe it myself, never mind convince anyone else...

ext.ext_cn: 许多坑洼处甚至给机动车都带来了危险，更别提骑自行车的人了。
ext.ext_en: Many of the potholes are a danger even to motor vehicles, never mind cyclists.

defs.def_en: You use never mind after a statement, often a negative one, to indicate that the statement is even more true of the person, thing, or situation that you are going to mention next.

ext.ext_cn: “它在哪里？”——“与你无关。”
ext.ext_en: 'Where is it?'  — 'Never you mind.'

defs.def_en: You use never you mind to tell someone not to ask about something because it is not their concern or they should not know about it.

defs.def_cn: (用于强调将要说的话)我不介意告诉你

ext.ext_cn: 说真的，我当时吓坏了。
ext.ext_en: I don't mind telling you I was absolutely terrified.

defs.def_en: You can say 'I don't mind telling you' to emphasize the statement you are making.

ext.ext_cn: 我很愿意喝杯咖啡。
ext.ext_en: I wouldn't mind a coffee...

ext.ext_cn: 安妮很愿意去意大利或法国定居。
ext.ext_en: Anne wouldn't mind going to Italy or France to live.

defs.def_en: If you say that you wouldn't mind something, you mean that you would quite like it.
The fuse box is the box that contains the fuses for all the electric circuits in a building. It is usually fixed to a wall.

ext.ext_cn: 该制度动机虽好，却易遭滥用。
ext.ext_en: The system, though well-meaning, is open to abuse...

ext.ext_cn: 他们使自己陷于被人指责搞双重标准和虚伪不实的境地。
ext.ext_en: They left themselves wide open to accusations of double standards and hypocrisy.

defs.def_en: If you say that a system, person, or idea is open to something such as abuse or criticism, you mean they might receive abuse or criticism because of their qualities, effects, or actions.

defs.def_cn: 悬而未决的；尚未决定的

ext.ext_cn: 所摆出事实的真实性仍然值得怀疑。
ext.ext_en: The truth of the facts produced may be open to doubt...

ext.ext_cn: 这一承诺能维持多久还不确定。
ext.ext_en: It is an open question how long that commitment can last.

defs.def_en: If you say that a fact or question is open to debate, interpretation, or discussion, you mean that people are uncertain whether it is true, what it means, or what the answer is.

defs.def_cn: 开放（被封的道路、边界等）；开通

ext.ext_cn: 叛乱分子已经开放了从蒙罗维亚到象牙海岸的道路。
ext.ext_en: The rebels have opened the road from Monrovia to the Ivory Coast...

ext.ext_cn: 把法庭围得水泄不通的一队警察让开一条路让他们通过。
ext.ext_en: The solid rank of police officers lining the courtroom opened to let them pass.

defs.def_en: If people open something such as a blocked road or a border, or if it opens, people can then pass along it or through it.

ext.ext_cn: 这条走廊通向一间烟雾弥漫的低矮房间。
ext.ext_en: The corridor opened into a low smoky room.

ext.ext_cn: 通向迷人广场的狭窄小街
ext.ext_en: ...narrow streets opening out into charming squares.

defs.def_en: If a place opens into another, larger place, you can move from one directly into the other.

ext.ext_cn: 警察还将继续在附近的开阔地带搜寻。
ext.ext_en: Officers will also continue their search of nearby open ground.

defs.def_en: An open area is a large area that does not have many buildings or trees in it.

defs.def_cn: 敞开的；无遮盖的；无围挡的

ext.ext_cn: 房间里有裸露的明火时，不要让孩子独处其中。
ext.ext_en: Don't leave a child alone in a room with an open fire.

ext.ext_cn: 单片三明治
ext.ext_en: ...open sandwiches.

defs.def_en: An open structure or object is not covered or enclosed.
An open wound is one from which a liquid such as blood is coming.

defs.def_cn: 把（衣服）解开；把…的拉链拉开

ext.ext_cn: 我解开外衣，让他看那条皮带。
ext.ext_en: I opened my coat and let him see the belt.

ext.ext_cn: 这件上衣可以系上纽扣，也可以里面套件T恤敞开穿。
ext.ext_en: The top can be worn buttoned up or open over a T-shirt.

defs.def_en: If you open your shirt or coat, you undo the buttons or pull down the zip.

ext.ext_cn: 银行星期五下午关门，直到星期一上午才营业。
ext.ext_en: Banks closed on Friday afternoon and did not open again until Monday morning.

ext.ext_cn: 显然一直潜伏着等待他打开店门营业的3人团伙
ext.ext_en: ...a gang of three who'd apparently been lying in wait for him to open the shop.

defs.def_en: When a shop, office, or public building opens or is opened, its doors are unlocked and the public can go in.

defs.def_cn: 为（大楼、工厂、公司等）举行揭幕典礼；开设；开办；开张

ext.ext_cn: 最初的车站于1754年落成。
ext.ext_en: The original station opened in 1754...

ext.ext_cn: 这幢综合大楼将于明天对公众开放。
ext.ext_en: The complex opens to the public tomorrow...

defs.def_en: When a public building, factory, or company opens or when someone opens it, it starts operating for the first time.

ext.ext_cn: 将于今天上午晚些时候召开的俄罗斯议会紧急会议
ext.ext_en: ...an emergency session of the Russian Parliament due to open later this morning...

ext.ext_cn: 他们现在已经准备好开始谈判。
ext.ext_en: They are now ready to open negotiations.

defs.def_en: If something such as a meeting or series of talks opens, or if someone opens it, it begins.

ext.ext_cn: 礼拜仪式从唱圣歌开始。
ext.ext_en: The service opened with a hymn...

ext.ext_cn: 她以一首优美动人的《我仍在寻找》开场。
ext.ext_en: She opened with an impressive version of 'I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For'...

defs.def_en: If an event such as a meeting or discussion opens with a particular activity or if a particular activity opens an event, that activity is the first thing that happens or is dealt with. You can also say that someone such as a speaker or singer opens by doing a particular thing.

ext.ext_cn: 苏黎世的金价下挫2美元，以385.50元开盘。
ext.ext_en: Gold declined $2 in Zurich to open at 385.50...

ext.ext_cn: 在巴黎和米兰，美元开市时几乎没有变化。
ext.ext_en: In Paris and Milan, the dollar opened almost unchanged.

defs.def_en: On the stock exchange, the price at which currencies, shares, or commodities open is their value at the start of that day's trading.

ext.ext_cn: 星期三一个摄影展在皇家艺术学院开幕。
ext.ext_en: A photographic exhibition opens at the Royal College of Art on Wednesday...

ext.ext_cn: 这场演出的门票也是几乎在开演前就销售一空了。
ext.ext_en: This show, too, was virtually sold out before it opened.

defs.def_en: When a film, play, or other public event opens, it begins to be shown, be performed, or take place for a limited period of time.

ext.ext_cn: 他想在自己银行离工作单位最近的网点开一个账户。
ext.ext_en: He tried to open an account at the branch of his bank nearest to his workplace.

defs.def_en: If you open an account with a bank or a commercial organization, you begin to use their services.

defs.def_cn: （机会、选择等）可利用的，可得到的

ext.ext_cn: 年轻人有各种职业选择机会。
ext.ext_en: There are a wide range of career opportunities open to young people.

defs.def_en: If an opportunity or choice is open to you, you are able to do a particular thing if you choose to.

defs.def_cn: （使）（机会、可能性等）出现;（使）产生

ext.ext_cn: 美国海军作战部长希望能为女兵提供机会。
ext.ext_en: The chief of naval operations wants to open opportunities for women in the Navy...

ext.ext_cn: 很多好机会陆续向他招手。
ext.ext_en: A series of fortunate opportunities opened to him.

defs.def_en: To open opportunities or possibilities means the same as to open them up.

defs.def_cn: 人人可以参加（或接受）的；开放的

ext.ext_cn: 最近的一次学会成员公开会上，大家普遍流露出不满情绪。
ext.ext_en: A recent open meeting of College members revealed widespread dissatisfaction...

ext.ext_cn: 项目组合的方法会使成为管理人员的机会公开灵活。
ext.ext_en: A portfolio approach would keep entry into the managerial profession open and flexible.

defs.def_en: You can use open to describe something that anyone is allowed to take part in or accept.

defs.def_cn: （提议等）有效的；（职位等）空缺的，可申请的

ext.ext_cn: 该提议仍然有效，直到另行通知。
ext.ext_en: The offer will remain open until further notice.

defs.def_en: See also:opening;If something such as an offer or job is open, it is available for someone to accept or apply for.

ext.ext_cn: 很多人因为没有栖身之所，只好露宿在外。
ext.ext_en: Many are sleeping in the open because they have no shelter.

defs.def_en: If you do something in the open, you do it out of doors rather than in a house or other building.

ext.ext_cn: 这家医疗机构建议我们保密，而我们却想公开此事。
ext.ext_en: The medical service had advised us to keep it a secret, but we wanted it in the open.

defs.def_en: If an attitude or situation is in the open or out in the open, people know about it and it is no longer kept secret.

defs.def_cn: 大开的；敞开的；（眼睛）睁大的

ext.ext_cn: 这个孩子将里面的门大敞着。
ext.ext_en: The child had left the inner door wide open.

defs.def_en: If something is wide open, it is open to its full extent.

defs.def_cn: （比赛、选举等）结果不确定的，胜负难定的

ext.ext_cn: 由于世界冠军缺阵，这场比赛变得胜负难定。
ext.ext_en: The competition has been thrown wide open by the absence of the world champion.

defs.def_en: If you say that a competition, race, or election is wide open, you mean that anyone could win it, because there is no competitor who seems to be much better than the others.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 好管闲事的；爱指手画脚的

ext.ext_cn: 他们不会欢迎任何来自警方的横加干涉。
ext.ext_en: They wouldn't welcome any officious interference from the police...

ext.ext_cn: 人们穿上制服后会信心倍增，也更爱管闲事了。
ext.ext_en: When people put on uniforms, their attitude becomes more confident and their manner more officious.

defs.def_en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 黄油很容易变质，而且会发臭。
ext.ext_en: Butter is perishable and can go rancid.

ext.ext_cn: 腐败牛奶发出的臭味
ext.ext_en: ...the odour of rancid milk.

defs.def_en: If butter, bacon, or other oily foods are rancid, they have gone bad and taste old and unpleasant.

ext.ext_cn: 她的背景对她不利。
ext.ext_en: Her background militates against her...

ext.ext_cn: 天有不测风云，所以我们永远都无法保证会航行到哪个地方。
ext.ext_en: We can never promise to sail anywhere in particular, because the weather might militate against it.

defs.def_en: To militate against something means to make it less possible or likely. To militate against someone means to prevent them from achieving something.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 我觉得我一直非常自私。总是只关心自己。
ext.ext_en: I think I've been very selfish. I've been mainly concerned with myself.

ext.ext_cn: 少数人的私利
ext.ext_en: ...the selfish interests of a few people.

defs.def_en: If you say that someone is selfish, you mean that he or she cares only about himself or herself, and not about other people.

ext.ext_cn: 如今的建筑结构复杂，需要建筑师和施工人员密切协作。
ext.ext_en: Today's complex buildings require close teamwork between the architect and the builders.

defs.def_en: Teamwork is the ability a group of people have to work well together.

ext.ext_cn: 她所做的就只是在工厂里荡来荡去，朝男人抛媚眼。
ext.ext_en: All she did was hang around ogling the men in the factory...

ext.ext_cn: 葆拉还不习惯在后台换衣服时所有人都色迷迷地盯着她看。
ext.ext_en: Paula is not used to everyone ogling at her while she undresses backstage.

defs.def_en: If you say that one person is ogling another, you disapprove of them continually staring at that person in a way that indicates a strong sexual interest.

ext.ext_cn: data 在拉丁文中是 datum 的复数形式。
ext.ext_en: 'Data' is the Latin plural form of 'datum'.

ext.ext_cn: 他对复数代词 we 的使用
ext.ext_en: ...his use of the plural pronoun 'we'.

defs.def_en: The plural form of a word is the form that is used when referring to more than one person or thing.

ext.ext_cn: person 的复数形式是什么？
ext.ext_en: What is the plural of 'person'?

ext.ext_cn: 不规则复数形式
ext.ext_en: ...irregular plurals.

defs.def_en: The plural of a noun is the form of it that is used to refer to more than one person or thing.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 英国是个世俗主导的多元社会。
ext.ext_en: Britain is a plural society in which the secular predominates...

ext.ext_cn: 他的政府已承诺要推动本国朝着多元民主的方向发展。
ext.ext_en: His government has pledged to move the country towards a plural democracy.

defs.def_en: A plural society or system involves different kinds of people.

ext.ext_cn: 用塑料薄膜防潮的木板箱
ext.ext_en: ...a wooden crate, sheltered from wetness by sheets of plastic...

ext.ext_cn: 汽车制造商使用的许多塑料制品是无法回收利用的。
ext.ext_en: A lot of the plastics that carmakers are using cannot be recycled.

defs.def_en: Plastic is a material which is produced from oil by a chemical process and which is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 航班上味同嚼蜡的食品
ext.ext_en: ...plastic airline food...

ext.ext_cn: 女孩子如果把眼影涂得过重，看起来就不自然了。
ext.ext_en: When girls put on too much eye-shadow, they look plastic.

defs.def_en: If you describe something as plastic, you mean that you think it looks or tastes unnatural or not real.

ext.ext_cn: 用信用卡支付订单是很简单的事。
ext.ext_en: Using plastic to pay for an order is simplicity itself.

ext.ext_cn: 用他们的信用卡购物
ext.ext_en: ...shopping with their plastic money.

defs.def_en: If you use plastic or plastic money to pay for something, you pay for it with a credit card instead of using cash.

ext.ext_cn: 这种泥浆呈灰色，它光滑、柔软，像黄油一样易塑。
ext.ext_en: The mud is smooth, gray, soft, and plastic as butter.

defs.def_en: Something that is plastic is soft and can easily be made into different shapes.

ext.ext_cn: 我们生活在意味着世界末日将要到来的灾难的阴影当中。
ext.ext_en: We live in the shadow of the apocalypse, of a catastrophe that will mean the end of the world itself.

defs.def_en: The apocalypse is the total destruction and end of the world.

defs.def_cn: （加在名词前）表示“以前的”，“前任的”

ext.ext_cn: 我的前妻
ext.ext_en: ...my ex-wife.

ext.ext_cn: 前任总统里根
ext.ext_en: ...ex-President Reagan.

defs.def_en: ex- is added to nouns to show that someone or something is no longer the thing referred to by that noun. For example, a woman's ex-husband is no longer her husband.

defs.def_cn: (尤指某人有控制力、影响力或权利的)领域，范围，范畴

ext.ext_cn: 艺术领域伟大的实验者们
ext.ext_en: ...the great experimenters in the domain of art...

ext.ext_cn: 这一消息应该为公众所知。
ext.ext_en: This information should be in the public domain.

defs.def_en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

ext.ext_cn: 势力强大的国王的领土
ext.ext_en: ...the mighty king's domain.

defs.def_en: Someone's domain is the area they own or have control over.
On the Internet, a domain is a set of addresses that shows, for example, the category or geographical area that an Internet address belongs to.
A vampire bat is a bat from South America which feeds by sucking the blood of other animals.

defs.def_cn: 出乎意料的变化;难以预测的转变

ext.ext_cn: 我带了各种衣服去度假，以防天气突变。
ext.ext_en: I take an assortment of clothes on holiday, as a provision against the vagaries of the weather.

ext.ext_cn: 复杂难解、变幻莫测的政坛风云
ext.ext_en: ...the perplexing vagaries of politics.

defs.def_en: Vagaries are unexpected and unpredictable changes in a situation or in someone's behaviour which you have no control over.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 严肃的;重要的;有意义的

ext.ext_cn: 她认为这些谈话将是一次具有建设性的、有意义的对话的开端。
ext.ext_en: She believes these talks will be the start of a constructive and meaningful dialogue...

ext.ext_cn: 他让人们讲讲他们生命中的重要事件或者阶段。
ext.ext_en: He asked people to tell him about a meaningful event or period in their lives.

defs.def_en: If you describe something as meaningful, you mean that it is serious, important, or useful in some way.

defs.def_cn: （指眼神、姿势）意味深长的，意在言外的

ext.ext_cn: 这句话一出口，丹和哈里马上交换了一个意味深长的眼神。
ext.ext_en: Upon the utterance of this word, Dan and Harry exchanged a quick, meaningful look.

defs.def_en: A meaningful look or gesture is one that is intended to express something, usually to a particular person, without anything being said.

defs.def_cn: 使(某人)想要却得不到(某物);逗引;挑逗;撩拨

ext.ext_cn: 那个男孩会到房间里拿狗食逗弄狗。
ext.ext_en: The boy would come into the room and tantalize the dog with his feed.

ext.ext_cn: 他们可望而不可即的民主梦想
ext.ext_en: ...the dreams of democracy that have so tantalized them.

defs.def_en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have what they appeared to offer.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: （机器、系统等）易操作的，便于使用的

ext.ext_cn: 这个系统完全由电脑操控，非常好用。
ext.ext_en: This is an entirely computer operated system which is very user friendly.

ext.ext_cn: 使用方便的图书馆
ext.ext_en: ...user-friendly libraries.

defs.def_en: If you describe something such as a machine or system as user-friendly, you mean that it is well designed and easy to use.

defs.def_cn: (爵士乐和摇滚乐中的)重复乐段
defs.def_en: In jazz and rock music, a riff is a short repeated tune.

defs.def_cn: (一小段表达一定主题或思想的)讲话，文章

ext.ext_cn: 罗就偏见的本质讲了一番很精辟的话。
ext.ext_en: Rowe does a very clever riff on the nature of prejudice.

defs.def_en: A riff is a short piece of speech or writing that develops a particular theme or idea.

ext.ext_cn: 穿短裤的小学生
ext.ext_en: ...young school kids in short pants.

defs.def_en: School kids are schoolchildren .
In a game such as football or hockey, a winger is an attacking player who plays mainly on the far left or the far right side of the pitch.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
defs.def_cn: 值得想望（或拥有）的;合意的;可取的;受欢迎的

ext.ext_cn: 拖长了的谈判并不是大家所想要的。
ext.ext_en: Prolonged negotiation was not desirable...

ext.ext_cn: 人群为了被视为最值得拥有的物品涌入屋里。
ext.ext_en: The crowd moved indoors for what were deemed the most desirable items.

defs.def_en: Something that is desirable is worth having or doing because it is useful, necessary, or popular.

defs.pos_cn: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词

ext.ext_cn: 他的同班同学认为最性感的年轻女子
ext.ext_en: ...the young women whom his classmates thought most desirable.

defs.def_en: Someone who is desirable is considered to be sexually attractive.

ext.ext_cn: 整个事件很不光彩，亟须彻查。
ext.ext_en: This is a disgraceful state of affairs and cries out for a thorough investigation.

defs.def_en: If you say that something cries out for a particular thing or action, you mean that it needs that thing or action very much.

defs.def_cn: 露天游乐会(通常在户外举行，包括竞赛、娱乐及出售旧货和家制商品)
defs.def_en: A fete is an event that is usually held outdoors and includes competitions, entertainments, and the selling of used and home-made goods.

ext.ext_cn: 英国服装设计师阿瑙斯卡·亨普尔本周在纽约出席豪华晚宴时大受追捧。
ext.ext_en: Anouska Hempel, the British dress designer, was feted in New York this week at a spectacular dinner...

ext.ext_cn: 从整日焦虑的妻子到受人追捧的作家，这变化迅速而剧烈。
ext.ext_en: The metamorphosis from anxious wife to feted author was rapid and dramatic.

defs.def_en: If someone is feted, they are celebrated, welcomed, or admired by the public.

ext.ext_cn: 夫人，请重复一遍好吗？
ext.ext_en: Would you repeat that please, ma'am?

defs.def_en: People sometimes say ma'am as a very formal and polite way of addressing a woman whose name they do not know or a woman of superior rank.

ext.ext_cn: 由于惊恐，安斯利的脉搏加快了。
ext.ext_en: Ainslie's pulse quickened in alarm...

ext.ext_cn: 他稍稍加快了步伐。
ext.ext_en: He quickened his pace a little.

defs.def_en: If something quickens or if you quicken it, it becomes faster or moves at a greater speed.

ext.ext_cn: 他要么是闷死的，要么是冻死的。
ext.ext_en: He either suffocated, or froze to death...

ext.ext_cn: 他们睡觉时窒息而死。
ext.ext_en: They were suffocated as they slept.

defs.def_en: If someone suffocates or is suffocated, they die because there is no air for them to breathe.

ext.ext_cn: 这样好些了，我刚才在那个小房间里快闷死了。
ext.ext_en: That's better. I was suffocating in that cell of a room...

ext.ext_cn: 房间里密不透风，憋得她喘不上气来。
ext.ext_en: The airlessness of the room suffocated her.

defs.def_en: If you say that you are suffocating or that something is suffocating you, you mean that you feel very uncomfortable because there is not enough fresh air and it is difficult to breathe.

ext.ext_cn: 和父母呆了几个星期后，她感到自己毫无自由。
ext.ext_en: After a few weeks with her parents, she felt she was suffocating...

ext.ext_cn: 总督的计划可能会造成上百万人失业，并束缚经济发展。
ext.ext_en: The governor's proposals would actually cost millions of jobs and suffocate the economy.

defs.def_en: You say that a person or thing is suffocating, or that something is suffocating them, when the situation that they are in does not allow them to act freely or to develop.

ext.ext_cn: 我们在11层办公。
ext.ext_en: We were working on the eleventh floor.

defs.def_en: The eleventh item in a series is the one that you count as number eleven.

defs.def_cn: (尤当 has 为助动词时， who is 或 who has 的常用口语形式）
defs.def_en: Who's is the usual spoken form of 'who is' or 'who has', especially when 'has' is an auxiliary verb.
